title:
G:C:G:C-Flanked i-Motifs
Are Thermodynamically
Favored and Their Sequences Highly Enriched in the Human Genome
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>i-Motifs are biologically relevant noncanonical DNA structures whose stability is strongly influenced by capping interactions. Among these, minor groove tetrads (MGTs) are among the most powerful stabilizing elements identified to date, yet the molecular factors governing their effects and their potential biological significance remain poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic experimental and computational analysis of 16 MGT-stabilized i-motifs (MGTiMs), encompassing all combinations of terminal tetrad composition and orientation within a common sequence scaffold. NMR spectroscopy confirms that all sequences adopt closely related architectures, enabling direct comparison of the effects of tetrad identity and orientation on stability. Thermal denaturation experiments reveal that the stability hierarchy, previously observed in selected structures (G:C:G:C ≳ G:C:G:T ≫ G:T:G:T), is broadly maintained across the series, although substantial positional effects are observed. Molecular dynamics simulations and energy decomposition analyses suggest that differences in electrostatic interactions and local conformational flexibility contribute to these trends. Notably, genome-wide analysis of the human genome reveals a strong enrichment of sequences capable of forming the most stabilizing tetrads, with motifs containing two G:C:G:C tetrads reaching a 45-fold enrichment relative to random expectation. Interestingly, this most abundant genomic motif is also the only one that undergoes pronounced pH-driven conformational transitions, highlighting the unique structural plasticity of these architectures. Together, these findings reveal how tetrad composition and positional context govern MGTiM stability and identify NN-type motifs as a particularly enriched class of structurally distinctive genomic sequences.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Radical Ring-Opening Polymerization of endo -Cyclic Monomers for Regioregularity Control in Vinyl Polymers
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Radical polymerization of vinyl monomers is inherently governed by propagation pathways that favor head-to-tail connectivity, limiting access to alternative backbone regioregularities. To address this challenge, we report the radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) of endo-cyclic monomers, a class of monomers that has been largely unexplored in radical processes. Whereas many established rROP systems have been designed to introduce functional or cleavable units into polymer backbones, the present endo-cyclic monomers undergo selective rROP to generate carbon–carbon-backboned vinyl polymers enriched with nonhead-to-tail linkages. Copolymerization with conventional vinyl monomers was also achieved, providing access to copolymers with tunable backbone microstructures. In particular, using vinyl ketones and their corresponding endo-cyclic cyclodimers as structurally matched pairs, we accessed poly(vinyl ketone)s with systematically varied head-to-tail linkage contents. This control over backbone regioregularity translated into tunable macroscopic properties, including glass transition temperature and photodegradation kinetics, establishing regioregularity as a structural handle for controlling material properties. The strategy was also compatible with controlled radical polymerization, enabling the synthesis of well-defined block copolymers. Micelles assembled from these block copolymers further exhibited regioregularity-dependent sizes and photoresponsive behavior. These findings establish endo-cyclic rROP as a previously unrecognized strategy for controlling backbone regioregularity and properties in vinyl polymers.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
NMR Reveals Coupled
Ligand and Protein Conformational
Equilibria That Modulate the Affinity of MDM2-Inhibitory Peptoids
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Peptoids, atypical peptides with N-substitutions, are a promising drug modality for targeting protein–protein interactions. The binding affinity of an MDM2-inhibitory peptoid decreases by more than 100-fold upon removal of the backbone-restricting methyl groups attached to the α-carbons, although this modification alters the population of the all-trans amide-bond isomer by only 1.6-fold. This discrepancy raises the possibility that backbone flexibility affects not only ligand preorganization but also the conformational ensemble of the target protein. Here, we used NMR to examine the binding mode of the MDM2-peptoid complexes. ZZ-exchange experiments demonstrated that peptoid isomers containing cis amide bonds bind less favorably to MDM2 than the all-trans amide bond isomer. In addition, observation of the I19 δ1-methyl resonance of MDM2 in complex with the peptoids revealed that MDM2 exists in equilibrium between an open state, corresponding to the crystal structure of the MDM2-peptoid complex, and a semiclosed state, which retains partial interactions between the N-terminal region of MDM2 and the ligand-binding cleft. Increased population of the semiclosed state correlated with reduced binding affinities of the peptoids. We propose that cis-trans isomerization of the peptoid amide bonds and the conformational equilibrium of MDM2 within the peptoid complex synergistically contribute to the more than 100-fold decrease in binding affinity. These results identify coupled ligand and protein conformational equilibria as determinants of binding affinity and suggest conformational-plasticity control as a potential design principle for oligomeric ligands targeting protein–protein interactions.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
Experimental and Computational
Identification of Wide-Gap
Quaternary Oxychalcogenides BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Oxychalcogenides have attracted attention as candidates for wide-gap p-type semiconductors in view of the energetically high and spatially spread characteristics of their valence electronic states. An appropriate choice of constituent cations would also enable n-type doping. However, reports on p-type doping have been mostly limited to Cu-based systems, which exhibit a strong p-type tendency due to hole generation and electron compensation by native Cu-vacancy acceptors. Oxychalcogenides with a practical level of n-type conductivity are yet to be developed. In this study, we focus on oxychalcogenides in the Ae–Zn–O–Ch (Ae = Ca, Sr, Ba; Ch = S, Se) quaternary system to explore new wide-gap semiconductors. Two as-yet-unreported compounds with wide band gaps, namely BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2, have been synthesized, along with four previously reported oxychalcogenides. First-principles calculations indicate that both BaZn2OS2 and SrZn2OSe2 feature direct-type band structures with low electron and hole effective masses, comparable to related compounds. Carrier compensation by native defects, however, is likely to make BaZn2OS2 insulating, whereas it can be well suppressed in SrZn2OSe2 by controlling the growth conditions. Systematic calculations of extrinsic dopants predict that bipolar doping of SrZn2OSe2 is feasible. Our results reveal the potential of non-Cu-based oxychalcogenides as a platform for the development of wide-gap, bipolar-dopable semiconductors, thereby stimulating exploration of related compounds.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
Direct-to-Biology Bifunctional
Screening Reveals Noncanonical
Mechanisms of Targeted Protein Degradation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for modulating protein function through small-molecule-induced proximity between a protein of interest (POI) and typically an E3 ubiquitin ligase to promote its proteasomal degradation. Despite significant progress, most degraders co-opt a narrow set of E3 ubiquitin ligases, motivating mechanistically agnostic strategies for discovering new routes to degradation. Here, we pursued a “degrader-first” approach using direct-to-biology (D2B) synthesis to construct and screen a 114-member library of BRD4-targeting bifunctional molecules to identify chemically tractable ligases that support TPD. Multiple compounds were found to induce Cullin-RING ligase (CRL)-dependent degradation, and two top hits were selected for mechanistic characterization. Unexpectedly, neither operates through canonical heterobifunctional E3 recruitment. Instead, one undergoes oxidative activation to generate a reactive electrophile that promotes degradation through DCAF11- or DCAF16-containing CRL4 complexes in a cell-context-dependent manner. The second acts through a bivalent bromodomain-binding mechanism that likely induces target conformational contraction and potentiates endogenous CRL3–SPOP-mediated ubiquitination. These findings highlight the capacity of D2B discovery approaches to expose noncanonical modalities of TPD while underscoring the importance of rigorous mechanistic deconvolution in interpreting screening-derived degraders.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
Halogenated
Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework
Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH &gt; 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
Catalytic Enantiodivergent
Neophyl Rearrangement
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The neophyl rearrangement is a long-established radical 1,2-aryl migration, yet catalytic enantioselective control of this process has remained elusive. Here we report a cooperative photoredox and chiral Brønsted acid catalytic system for the enantioselective neophyl rearrangement of tertiary alcohol-derived olefins. The reaction affords 1,5-dicarbonyl compounds bearing azaarene-substituted all-carbon quaternary stereocenters with up to 97% ee. Changing the radical precursor alters the preferred mode of catalyst recognition and reverses the absolute stereochemical outcome with the same catalyst configuration, providing access to opposite product enantiomers. The reaction also accommodates racemic olefin substrates, and experiments with the individual substrate enantiomers show that the chiral catalyst can counter their intrinsic stereochemical preferences. The results reveal how changes in catalyst–substrate recognition can alter stereochemical control during a transient radical rearrangement.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
Resolving Chlorine
Sites in Pharmaceuticals by Integrated
Site-Resolved Zeeman-Perturbed NQR, Solid-State NMR, and Electron
Diffraction Crystallography
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Many active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and high-value chemicals feature covalently bonded chlorine functionalities that influence molecular packing, stability, and bioavailability. However, site-resolved structural characterization of chlorine sites in powders remains challenging, especially in systems with multiple chemically or crystallographically nonequivalent sites, disorder, or hydration sensitivity. We report here a novel combined 35Cl nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR), 35Cl Zeeman-perturbed NQR (Zp-NQR), 35Cl solid-state NMR, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED/microcrystal electron diffraction) approach to characterizing powdered chlorine-bearing chemicals. Case studies of ketoconazole and chloramine-T demonstrate the utility of the approach in characterizing local structural heterogeneity and the hydration state. The role of crystal packing and noncovalent interactions on the spectroscopic observables is provided through an analysis of chlorzoxazone and five of its cocrystals, of which three are novel. Compared to ultrahigh-field NMR spectra alone, NQR and Zp-NQR spectra provide improved sensitivity to small changes in the electric field gradient and in the degree of disorder around chlorine. Experimental NQR/Zp-NQR data combined with gauge-including projector augmented-wave density functional theory (GIPAW-DFT) provide local structural constraints for a partially dehydrated chloramine-T phase. The refinement protocol does not require single crystals, and in the case of NQR experiments, intact tablets containing APIs are analyzed directly without further treatment or grinding. As a proof of principle, commercial tablets are shown to contain ketoconazole in the same crystalline form as that seen for the pure API. The general approach could be extended to other complex solids incorporating quadrupolar nuclei and is not limited to solid-form screening, polymorph identification, and differentiation of salts and cocrystals.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
Nanoscale Flexibility
Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative
Water Sorption
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Passive, sorption-based atmospheric water harvesting technologies (AWHTs) have attracted recent interest as an alternative to energy-intensive condensation-based technologies. Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer wide chemical tunability to design sorbents, but in practice, sorbents must retain moisture during humidity fluctuations, and small adsorption enthalpies are necessary for regeneration of the sorbent material. Here, we report that Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles with diameters less than 120 nm exhibit structural flexibility at the Cu2+ centers that enables a “breathing”-type cooperative water sorption. This cooperative structural phase change occurs only for nanoparticles that contain Cu2+, and not for the isomorphic magnesium triazolate. The phase change significantly decreases the onset pressures of adsorption and desorption compared to large particles and opens a practically useful hysteresis window in the isotherms, while maintaining small adsorption enthalpies (48 kJ/mol averaged over the isotherm, approaching the 44 kJ/mol latent heat of water at low RH). Mechanistic analysis indicates that adsorption initiates with weak electrostatic and dispersion interactions between water and triazolate rings brought into close proximity only by the distorted Cu2+ centers of the nanoparticles. Together, these results present a distinct water sorption mechanism and design strategy that leverages size- and metal-dependent lattice flexibility in a wide class of porous materials.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
Entropy Engineering
Accelerates High-Temperature Oxygen
Evolution Reaction Rate via Spin Manipulation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The high-temperature oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity is closely correlated to the spin state of transition metals in perovskite anodes. However, the roles of entropy engineering in modulating the spin state and influencing high-temperature OER kinetics remain poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that entropy engineering of La0.7Sr0.3FeO3−δ to (SmNdPrLaBaSrCa)FeO3−δ (SNPLBSCF) induces a transition of B-site Fe species from high-spin to low-spin states. This transition enhances the d–p hybridization of Fe–O bonds, lowers the energy barriers for electron transfer and oxygen ion migration, and finally accelerates the high-temperature OER kinetics. Consequently, the SNPLBSCF anode in a solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) achieves a current density of 3.64 A·cm–2 at 800 °C and 1.6 V, outperforming most reported anodes. This work not only provides fundamental insights into the spin state-activity relationships of perovskite oxides but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of highly efficient SOEC anodes through entropy engineering.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Chemical Programming of Stacking Order and Superconductivity Dimensionality in NbSe 2–x Te x Polytypic Heterostructures
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Layered transition-metal dichalcogenides exhibit electronic states highly sensitive to lattice symmetry, yet elucidating the structure–superconductivity relationship has been challenging due to the lack of a continuous structural evolution within a single material system. Here, we establish NbSe2–xTex as a model system, where Te substitution drives a sequential polytypic transition across the full composition range─from the low-Te 2H phase, through mixed 1H/1T heterostructured 4H and 6R polytypes at intermediate substitution, to ideal 1T and distorted 1T′ structures at high Te content. Combining comprehensive characterizations, we map both the structural evolution and the accompanying changes in spectral weight and orbital character near the Fermi level. Electrical transport measurements reveal a striking phase-dependent superconducting dimensionality: the 4H phase (NbSe1.4Te0.6) exhibits enhanced anisotropy and an anomalous boost in the in-plane upper critical field, while the 6R phase (NbSe1.2Te0.8) shows suppressed Tc (∼2.8 K) and three-dimensional-like behavior. The combined electronic-structure and superconducting results connect the stacking sequence to effective interlayer coherence and the local spin–orbit environment. SOC band calculations resolve the distinct symmetry constraints on the 4H and 6R electronic states. These mechanisms fundamentally differ from conventional approaches by leveraging intrinsic, composition-driven polytypism to modify interlayer coupling and band structure. Thus, by establishing a definitive phase diagram that directly correlates polytypism with superconducting dimensionality, our work provides a clear roadmap for the rational design of low-dimensional superconducting devices through stacking-sequence engineering.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
A Unique Conformationally
Assisted [2+2] Configuration
in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Two π-conjugated macrocycles, namely the well-known [12]cycloparaphenylene and a newly designed macrocycle combining benzenes and rigid stilbene units, are presented for the first time as light-amplifying gain media in distributed feedback (DFB) laser devices. Both systems show good photonic functionality arising from a four-state photonic cycle comprising a [2+2] state configuration (two delocalized and two conformationally distorted localized states). The mechanism involves the generation of two optically coupled states through excited-state structural distortion induced during internal conversion, which reduces light reabsorption losses and promotes rapid population inversion. Comprehensive steady-state absorption and fluorescence and transient absorption spectroscopy studies are conducted in order to reveal the nature of the low energy lying excited states. Furthermore, amplified spontaneous emission studies of the compounds in polystyrene thin films, followed by the preparation and characterization of optically pumped DFB lasers, were performed. The results reveal new properties of these multifunctional cyclic π-conjugated molecules and unique structure-property relationships.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Enantioconvergent N -Alkylation of Indoles with Alcohols Promoted by an Axially Chiral Iridacycle
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Achieving chemo- and enantioselective N-substitution of indoles presents significant challenges for catalytic method development. Herein, we report an enantioconvergent N-substitution of indoles with racemic secondary alcohols enabled by a newly developed axially chiral biaryl-supported iridacycle and chiral phosphoric acid. This borrowing-hydrogen process proceeds through an intriguing sequence involving transfer hydrogenation of indole, enantioselective reductive amination of an indoline intermediate, and subsequent rearomatization. Controlled reaction temperatures also enable selective access to the N-substituted indolines prior to rearomatization. The catalytic process accommodates diverse indoles and unactivated secondary alcohols without additional stoichiometric reagents, providing a direct and atom-economical approach to enantioenriched N-substituted indoles, including analogs of established drug candidates.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title:
An Allosteric
CLR N-Terminal Swing-Out Mechanism
for RAMP-Mediated Adrenomedullin Receptor Selectivity
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Three receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMP1–3) form heterodimers with the calcitonin (CTR) and calcitonin-like (CLR) G protein-coupled receptors and determine their selectivity for six CGRP family peptide agonists. These ligand–receptor systems are drug targets for migraine headache, diabetes and obesity, and circulatory system disorders. Here, we used molecular dynamics simulations and pharmacological assays of receptor chimeras and point mutants to identify a crucial allosteric component of the mechanism by which RAMP2 and RAMP3 modulate CLR to confer selectivity for two adrenomedullin (AM) peptides. We found that the extracellular domain (ECD) of RAMP2 and RAMP3, but not RAMP1, stabilized a partially unwound “swing-out” conformation of the CLR ECD N-terminal α-helix to accommodate the unique binding mode of the midregion of the AM peptides. The inability of the CTR N-terminus to adopt the swing-out conformation contributed to the distinct peptide selectivity profile of the three CTR-RAMP amylin receptors. By exploiting the CLR swing-out conformation, we engineered AM antagonist peptide variants with enhanced affinity and selectivity for CLR-RAMP2 and -RAMP3. Our results reveal the long-sought mechanism of RAMP-altered CLR ligand selectivity and have significant implications for drug development targeting the CLR- and CTR-RAMP complexes.</jats:p>
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Fast-Charging Sodium Solid-State Batteries Enabled by closo -Hydridoborate Anode Interlayers for Sulfide Electrolytes
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Sodium solid-state batteries may offer high-power operation through highly conductive sulfide solid electrolytes but remain limited by unstable electrode|electrolyte interfaces. Bilayer separators can decouple interfacial requirements if electrochemical compatibility, contact quality, and charge transfer are ensured. Here, the closo-hydridoborate Na4(B10H10)(B12H12) is identified as an effective interlayer material for sulfide electrolytes. Time-dependent impedance measurements reveal that Na3PS4 bilayer cells still suffer from severe instability, while Na3SbS4 and Na2.9P0.9W0.1S4 bilayers are stabilized by the hydridoborate interlayer. For the latter cells, the interface resistance is easily dominated by poor mechanical contact but can be eliminated under moderate stack pressure. Incorporating Na4(B10H10)(B12H12) enables stable cycling of Na2.9P0.9W0.1S4-based cells with a TiS2-based cathode and Na15Sn4/Na3Sn anode, delivering &gt;90% capacity retention over 250 cycles and capacitor-like charging from 0–50% SOC in 30 s (82 mA cm–2) at 80 °C. The results identify closo-hydridoborate interlayers as key enablers for high-power sodium sulfide solid-state batteries.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Differentiable Solvation Shell Model for Rational Electrolyte Design
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tailoring the Li+ solvation shell is a central design principle for many emerging Li metal battery electrolytes but remains largely qualitative. Here, we introduce a mean-field Ising model that predicts the Li+ solvation shell from the donor number (DN), acceptor number, molar ratio, and molecular size. The model is end-to-end differentiable, enabling direct parameterization from molecular dynamics (MD) solvation structures. For localized high-concentration electrolytes, it reproduces MD shell compositions with 10.7% RMSE at much reduced cost and captures solvation trends in other electrolyte classes without re-fitting. Model interaction terms show that DN dominates Li+ solvation energetics, explaining the empirical DN-based design rules. For LiTFSI in tetraglyme absent from training, the model identifies fluorobenzene as a diluent and a concentration window with anion-rich solvation shells and low free solvent. The predicted solvation structure is confirmed by MD, and published experiments on related electrolytes support the design principles.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Ligand-field reconstruction enables 4.7 V LiCoO 2  with suppressed chemomechanical degradation for high-energy batteries
content: Raising the operating voltage of LiCoO2 cathodes offers a direct and attractive route to higher energy density. However, deep delithiation inevitably triggers severe chemomechanical degradation driven by excessive Co 3d–O 2p orbital hybridization, subsequent lattice oxygen evolution and catastrophic particle fracturing. Here we demonstrate that reconstructing the local transition-metal ligand-field stabilizes the LiCoO2 lattice during ultrahigh-voltage cycling at 4.7 V. By utilizing the moderate ionic potential of fluorine anions to drive this ligand-field reconstruction, we downshift the oxygen 2p band center and thereby decouple detrimental orbital overlap. This targeted electronic regulation dissipates lattice shear stress and minimizes anisotropic lattice distortion. While pristine LiCoO2 accumulates critical stress concentrations reaching 3.0 GPa that initiate extensive intragranular fracturing, our modified architecture alleviates internal stress accumulation and restricts the crack volume ratio to 0.034% after 500 cycles. Consequently, the anion-potential-modified LiCoO2 cathode delivers exceptional durability at 4.7 V, retaining 81.9% capacity over 500 cycles and 71.8% capacity over 1000 cycles at 1C. This work establishes a fundamental design paradigm for high-voltage cathodes, advancing the strategy from conventional surface protection toward intrinsic bulk electronic engineering, and offering a scalable pathway for next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries.
journal: Energy & Environmental Science advanceAccess

title: 4 V‐Class Calcium‐Based Water‐in‐Salt Electrolyte for Aqueous Calcium‐Ion Batteries
content:
A 6.2 m Ca(TFSI)2 water‐in‐salt electrolyte delivers a 4.19 V electrochemical stability window and remains liquid at sub‐zero temperatures after adding only 3 wt% acetonitrile. Its ion‐correlated Ca2+‐H2O‐TFSI− solvation structure supports low water activity and fast ion transport. These properties enable aqueous calcium‐ion full cells with stable operation down to −20°C, including a 3.2 V Sn‐based cell.








ABSTRACT
We report the first systematic investigation and demonstration of calcium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (Ca(TFSI)2) as a water‐in‐salt electrolyte for aqueous calcium‐ion batteries (CIBs). At its solubility limit (6.2 m), Ca(TFSI)2 exhibits a surprisingly wide electrochemical stability window (ESW) of 4.19 V, notably with the cathodic limit extending to ‐2.52 V vs Ag/AgCl, significantly surpassing previously reported Ca‐based aqueous electrolytes. Spectroscopic characterization combined with molecular simulations reveals a distinctive solvation structure in which Ca2+ coordinates oxygen atoms from both H2O and TFSI− within the first coordination shell, with an average coordination number of 7. Extensive ion association is also evident through solvent‐shared ion pairs, consistent with suppressed water activity and an expanded ESW. Furthermore, the addition of a small amount of acetonitrile enables the electrolyte to remain liquid at sub‐zero temperatures, while lowering viscosity and enhancing ionic conductivity without substantially disrupting the Ca2+ solvation structure. Leveraging these electrolyte properties, full cells employing perylene‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic diimide or Sn anodes and a Prussian blue analogue cathode demonstrate robust electrochemical performance at −20°C, including operation over a 3.2 V window with the Sn‐based cell, with long‐term cycling stability and sub‐zero device operation. These findings establish Ca(TFSI)2‐based water‐in‐salt electrolytes as a versatile platform for wide‐voltage, low‐temperature aqueous CIBs.

title: Investigation of Structure‐Property‐Performance Relationships of Binders in Graphitic Negative Electrodes for Lithium Ion Batteries on the Example of Systematically Modified Xanthan
content:
Systematic variation of xanthan‐based biopolymer binder structure reveals distinct links between acetylation, pyruvylation, side‐chain size and molecular weight and electrode performance. Acetylation enhances adhesion, whereas pyruvylation reduces adhesion and conductivity. Molecular weight governs rheology and processing stability, establishing molecular design principles for balancing adhesion, conductivity and paste control in graphitic lithium‐ion battery electrodes.








ABSTRACT
This study investigates structure‐property‐performance relationships of xanthan‐based biopolymer binders in graphitic negative electrodes in lithium‐ion batteries. Xanthan gum (XG) variants possess well‐defined molecular structures and stable shear‐thinning behavior, which makes them ideal for systematic investigations. The influence of side chain composition, degree of acetylation and/or pyruvylation, and polymer molecular weight is investigated on electrode and paste properties (i.e., adhesion, conductivity, rheology, and electrochemical performance). A higher degree of acetylation enhances adhesion through improved interaction with the non‐polar copper current collector, while other properties remain unaffected. In contrast, a pyruvyl group reduces adhesion and conductivity due to poor compatibility with non‐polar components, promoting carbon‐binder heterogeneity. Larger side groups hinder adhesion and thixotropy (paste relaxation) as steric effects restrict polymer flexibility and prolong paste relaxation. Higher polymer molecular weight improves shear‐thinning behavior and thixotropy, minimizing sedimentation and edge effects, though slightly decreasing conductivity. Overall, these results establish clear correlations between the molecular structure of (XG‐based) biopolymer binders and electrode performance. The insights provide design guidelines for optimizing binder composition to balance rheological control, adhesion, and conductivity, contributing to more efficient electrode processing and improved performance in next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents

title: Gating Oxygen Flux in High‐Nickel Layered Cathodes via a Surface‐Bulk Oxygen‐Fixation Framework
content:
An oxygen‐fixation‐gate strategy was proposed by introducing LaCeNb6O18 into high‐Ni layered cathodes, constructing a La/Ce‐rich surface oxygen‐buffering layer and Nb‐assisted bulk oxygen‐locking framework. The optimized 867‐LCNO0.5 cathode effectively suppressed lattice oxygen release, gas evolution, defect accumulation, and phase degradation, delivering 158.15 mAh g−1 at 10 C and 87.23% capacity retention after 200 cycles.








ABSTRACT
High‐Ni layered oxide cathodes suffer from severe high‐voltage degradation driven by oxygen‐vacancy evolution, lattice oxygen release, and interfacial reconstruction. Here, a LaCeNb6O18 ‐modified LiNi0.867Co0.103Mn0.003O2 cathode is designed to establish an oxygen‐fixation‐gate (OFG) framework for regulating oxygen flux across the surface‐bulk region. The modified cathode establishes a spatial oxygen‐fixation‐gate framework, integrating bulk oxygen locking by Nb, surface oxygen retention by La/Ce, and interfacial oxygen buffering by the oxygen‐vacancy‐rich layer. STEM, depth‐resolved XPS, XAS, DEMS, EPR, in situ XRD, and DFT calculations reveal that this coupled regulation stabilizes both oxygen chemistry and structural evolution. Specifically, the oxygen‐vacancy formation energy at the fully delithiated state increases from 1.13 to 1.31 eV, O2 evolution during initial high‐voltage charging is nearly eliminated, and oxygen‐defect accumulation during cycling is markedly restrained. Consequently, the optimized 867‐LCNO0.5 cathode delivers 158.15 mAh g−1 at 10 C, retains 87.23% capacity after 200 cycles, and maintains 80.03% retention after 200 cycles at 4.5 V vs. Li/Li+. This work establishes a spatially programmed oxygen‐fixation framework integrating bulk lattice oxygen locking, surface/subsurface oxygen anchoring, and interfacial oxygen‐vacancy buffering.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents

title: Dithioerythritol Enables Synchronized Crystallization and Buried Interface Passivation for Sn–Pb Perovskite Tandems
content:
A multifunctional dithioerythritol additive synchronizes crystallization kinetics and mitigates Sn2+ oxidation in narrow‐bandgap Sn–Pb perovskites. It eliminates buried‐interface voids, suppresses non‐radiative recombination, and boosts device efficiency and stability. High‐performance monolithic all‐perovskite tandem solar cells are achieved via coordinated defect passivation and morphological optimization.








ABSTRACT
Tin‐lead (Sn‐Pb) mixed narrow‐bandgap (NBG) perovskites (PVK) are key to all‐perovskite tandem solar cells (AP‐TSCs), but their development is hindered by Sn2+ oxidation and mismatched crystallization kinetics between Sn and Pb species. A critical issue is the “skin effect” during film formation, which traps solvent at the buried interface, creating voids and undercoordinated defects that cause non‐radiative recombination. Here, we introduce dithioerythritol (DTE) as a multifunctional additive. DTE's bidentate thiol groups coordinate with both Pb2+ and Sn2+, inducing delayed nucleation and slow growth, allowing complete solvent escape and eliminating voids. Simultaneously, DTE passivates defects, suppresses Sn2+ oxidation, and optimizes interfacial energy alignment. Consequently, DTE‐treated films show enhanced crystallinity, no buried voids, reduced Sn4+ fraction (from 50.27% to 22.95%), 50% lower trap density, and 7.9‐fold longer carrier lifetime. The optimized single‐junction NBG cell achieves 23.31% efficiency (Reverse scan, RS) with damp heat (DH) stability T80 of 750 h, outperforming the control (20.50%, 320 h). When integrated into monolithic two‐terminal (2T) tandems, the champion device delivers 28.82% efficiency (RS) and DH stability T80 of 1290 h, a 2.5‐fold enhancement over the control. This work demonstrates DTE as a promising additive that synchronizes crystallization, passivates defects, suppresses oxidation, and optimizes electronic structure for efficient and stable AP‐TSCs.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents

title: Function‐Decoupled Dual‐Anion Doping via Site‐Preferential Regulation Enables High‐Performance Lithium Argyrodite Electrolytes
content:
This work pioneers a site‐preferential dual‐anion doping strategy for lithium argyrodite electrolytes. O preferentially enriching the 16e sites enhances air stability and high‐voltage cathode compatibility, while Se at the 4d sites facilitates Li+ transport and promotes in situ formation of stable Li2O/Li2Se‐rich interphase. The decoupled design enables ultralong cycling over 4000 h in symmetric cells and maintains stable performance for 500 cycles in NCM811 full cells.








ABSTRACT
All‐solid‐state lithium metal batteries adopting argyrodite‐type sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SSEs) offer enhanced safety and energy density, yet face challenges in balancing ionic conductivity, air stability and interfacial compatibility. Herein, we pioneer a precursor‐directed site‐preferential dual‐anion doping strategy to address these trade‐offs. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal the oxygen precursor dictates the predominant anion occupancy: Li2O kinetically favors O at the 4d sites, whereas P2O5 preferentially directs O to the 16e sites. Guided by this principle, Li6PS4.2O0.4Se0.4Cl (LPSOSeCl) SSEs is designed, wherein O preferentially enriches 16e sites to enhance air stability and widen the electrochemical window for high‐voltage cathode compatibility, whereas Se preferentially enriches 4d sites to compensate ionic conductivity and promote a Li2Se/Li2O‐rich interphase for dendrite suppression. Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations combined with radial distribution functions (RDFs) further reveal that the Se/O co‐doping facilitates the formation of a stable Li/SSE interface, significantly inhibiting LPSOSeCl SSE reduction. The resulting LPSOSeCl SSE achieves high ionic conductivity, excellent moist air stability and remarkable critical current density (CCD) of 2.6 mA cm−2. The Li||Li symmetric cells demonstrate ultralong cycling stability over 4000 h at 0.2 mA cm−2 and LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 full cells rentain 70.7% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 0.3C.
journal: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents

title: Synergistic Interface Lubrication and Anion Anchoring in a Composite Solid‐State Electrolyte for Dendrite‐Free and Wide‐Temperature Zinc Metal Batteries
content:
This work introduces a composite solid‑state electrolyte that synergistically integrates EMIMTFSI ionic liquid and BN nanosheets into a PVDF‑HFP matrix to simultaneously address the interdependent challenges of low ionic conductivity, poor interfacial contact, and sluggish Zn2+−TFSI− coordination dynamics. EMIMTFSI acts as a plasticizer and interfacial lubricant, while BN serves as an anion‑anchoring agent via Lewis acid‐base interactions with TFSI−, facilitating interfacial ion dissociation and guiding uniform (002)‑oriented Zn deposition. This synergistic design enables dendrite‑free plating/stripping and stable wide‑temperature operation in solid‑state zinc metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
Solid‐state zinc‐ion batteries are promising for safe and flexible energy storage but suffer from low ionic conductivity and poor interfacial contact of polymer electrolytes. Herein, we report a composite solid‐state electrolyte (CSE) integrating 1‐ethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (EMIMTFSI) ionic liquid and boron nitride (BN) nanosheets into polyvinylidene fluoride hexafluoropropylene (PVDF‐HFP) matrix. EMIMTFSI acts as a plasticizer to suppress polymer crystallization, enhance ionic conductivity (5.23/0.76 mS cm−1 at 30/−20°C), and improve interfacial contact. Concurrently, BN anchors TFSI− via Lewis acid‐base interactions, regulating Zn2+−TFSI− coordination and facilitating ion dissociation, thereby guiding uniform Zn deposition along the (002) orientation. This synergy endows CSE with a high Zn2+ transference number (0.56) and a low activation energy (0.21 eV). Consequently, Zn//Zn cell cycles stablely for 2000 h at 0.5 mAh cm−2, and Zn//Cu cell delivers an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.75% for 1000 cycles. The Zn//hydrated aluminum vanadate (HAVO) full cell exhibits outstanding cycling stability (90.6% capacity retention after 6000 cycles), and stable operation at −20°C to 50°C. The Zn//HAVO pouch cell further demonstrates the practical viability of CSE in flexible electronics. This work presents a synergistic strategy for high‐performance polymer electrolytes, advancing the prospects of durable solid‐state zinc metal batteries.

title: Single‐Device Bidirectional Photonic Synapses: From Polarity Switching to Adaptive Neuromorphic Computing
content:
Single‐device bidirectional photonic synapses enable positive and negative photoresponses within one physical element, providing a compact platform for neuromorphic information processing. This review unifies their Structure–Regulation–Mechanism–Function relationships, benchmarks device and system performance, and identifies deterministic polarity control, programmable operation, and reproducible scaling as key directions toward adaptive photonic computing.








ABSTRACT
Neuromorphic vision requires hardware capable of integrating sensing, memory, and computation with bidirectional information processing. Single‐device bidirectional photonic synapses (BPS), which enable positive and negative photoresponses within the same physical element, provide a compact platform for adaptive photonic computing. However, the diverse architectures, regulation strategies, and physical mechanisms reported for BPS have hindered systematic understanding and quantitative comparison. Here, we establish a unified Structure–Regulation–Mechanism–Function (S–R–M–F) framework to organize single‐device BPS from device architecture and polarity regulation to physical mechanisms, synaptic functions, quantitative benchmarks and neuromorphic applications. We further distinguish physical photoresponse polarity from its functional interpretation in synaptic computing and highlight key considerations including energy consumption, reproducibility, variability, and system‐level scaling. Finally, we identify the transition from empirically observed PPC–NPC switching toward predictive, deterministic, programmable and reproducible operation as a key direction for future BPS development, with physics‐informed modeling and closed‐loop control offering promising routes toward adaptive photonic neuromorphic hardware.

title: Task‐Oriented Co‐Design of Optoelectronic Synaptic Devices: From Physical Mechanisms to System Integration
content:
A review on optoelectronic synaptic devices presents a task‐oriented framework that links application requirements with target device performance and cross‐level design strategies. Physical mechanisms and coordinated engineering of materials, interfaces, device architectures, and arrays are discussed to establish design principles for matching device characteristics to specific neuromorphic tasks and advancing scalable, energy‐efficient hardware.








ABSTRACT
Optoelectronic synaptic devices integrate optical sensing, state storage, and conductance modulation, offering high bandwidth, ultrafast response, and low energy consumption. These capabilities enable the development of energy‐efficient, scalable intelligent vision systems with rich synaptic plasticity, making optoelectronic synaptic devices one of the most promising approaches for overcoming the limitations of conventional von Neumann computing architectures. However, existing studies often evaluate device performance and synaptic functions under disparate structures and operating conditions, obscuring the relationships among physical mechanisms, device design, and task requirements, and limiting the establishment of generalizable design principles. This Review presents a task‐oriented framework that connects biological functions and application requirements with physical mechanisms, multilevel hardware design, and system integration. We first summarize biological synaptic and retinal functions and define key evaluation metrics and task requirements. We then discuss major operating mechanisms and strategies for coordinated optimization across materials, interfaces, device structures, and arrays. Representative applications are further reviewed, together with key challenges, including device stability, array uniformity, large‐scale integration, peripheral‐circuit overhead, and standardized benchmarking. By shifting the focus from isolated performance optimization toward cross‐level co‐design, this Review provides design guidelines for reproducible, scalable, and energy‐efficient optoelectronic neuromorphic hardware.

title: Self‐Calibrating Fluorescence‐Exclusion Microfluidic Platform for 3D Topographic Profiling of Living Cell Monolayers
content:
Multilayered micropillar references transform fluorescence exclusion images into self‐calibrated 3D height maps of living cell monolayers, enabling rapid, long‐term, label‐free topographic imaging in real time. This platform reveals vertical architectural descriptors across cell types and vertically biased osmotic remodeling in confluent cell monolayers, characterized by geometrically anisotropic and temporally decoupled vertical–lateral responses.








ABSTRACT
Cell monolayers are active living matter whose three‐dimensional (3D) architecture and mechanical remodeling regulate tissue function, yet fast and continuous topographic monitoring remains difficult. Here, we present fluorescence exclusion microscopy for monolayers (FLEXOM), a microfluidic platform combining multilayer micropillar arrays with negative‐staining optics to convert wide‐field images into self‐calibrated 3D height maps. Geometry‐anchored cavities allow in‐frame self‐calibration at confluence, correcting global intensity variations shared by sample and reference regions. FLEXOM enables longitudinal 3D profiling from isolated cells to confluent sheets with sub‐second temporal resolution, sub‐micrometer temporal height precision, and multiday biocompatibility and operational stability. FLEXOM reveals two distinct anisotropic signatures. First, monolayers show distinct cell type‐dependent vertical thickness profiles despite comparable lateral footprints. Two vertical descriptors, mean height and within‐cell height standard deviation, distinguish cell types more accurately than nine two‐dimensional (2D) lateral descriptors. Second, under acute osmotic shock, diverse confluent cell monolayers exhibit geometrically anisotropic vertical–lateral remodeling. Under hypotonic stimulation, projected area changes lag behind height changes. Consistent with this lag, cyclic hypotonic–isotonic switching at 3‐min intervals produces predominantly vertical remodeling with limited cycle‐dependent lateral changes. Our work provides a high‐resolution 3D profiling tool and a framework for axis‐resolved analysis of topographic responses in active living matter.

title: Ultrastable Chromium Pyrazolate Polyhedra With Amorphization‐Enhanced Microporosity for Corrosive Guest Capture
content:
A robust Cr(III)–pyrazolate metal–organic polyhedron (MOP) is constructed by combining strong‐field pyrazolate ligands with kinetically inert Cr(III) centers, exhibiting exceptional acid and alkali resistance. Remarkably, water‐induced amorphization largely preserves the discrete MOP cages while increasing the BET surface area from 614 to 1135 m2 g−1, thereby enhancing microporosity and adsorption capacity for corrosive gases.








ABSTRACT
The chemical stability of porous coordination solids is commonly rationalized using hard–soft acid–base (HSAB) considerations, which have largely excluded chromium(III)‐pyrazolate architectures owing to their incompatibility and the kinetic inertness of Cr(III). Here, we report the first porous chromium(III) pyrazolate metal–organic polyhedron. The material exhibits extraordinary chemical robustness, remaining chemically intact over a pH window spanning 13.7 units (pH < 0 to 13). The protonation tendency of azolate ligands is largely suppressed upon coordination to Cr(III), leading to resistance to acidic environments. Remarkably, even after amorphization induced by prolonged boiling in water (Cr(III)‐MOP‐A), the discrete Cr–pyrazolate cages persist, as evidenced by XPS and EXAFS, accompanied by an approximately twofold increase in the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface area. This unexpected robustness originates from a ligand‐field‐dominated stability regime in which the d3 electronic configuration of Cr(III) maximizes crystal‐field stabilization energy, leading to unusually strong Cr–N (pyrazolate) bonding that overrides HSAB‐based expectations. Such robustness enables efficient and recyclable adsorption of highly corrosive guests, including water vapor, SO2, and NH3. Notably, the amorphous MOP achieves the highest SO2 uptake reported among metal–organic polyhedra, exceeding the previous benchmark by 74%, together with outstanding SO2/CO2 selectivity that is corroborated by dynamic breakthrough experiments.

title: Oxygen‐Stacking Reconstruction of Spent LiCoO2 for Fast Li‐Ion Kinetics and High‐Voltage Stability
content:
Hydrometallurgical recovery of spent LiCoO2 enables conventional O3‐type regeneration and ion‐exchange upgrading to O2‐type LiCoO2. Compared with O3‐LiCoO2, the O2‐LiCoO2 exhibits larger Li‐layer spacing, faster Li+ transport, and improved high‐voltage cycling stability, delivering 201 mAh g−1 at 20C in coin cells and 486 Wh kg−1 at 1C in a 2 Ah‐level pouch cell.








ABSTRACT
Recycling spent LiCoO2 battery cathodes is essential for securing the sustainable supply of lithium and cobalt, yet current recycling methods mainly produce metal salts, precursors, or conventionally regenerated cathodes, making the recovery of high‐value LiCoO2 with enhanced electrochemical performance remain challenging. To address this challenge, we systematically investigate and compare conventionally regenerated O3‐type LiCoO2 (O3‐R‐LCO) and O2‐type LiCoO2 produced through a hydrometallurgy‐assisted ion‐exchange upcycling strategy (O2‐UP‐LCO). The upgraded O2‐UP‐LCO preserves the local CoO6 framework while exhibiting enlarged Li‐layer spacing and a more open interlayer structure compared with O3‐R‐LCO. Multiscale characterizations further reveal that the distinct oxygen stacking in O2‐UP‐LCO enables fast Li+ transport and stable interfacial reaction kinetics, despite reversible phase transitions during cycling. Benefiting from these structural and kinetic advantages, O2‐UP‐LCO delivers 201 mAh g−1 even at 20C in coin cells and achieves an energy density of 486 Wh kg−1 at 1C in a 2 Ah‐level pouch cell. In contrast, O3‐R‐LCO suffers from restricted Li+ diffusion and increased interfacial impedance at high voltage, accompanied by aggravated particle cracking after cycling. Overall, this work provides a polymorph‐upgrading strategy for efficient recovery of spent LiCoO2 material.

title: Dynamic Commercial Silicones Toward Sustainable, Task‐Reconfigurable Suction Gripping
content:
An all‐silicone, hierarchically structured suction gripper combining a reconfigurable load‐bearing body with a compliant sealing interface that balances customization, system complexity, and gripping performance towards task‐reconfigurable applications. The shape reconfigurability is enabled by NTBD‐trigger dynamic siloxane bonds exchange that are generally applicable to commercial silicones.








ABSTRACT
Silicone suction cups are widely used in industrial automation for scalable, high‐throughput handling, yet conventional designs are restricted to limited geometries. Advancing toward gripping is essential to transition robotics from single‐task execution to versatile handling across dynamic environments but presents a fundamental materials challenge: balancing the properties of on‐demand geometric reconfigurability with operational strength and elasticity. Existing universal grippers typically utilize composite materials that couple shape adaptation and gripping operation within a single cycle, introducing critical performance trade‐offs in force, speed, and preload requirements while adding structural complexity that together hinder broad industrial adoption. To address this, we establish a versatile post‐fabrication strategy that transforms commercial silicone thermosets into dynamic silicone materials via catalyst‐mediated exchange of intrinsic siloxane bonds. This enables scalable transformation of industrial suction cups to reconfigurable grippers that reconfigure shapes at elevated temperatures while preserving high gripping performance via thermosetting properties at ambient temperatures. We demonstrate an all‐silicone, hierarchically structured suction gripper combining a reconfigurable load‐bearing body with a compliant sealing interface towards sustainable, task‐reconfigurable gripping, ensuring infrastructure compatibility while delivering rapid suction actuation (50 ms) following thermal reconfiguration (e.g., ∼30 min at 140°C), efficient load capacity (27 kPa), and zero‐preload attachment across diverse environments.

title: Chiral Bobbers in the Room‐Temperature Magnet Co8Zn10Mn2
content:
Chiral bobbers are three‐dimensional magnetic solitons that form where a skyrmion string terminates inside the magnet at a Bloch point. So far, they appear only at cryogenic temperatures. Lorentz transmission electron microscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations now reveals them at room temperature in chiral magnet Co8Zn10Mn2 and captures skyrmion strings transforming into bobbers as the magnetic field increases.








ABSTRACT
Chiral bobbers are three‐dimensional magnetic solitons that emerge near surfaces of chiral magnets with bulk‐type Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. They can be regarded as skyrmion strings terminated by a Bloch point inside the material. So far, chiral bobbers have been observed only at cryogenic temperatures. Here, we report the direct observation of chiral bobbers in Co8Zn10Mn2${\rm Co}_8{\rm Zn}_{10}{\rm Mn}_2$ over a broad temperature range, including room temperature. Using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations, we identify a previously unreported nucleation pathway in which skyrmion strings transform into chiral bobbers under an applied magnetic field. We also demonstrate that chiral bobbers on opposite surfaces can be coupled to form double‐bobber states. These findings establish chiral bobbers as room‐temperature magnetic textures and identify their role in the nucleation pathways of topological magnetic solitons.

title: Medium‐Entropy Metallene Enables Sequential Hot‐Carrier Nanocatalytic Triaptosis Induction for Suppressing Tumor Growth and Metastasis
content:
Ultrathin PdCuCo medium‐entropy metallenes convert ultrasound energy into hot carriers that drive sequential nanocatalysis. By amplifying oxidative stress, depleting antioxidant defenses, and disrupting endosomal homeostasis, this process induces triaptosis, an endosomal dysfunction‐driven cell death modality. This ultrasound‐activated strategy suppresses both primary tumor growth and distant metastasis, establishing medium‐entropy metallenes as a sonocatalytic cancer therapy platform.








ABSTRACT
Triaptosis, a newly recognized cell death modality driven by endosomal dysfunction and persistent vacuolization, holds promise for tumor therapy. However, its clinical translation has been hindered by the lack of spatiotemporally controllable strategies to disrupt endosomal homeostasis. Herein, we engineer ultrathin PdCuCo medium‐entropy metallene catalysts (PCC MEMCs) as a new class of sono‐activatable catalytic biomaterials that induce triaptosis for tumor therapy. Upon ultrasound irradiation, lattice oscillations in PCC MEMCs generate non‐equilibrium hot carriers that execute two synergistic catalytic functions. These high‐energy hot carriers directly drive interfacial electron transfer with H2O and O2 to produce hydroxyl radicals and superoxide anions, with sufficiently energetic carriers further converting triplet oxygen to singlet oxygen. Simultaneously, these hot carriers accelerate the intrinsic enzyocatalytic reactions by lowering surface adsorption barriers and enhancing charge transfer. This sequential nanocatalysis triggers a massive oxidative burst and substantial depletion of antioxidants, leading to VPS34 oxidation, PI(3)P depletion, and disruption of early endosomal processing. Consequently, persistent vacuolization and membrane collapse induce triaptosis, effectively suppressing tumor growth and metastasis. Collectively, this work establishes a sono‑activatable hot‑carrier sequential nanocatalytic paradigm, offers a distinct nanotherapeutic strategy against tumors via triaptosis induction, and broadens the biomedical scope of medium‐entropy metallenes toward sonocatalytic therapy.

title: Interfacial Electronic‐Structural Coupling Suppresses Jahn‐Teller Instability in NASICON Cathode Casting Long Cycling Life
content:
To suppress the Jahn‐Teller effect in NVMP, a mosaic‐like heterostructure with abundant NVMP/NFP interfaces is constructed. The Interfacial charge redistribution strengthens Mn─O interactions, weakens the localization and spin polarization of Mn‐centered electronic states, and reduces local structural distortion, while dispersed NFP domains act as internal structural boundaries to accommodate strain and inhibit the amplification of local instability into bulk lattice degradation.








ABSTRACT
NASICON‐type Na4VMn(PO4)3 cathodes possess attractive high‐voltage and structural robustness, yet its application is hindered by the intrinsic instability of Mn3+‐induced Jahn‐Teller distortion. A mosaic‐like Na4VMn(PO4)3/NaFePO4 (NVMP/NFP) heterostructure is constructed to achieve interfacial electronic‐structural synergistic regulation. The nanoscale heterointerfaces induce charge redistribution and modify the local electronic environment, thereby strengthening Mn─O interactions indirectly and interrupting the spatial correlation of local distortions, which successfully suppresses the Jahn‐Teller instability. The suppression of local electronic instability by the NVMP/NFP heterostructure is confirmed by complementary experimental and theoretical analyses, which further reveal reversible V3+/V4+ and Mn2+/Mn3+ redox reactions. Furthermore, the heterointerface reconstructs the Na+ transport network by generating more interconnected and multidimensional migration pathways with reduced diffusion barriers, mitigates the accumulation of lattice strain during Na+ extraction/insertion and fosters electron transfer, casting fast reversible electrochemical reaction. Benefiting from this interfacial electronic‐structural coupling, the optimized NVMP/NFP cathode delivers excellent wide‐temperature cycling stability, retaining 89.91% capacity after 6000 cycles at 2 A g−1, 91.80% after 2500 cycles at ‐15°C, and 80.23% after 6000 cycles at 45°C. This work provides an interfacial engineering strategy for decoupling electronic instability from structural degradation and offers a general pathway for stabilizing Jahn‐Teller active electrode materials.

title: Coordination‐Driven Spiral Self‐Assembly of Helical Mesoporous Polymer Nanospheres and Derived MoS2/Carbon Colloidal Nanospheres for Fast Lithium Storage
content:
A coordination‐driven spiral self‐assembly strategy is developed to construct helical mesoporous polymer nanospheres with inner‐outer helical features, tunable pore size and composition. After carbonization, the derived monolayer MoS2/C colloidal nanospheres with abundant active sites and continuous helical transport pathways facilitate Li+ transport, ion enrichment, and interfacial charge transfer, showcasing exceptional lithium‐storage performance.








ABSTRACT
Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied on chiral templates or complex assembly procedures, limiting structural tunability and compositional flexibility. Herein, we develop a coordination‐driven spiral self‐assembly (CSS) strategy that converts achiral building blocks into helical mesoporous polymer nanospheres (HMPSs) with continuous spiral surface textures and internal helical mesopores. Interfacial Mo–S coordination drives micellar spiral organization without chiral additives, enabling systematic regulation of pore size, morphology, and composition. Subsequent carbonization transforms HMPSs into helical mesoporous MoS2/C nanospheres (HMMoS2/C) containing uniformly dispersed monolayer MoS2 while retaining the helical mesostructure. Finite‐element simulations and density functional theory calculations reveal that the helical mesoporous architecture facilitates rapid Li+ diffusion, local ion enrichment, and interfacial charge transfer, thereby improving Li‐storage kinetics. Consequently, HMMoS2/C delivers a reversible capacity of 1776.3 mAh g−1 at 0.3 A g−1 after 150 cycles, a high‐rate capacity of 752.7 mAh g−1 at 10 A g−1, and outstanding long‐term cycling stability. This work establishes coordination‐driven self‐assembly as a versatile route to helical mesoporous materials for energy storage.

title: Octahedral Co3+ Spin‐State Regulation in W‐Doped Co3O4 for Accelerated Sulfur Redox Kinetics
content:
The role of transition metal spin‐state modulation in enhancing the electrocatalysis of lithium–sulfur reactions has been elucidated, with particular emphasis on the associated charge transfer processes. This provides valuable guidance for the design and engineering of advanced cathode materials for next‐generation sulfur‐based batteries.








ABSTRACT
Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) are promising high‐energy storage systems, but their practical application remains limited by the low electronic conductivity of sulfur, sluggish Li–S redox kinetics, and the lithium polysulfide (LiPS) shuttle effect. These challenges require the rational design of cathode catalysts with well‐regulated electronic structures and active sites. Herein, Cu2+ and Al3+ substitution in Co3O4 was first used to identify the catalytic roles of Co sites with different coordination environments, forming CuCo2O4 and CoAl2O4 as model systems. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that octahedral Co3+ sites play a key role in enhancing LiPS adsorption and Li–S reaction kinetics. Guided by this insight, tungsten species with different oxidation states were used to direct distinct local perturbations of tetrahedral‐ and octahedral‐Co‐site environments in Co3O4, yielding WTd‐Co3O4@NC and WOh‐Co3O4@NC, respectively, where NC denotes nitrogen‐doped carbon. Magnetic measurements and DFT calculations demonstrate that W6+ doping induces a low‐spin to high‐spin transition of Co3+, generating additional unpaired 3d electrons that strengthen LiPS adsorption and accelerate LiPS conversion. As a result, WOh‐Co3O4@NC/S delivers high capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling stability, even under lean‐electrolyte conditions. This work demonstrates spin‐state engineering of octahedral Co3+ sites as an effective strategy to optimize catalytic activity for LSBs.

title: A Mesohydrous Metallic Gel for Imperceptible Electrophysiology
content:
Inspired by the mesohydrous, ultrathin human stratum corneum, we design a biomimetic mesohydrous metallic gel (25 wt% water, sub‐micrometer) with a percolating silver nanowire network. It achieves metal‑grade conductivity, dual‑mode conduction, conformability, and ambient stability without encapsulation. Such a mesohydrous metallic gel is promising for the design of imperceptible, long‐term stable next‐generation bioelectronic interfaces.








ABSTRACT
Imperceptible skin electronic interfaces for bidirectional communication are essential for next‑generation healthcare and human–machine interfaces. The long‑standing absence of an ideal interfacing material has made it challenging to achieve high‑quality bidirectional electrophysiology without disturbing innate perception. Inspired by the human stratum corneum's mesohydrous state, we report a metallic stratum corneum (MSC): a synthetic mesohydrous gel reinforced with a silver nanowire network. MSC achieves > 106 S m−1 conductivity, dual‑mode (electronic/ionic) conduction, sub‐micron thickness, and months‑long ambient stability. Its porous ultrathin architecture enables multidimensional imperceptibility (tactile, mechanical, thermal, and vapor‑permeable). MSC records electrophysiology with signal‑to‑noise ratio surpassing commercial gel electrodes, delivers efficient neuromuscular stimulation, and forms high‑resolution electrode arrays for spatiotemporal muscle mapping. By reconciling electronic performance, skin compatibility, and imperceptibility, the mesohydrous gel establishes a promising material platform for next‐generation on‐skin bioelectronics.

title: A Climate‐Adaptive Window Enabling All‐Day Anti‐/Deicing and Dynamic Thermal Management
content:
A climate‐adaptive transparent window integrates spectrally selective thermochromism, photo‐electrothermal heating, and superhydrophobicity to enable efficient anti‐/deicing and dynamic thermal management. By balancing solar energy harvesting in cold conditions with reduced solar heat gain in warm conditions, this multifunctional architecture offers an integrated strategy for year‐round window performance across various climate regions.








ABSTRACT
Transparent anti‐/deicing materials have traditionally focused on maximizing solar harvesting to achieve efficient ice mitigation under cold conditions. However, this approach can introduce overheating risks during warm periods, creating a challenge in balancing anti‐/deicing and thermal management. Here, we report a climate‐adaptive window consisting of a spectrally selective optical switch, a hybrid Joule‐heating and a highly transparent superhydrophobic coating. Guided by an energy‐balance framework for full spectrum design, the window simultaneously achieves high luminous transmittance (65.2%), strong near‐infrared absorption (76.1%), and large solar modulation capability (36.0%), enabling dynamic thermal regulation while preserving robust anti‐/deicing functionality. The synergistic interplay of photo‐electrothermal heating, thermal retention, and superhydrophobicity extends icing delay by 11‐fold and realizes rapid all‐day deicing at −20°C. Under hot conditions, the thermochromism reduces the average indoor temperature by 15.2°C, substantially reducing building cooling demand and boosting greenhouse seedling biomass relative to conventional configurations. By integrating solar modulation with transparent anti‐/deicing functionality, this work paves the way for the development of next‐generation climate‐adaptive windows.

title: Ultrasound Rechargeable Bioelectronics With Acoustic Metamaterial‐Enhanced Triboelectric Energy Harvesting
content:
A transmissive acoustic metamaterial shell confines ultrasound within an internal chamber, enhancing energy harvesting by a thin‐film triboelectric nanogenerator. Integrated power management enables low‐duty‐cycle trans‐tissue recharging and programmable electrical stimulation. This proof‐of‐concept platform elicits reproducible neuromuscular responses ex vivo, providing a system‐level strategy for ultrasound‐rechargeable bioelectronics and a foundation for future implantable neuromodulation systems.








ABSTRACT
Wireless transcutaneous energy transfer to deep‐tissue bioelectronic implants remains challenging for long‐term autonomous bioelectronic operation because tissue attenuation limits the available acoustic excitation. Here, we present a proof‐of‐concept ultrasound rechargeable bioelectronic platform that integrates spatially confined acoustic energy delivery, energy harvesting, power management, and programmable electrical stimulation. A non‐resonant, transmissive acoustic metamaterial reshapes the incident ultrasound wavefront to form a localized field in the receiving region. The platform couples this acoustic structure with a compliant thin‐film triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for energy harvesting in a fluidic environment. An on‐board power conditioning circuit regulates the harvested energy to support recharging and controlled electrical pulse delivery. In ex vivo evaluations using a layered porcine‐tissue configuration, approximately 3.5 min of ultrasonic recharging supports nearly 16 h of programmed pulse generation into a 5 kΩ surrogate load, corresponding to an acoustic charging duty cycle of 0.36%. The stored energy also powered electrical pulses that evoked repeatable limb movement in ex vivo frog preparations. These results demonstrate a system‐level strategy for ultrasound‐rechargeable bioelectronics, providing a basis for future implantable neuromodulation systems.

title: Coupling Macrophage Reeducation With Mechanical Remodeling of the Tumor Extracellular Matrix to Enhance Pancreatic Cancer Immunotherapy
content:
A multi‐arm polymer conjugate of resiquimod and soy protein (mPDPC‐RS) enhances tumor‐associated macrophage uptake, switches them to an antitumor M1 phenotype, and reduces extracellular matrix, interstitial fluid pressure, solid stress, and Young's modulus. This dual bio‐mechanical approach unleashes CD8+ T‐cell infiltration, suppresses tumor growth, and offers a novel platform with high macrophage avidity for pancreatic cancer immunotherapy.








ABSTRACT
One major challenge in reeducating macrophages lies in the specific delivery of therapeutic agents to these cells. Here we report a multi‐arm polymer conjugate of the toll‐like receptor 7/8 agonist resiquimod and soy protein (mPDPC‐RS) that simultaneously dismantles the immune and physical barriers within pancreatic tumors. Upon systemic administration, mPDPC‐RS preferentially accumulates in tumor‐associated macrophages in vivo, repolarizes them toward an antitumor phenotype, and thereby initiates robust immune responses. Concurrently, mPDPC‐RS reduces interstitial fluid pressure and solid stress of the tumor as well as tumor stiffness, thereby facilitating CD8+ T cell infiltration. In murine pancreatic cancer models, this dual‐function platform produces profound tumor suppression and markedly extends survival. Our findings provide a versatile platform with high macrophage avidity for cancer immunotherapy and establish a comprehensive strategy for overcoming both biological and mechanical defenses of the tumor microenvironment to improve immunotherapeutic outcomes in pancreatic cancer.

title: Tuning σ‐Type Ni─O Orbital Hybridization for Stable Ultrahigh‐Ni Cathodes
content:
ABSTRACT
Ultrahigh‐Ni layered oxides have emerged as leading candidates for next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs), yet they suffer from severe chemo‐mechanical degradation driven by irreversible lattice oxygen loss during cycling. In this study, we propose an orbital hybridization regulation strategy via co‐doping high‐electronegativity cations (M = Zr4+/Ta5+/W6+) to stabilize lattice oxygen and improve redox reversibility. Combined structural and theoretical analyses reveal that co‐doping induces electron redistribution around oxygen atoms, thereby weakening σ‐type Ni–O hybridization and suppressing irreversible ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer and oxygen vacancy formation. Concurrently, the enhanced covalency of M─O bonds facilitates electron delocalization for charge compensation that reduces highly oxidized nickel species in the charged state. This stabilized redox chemistry mitigates transition metal (TM) migration, lattice distortion, and crack propagation. Additionally, elemental co‐doping also induces a lattice‐coherent rock‐salt surface layer that effectively suppresses interfacial parasitic reactions. The co‐doped cathode delivers exceptional cycling stability, with nearly 100% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 1 C (2.7–4.3 V) in half cells, and 93.5% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C (2.8–4.2 V) in pouch cells. This study provides an alternative avenue for stable ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes from the perspective of local chemistry and orbital hybridization modulation.

title: Reaction‐Pathway Regulation for Degradation‐Insensitive Direct Regeneration of Spent LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 Cathode Materials
content:
Direct regeneration of NCM523 is governed by degradation‐dependent competition among relithiation, structural recovery, and thermal decomposition. Replacing Li2CO3 with LiAc redirects differently degraded cathode materials through the same type of low‐symmetry reconstruction state, reducing degradation‐state dependence and enabling regeneration under unified conditions. The lithium‐source reactant thus emerges as an active regulator of the regeneration pathway.








ABSTRACT
Direct regeneration is limited by degradation‐dependent processing because cathodes with different degradation states cannot be regenerated using a uniform protocol. Using LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 (NCM523) cathode materials with different degradation states, we show that this limitation originates from competition among relithiation, structural recovery, and thermal decomposition during calcination. As the balance of these competing reactions shifts with degradation state, cathodes evolve along distinct reaction trajectories. Recognizing that these reactions are governed by the reactants, we regulate the regeneration reaction through the lithium‐source reactant, causing cathode materials with different degradation states to pass through the same type of low‐symmetry, synthesis‐derived intermediate structure during calcination. This redirects regeneration toward a reconstruction pathway with favorable thermodynamics and improved ion diffusion, enabling rapid Li replenishment, long‐range cation ordering, and structural restoration. Consequently, practical NCM523 black mass is regenerated into cathodes that deliver higher capacity and better capacity retention than those regenerated via the conventional pathway, and a 1.3 Ah pouch cell with the regenerated cathode retains 80.2% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles. This reconstruction pathway also enables direct upcycling of degraded NCM523 toward higher‐Ni compositions. Broadly, this work provides a mechanistic framework for reducing degradation‐state dependence in direct regeneration of spent cathode materials.

title: Size‐Dependent Photoelectric and Photothermal Effects in Plasmon‐Induced Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
content:
Nanoparticle size governs the competition between hot‐electron and photothermal pathways in plasmon‐driven hydrogen evolution. Quantitative analysis reveals a mechanistic transition from hot‐electron‐dominated catalysis to photoelectronic and photothermal synergy, while electrolyte conditions further reshape the catalytic pathway. The results establish mechanistic framework for engineering plasmonic photocatalysts.








ABSTRACT
Plasmonic photocatalysis relies on the conversion of photon energy into nonequilibrium charge carriers and heat. However, the relative contributions of these processes and their size‐dependent roles in photocatalysis remain unclear because of their intrinsically intertwined nature. Here, size‐controlled Ag NPs/p‐GaN heterostructures are employed to quantitatively disentangle the size‐dependent roles of hot‐electron injection and surface heating in determining photocatalytic activity. Analysis of the size‐dependent hydrogen evolution reaction activity shows that the apparent contribution of localized heating is strongly dependent on Ag NP size, accounting for less than 10% of the overall activity in smaller particles (< 28 nm) but increasing to nearly 50% in larger particles. Spatially resolved SPV imaging reveals enhanced charge separation with increasing Ag NP size, while ultrafast spectroscopy shows elevated electron temperatures and prolonged electron‐phonon coupling dynamics. By combining spatially and temporally resolved techniques, we observe a correlation between the systematic evolution of local charge density and hot‐carrier relaxation dynamics with particle size while identifying an important role of heat in the enhancement. These results identify plasmonic nanoparticle size as a critical determinant of the photocatalytic mechanism, offering a mechanistic framework for selectively routing solar energy into targeted photocatalytic pathways.
