title: Copper‐Catalyzed Enantioconvergent 1,4‐Difunctionalization of Homoallylic and Homopropargylic Alcohols via Radical‐Relay Deoxygenation
content:
A general and efficient platform for the enantioconvergent deoxygenative 1,4‐difunctionalization of racemic homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols upon an unprecedented remote hydrogen atom transfer‐triggered radical deoxygenation process is presented. Both 1,4‐perfluoroalkylamidation and 1,4‐cyanoperfluoroalkylation have been developed by copper/bisoxazoline asymmetric catalysis, enabling facile access to diverse chiral perfluoroalkyl‐containing amides and nitriles with excellent enantiomeric excess.








ABSTRACT
Despite the long‐recognized structural diversity and accessibility of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols as synthetic building blocks, their deoxygenative radical difunctionalization remains a formidable challenge due to the lack of a linkage strategy integrating the respective functionalization of non‐adjacent hydroxyl and alkene/alkyne groups. Herein, we present an efficient platform for the deoxygenative radical 1,4‐difunctionalization of homoallylic and homopropargylic alcohols through an unprecedented remote hydrogen atom transfer‐triggered radical‐relay deoxygenation process. Utilizing 1,3‐benzodithiolylium as an effective hydroxyl‐activating reagent, copper‐catalyzed enantioconvergent 1,4‐perfluoroalkylamidation and 1,4‐cyanoperfluoroalkylation have been achieved with excellent regio‐ and enantioselectivity.

title: Quenching or Accelerating Large‐Scale Surface Reconstruction by the Lightest Element: Facet‐Dependent Hydrogen‐Induced Reconstruction (HIR)
content:
The facet‐dependent kinetics of hydrogen‐induced reconstruction (HIR) on Pd–Ag surfaces is revealed by machine‐learning (ML)‐based global potential‐energy exploration combined with large‐scale molecular dynamics (MD) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The outcomes underscore that hydrogen stabilizes Pd domains on Ag(111) but promotes Pd dispersion on Ag(100), thereby shaping Pd3 active motifs for selective acetylene hydrogenation.








ABSTRACT
Adsorbate‐induced surface reconstruction is believed to be a critical determinant of catalyst performance under operando conditions. The Pd–Ag bimetallic catalyst, used industrially for selective acetylene hydrogenation, is thought to undergo hydrogen‐induced surface reconstruction (HIR) that exposes Pd active sites. However, the kinetic origin of HIR remains unknown because hydrogen is difficult to image. Here, using large‐scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we resolve the kinetics of H‐driven reconstruction. On Pd‐covered Ag surfaces, reconstruction initially involves Pd–Ag exchange at domain peripheries and Ag atoms popping up to encapsulate exposed Pd. This process is faster on (100) than on (111). Hydrogen suppresses reconstruction on (111) above 0.3 ML, but accelerates Pd dispersion and encapsulation on (100) mediated by transient Pd–H pair formation. This facet dependence arises from hydrogen‐induced kinetic hindrance of edge Pd diffusion away from Pd domains on (111). Analysis of MD‐derived surface structures further shows that the Pd3 triangular surface pattern favors selective acetylene hydrogenation, confirming HIR's role in determining active‐site structure. These findings provide the first evidence for facet‐dependent, large‐scale surface reconstruction induced by the lightest element and establish HIR as a key determinant of catalytic activity and selectivity.

title: Multi‐Scale Structural Degradation Mechanisms in Ni‐Rich NCM Cathodes
content:
Structural degradation in Ni‐rich cathodes arises from interconnected processes across electronic/chemical‐bonding, local atomic, lattice/phase, and particle/interface levels. This review elucidates cross‐scale causal propagation and bidirectional feedback through advanced characterization and theoretical analysis, identifying critical coupling nodes to guide predictive multiscale design strategies for improved structural stability and electrochemical performance.








ABSTRACT
Ni‐rich layered oxides (LiNixCoyMnzO2, x > 0.8, NCM) are among the most promising cathode materials for high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries, yet increasing nickel content intrinsically amplifies structural instability during deep delithiation and prolonged cycling. The resulting performance decay is not governed by an individual failure mode, but emerges from coupled evolution of electronic/chemical‐bonding, local atomic, lattice/phase, and particle/interface levels. This review establishes a multiscale structure‐performance framework. The evolution of Ni 3d‐O 2p hybridization and oxygen redox activity modifies metal‐oxygen bonding, triggering local structural disorder, lattice reconstruction, and strain accumulation. These changes promote particle cracking and interfacial degradation, while particle damage further accelerates electrolyte reactions and oxygen loss through feedback interactions, establishing a self‐amplifying degradation network. By integrating operando characterization and theoretical analysis, this review identifies critical coupling nodes and provides mechanism‐guided principles for rational modification strategies. Future efforts should develop predictive multiscale design frameworks that bridge fundamental degradation mechanisms with practical engineering of next‐generation Ni‐rich cathodes.

title: A General Workflow for Ab Initio Nanocrystal Structure Determination From Serial Electron Diffraction, Demonstrated Using 4DSTEM Data
content:
The manuscript presents a fully ab initio workflow for serial electron‐diffraction structure analysis, including unit‐cell parameter determination, from 4DSTEM data. The workflow is demonstrated on a nanocrystalline organic pigment with triclinic symmetry, a particularly challenging test case, showing robust and reproducible structure determination from submicron crystals using serial 4DSTEM datasets.








ABSTRACT
We present an end‐to‐end ab initio workflow for crystal‐structure determination from parallel‐beam, precession‐assisted 4DSTEM serial electron diffraction data. The pipeline combines automated unit‐cell determination from zonal‐pattern subsets, large‐scale pattern filtering and integration with CrystFEL, and integration of filtered condensed datasets in PETS2 followed by dynamical refinement. Beam precession enables dynamical refinement using condensed datasets, revealing fine structural features: For β‐Pigment Orange 36 we resolve the tautomeric state and unambiguously identify the hydrazone form. We also characterize the sample texture, demonstrating an unusual biaxial orientation distribution that explains the high completeness observed at zero sample tilt. The workflow is truly ab initio and handles large datasets efficiently, though creation of condensed inputs remains manual; full automation is a target for future development.

title: Targeted NIRF‐OCT Imaging of Inflammatory Atherosclerotic Plaques Using Donor–Acceptor Nanoprobes
content:
A dual‐modality intravascular NIRF‐OCT catheter combines optical coherence tomography with near‐infrared fluorescence imaging using osteopontin‐targeted donor–acceptor nanoprobes. A pseudocolor fluorescence ring complements OCT cross‐sections, providing spatially co‐registered structural and molecular information. Preferential nanoprobe accumulation in plaques and associations between fluorescence intensity and osteopontin staining support complementary assessment of plaque morphology and inflammation‐associated molecular heterogeneity.








ABSTRACT
Current intravascular imaging modalities lack biological insight into atherosclerotic plaque inflammation, a key driver of plaque vulnerability. To address this limitation, we developed a targeted molecular probe for near‐infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging, integrated with optical coherence tomography (OCT) within a dual‐modality catheter. This approach enables co‐registered structural and molecular visualization of high‐risk inflammatory plaques by detecting osteopontin (OPN)‐rich regions associated with macrophage‐derived foam cells. We synthesized a planar donor–acceptor small‐molecule probe, termed DMe‐DFIC, and formulated it into nanoparticles (NPs) exhibiting broad absorption from 600 to 800 nm and near‐infrared emission from 900 to 1300 nm. Following conjugation with an anti‐OPN antibody, the resulting targeted formulation, designated OPDD NPs, showed preferential accumulation in atherosclerotic iliac‐femoral arteries, with fluorescence intensity peaking 12 h after injection. In vivo multimodal NIRF‐OCT imaging showed that elevated fluorescence signals were observed in regions exhibiting lipid‐associated OCT morphology. Histopathological analyses further confirmed that these regions exhibited substantial lipid deposition, intense OPN expression, and dense macrophage infiltration. Collectively, the integration of targeted OPDD NPs with dual‐modality NIRF‐OCT imaging provides synchronized structural and molecular characterization of inflammatory plaques, supporting further preclinical evaluation of this approach for inflammation‐associated molecular imaging.

title: Residue‐Assisted Surface Reconstruction Enables High Compatibility and Stable Electrochemical Performance of LLZTO for Composite Separator
content:
Alkaline residues on LLZTO are repurposed to trigger PVDF dehydrofluorination, creating a LiF/polymer‐containing interphases rather than remaining passive contaminants. The reconstructed particles form a uniform coating on PE, improve electrolyte affinity and Li+ transport, and enable stable lithium plating/stripping for over 1100 h, revealing an unexpected route from surface residues to functional interfaces.








ABSTRACT
Among the various designs of lithium metal batteries using limited liquid electrolyte, separator coating with garnet oxides is a promising alternative because it is compatible with existing battery manufacturing processes and can improve electrochemical performance. However, alkaline residues on surface of garnet oxides induce PVDF dehydrofluorination and slurry gelation during slurry preparation, leading to uneven separator coatings and poor electrochemical performance. Herein, a residue‐assisted surface reconstruction strategy is proposed to convert the surface residues on Ta‐doped garnet Li6.5La3Zr1.5Ta0.5O12 (LLZTO) into a LiF/polymer‐containing compositionally graded interphase. Specifically, LLZTO powders were first immersed in a PVDF‐containing solvent before slurry preparation, during which the native residues promoted PVDF dehydrofluorination and were partially consumed. The resulting LiF/polymer co‐modified LLZTO powders (LLZTO‐LP) show improved air stability and slurry processability and can be uniformly coated onto polyethylene separator to form a PE@LLZTO‐LP composite separator. As a result, Li|PE@LLZTO‐LP|Li symmetric cells maintain stable cycling for over 1100 h at 1 mA cm−2 with a fixed capacity of 1 mAh cm−2, and NCM811|PE@LLZTO‐LP|Li cells retain a high‐capacity retention of 80.0% after 425 cycles at 0.5 C. This surface‐reconstruction method provides a potential strategy for preparing LLZTO‐based composite separators for lithium‐metal batteries.

title: Ultrafast Laser Synthesis of Titanium Silicalite‐1 Zeolite: Titanium Substitution Behavior
content:
Ultrafast laser method offers a novel approach for material synthesis where laser induced cyclic flows accelerate the reactions. The undesired phase formation during heteroatom substitution has been suppressed due to far‐from equilibrium conditions, while volume expansion of the synthesis method has been shown through double microreactor configurations. This methodology provides a robust platform for engineering heteroatom‐substituted materials.








ABSTRACT
Controlling heteroatom substitution while suppressing undesired secondary phases remains a fundamental challenge in zeolite synthesis. Here we show that ultrafast laser driven far‐from‐equilibrium microreactors provide a fundamentally different pathway for heteroatom substitution compared to conventional near equilibrium hydrothermal synthesis. Titanium Silicalite‐1 (TS‐1) zeolite is a model system to investigate volume upgrade potential of the ultrafast laser synthesis method because titanium substitution is highly sensitive to synthesis dynamics. The substitution process in TS‐1 case is strictly limited to ∼2.5% due to rigorous framework structure of zeolite and exceeding this limit causes the excess titanium to accumulate in pore openings and external surface, eventually degrading catalytic activity. Comprehensive analyses (XAFS, UV‐Raman, UV‐Vis) reveal that the dynamic synthesis environment of ultrafast laser effectively prevents anatase accumulation. The laser induced flows and far‐from equilibrium conditions facilitate the kinetic trapping of excess titanium in the form of intermediate species within the liquid phase. Furthermore, the double laser beam configuration enables irradiation of more reaction volume without compromising crystallinity, particle uniformity, or titanium substitution quality. The pathway offers control over heteroatom incorporation while suppressing undesired phase formation in TS‐1 zeolites.

title: Tuning Alkyl Chain Length of Sulfonate Additives to Balance Solvation/Interfacial Chemistry for Highly Stable Aqueous Zinc Batteries
content:
The sodium butanesulfonate (C4) additive simultaneously coordinate with Zn2+ in the solvation shell and achieve sufficient interfacial adsorption on Zn anodes, resulting in accelerated desolvation of Zn2+, suppression of water‐induced side reactions, and uniform zinc deposition. The medium‐chain C4 overcomes the limitations of additives with short and long alkyl chains.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous zinc batteries are promising for grid‐scale energy storage but are plagued by sluggish desolvation kinetics and water‐induced parasitic reactions. However, additives with short chains are adept at solvation tuning but offer limited interfacial protection, whereas those with long chains offer hydrophobic protection but hinder ion transport. Herein, we systematically vary the alkyl chain length of sodium sulfonates to elucidate how chain length balances Zn2+ solvation and interfacial chemistry. The medium‐chain sodium butanesulfonate (C4) additive overcomes the limitations of additives with short and long alkyl chains. C4 weakly coordinates with Zn2+ to modulate solvation, and its sufficient interfacial adsorption constructs a water‐depleted electric double layer to suppress side reactions. Finally, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell with the designed electrolyte achieves an ultra‐long cycle life of 3500 h under conditions of 0.5 mA cm–2/0.25 mAh cm−2, and the Zn||Cu asymmetric cell achieves a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 1800 cycles (3 mA cm−2/1 mAh cm−2). This work indicates that alkyl chain length is a key parameter governing solvation and interfacial chemistry regulation, offering guidance for electrolyte design in aqueous zinc‐ion batteries.

title: Arbitrary Reconfigurable Light‐Responsive Surface Topographies in Liquid Crystal Elastomer Films Using a Digital Micromirror Device
content:
Digital micromirror device (DMD)‐based photo‐imprinting is employed as a maskless technique for creating dynamic and reconfigurable surface topographies in light‐responsive liquid crystal elastomers. Beyond replacing conventional photomasks, this approach enables rapid, software‐controlled, and cost‐effective fabrication with high spatiotemporal precision. The resulting programmable, light‐responsive surface patterns offer potential for applications in optics, soft robotics, microfluidics, and biomedical systems.








ABSTRACT
Arbitrary reconfigurable light‐responsive topographies enable repeated programming of surfaces with light, enabling applications in optics, biotechnology, microfluidics, and soft robotics. However, achieving such adaptive surfaces remains challenging. Here, we introduce digital micromirror device (DMD)‐based photo imprinting as a rapid, maskless technique for generating dynamic surface topographies in light‐responsive liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) films. The resulting surfaces exhibit reversible height modulations up to sub micrometers with lateral feature sizes down to 12.5 µm, and can be written, erased, and re‐written in arbitrary geometries. Additionally, preconfigured imprinted surface topographies are created via DMD‐directed polymerization, inducing spatial variations in crosslinking density throughout the LCE film. These fixed regions enable reversible, light‐driven formation and removal of surface topographies with (sub)micrometer resolutions. Combining these approaches allows permanent DMD imprinting of surface topographies that can be selectively addressed, generating complex topographies with tunable heights in a contact‐free manner, thereby enabling hierarchical, multilevel surface architectures through the integration of permanent and dynamically reconfigurable features. This establishes DMD as a versatile platform for arbitrary, reconfigurable light‐driven surface patterning with potential for high‐speed, high‐resolution, and reversible patterning, overcoming key limitations of conventional photomask imprinting by enabling smaller and more precise feature formation.

title: Precise Measurement of Piezoelectric Response With Interferometric Piezoresponse Force Microscopy
content:
A robust interferometric displacement sensor‐based piezoresponse force microscopy (IDS‐PFM) measurement strategy is presented. This strategy combines surface‐potential compensation with precise on‐tip laser alignment, which minimizes electrostatic artifacts and enables reliable quantitative piezoelectric characterization. Consistent results are obtained across different probe stiffnesses, loading forces, and scan angles, validating the robustness and reliability of this method.








ABSTRACT
Quantitative measurements of piezoelectric response using piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) are often compromised by non‐piezoelectric contributions, particularly electrostatic interactions. Interferometric displacement sensor (IDS)‐based PFM can directly measure tip displacement and thereby suppress many of these artifacts. However, accurate determination of the piezoelectric response remains highly sensitive to measurement conditions. Here, the combined effects of laser‐spot position, surface‐potential compensation, and cantilever stiffness on the measured vertical effective piezoelectric coefficient deff are systematically evaluated. Precise on‐tip alignment of the IDS laser spot is shown to be a prerequisite for capturing the true tip displacement. Only when this condition is met and the local surface potential is properly compensated, does the piezoresponse amplitude between oppositely polarized domains converge across all tested conditions. Soft cantilevers are more susceptible to electrostatic artifacts than stiff cantilevers. A three‐step protocol for quantitative IDS‐PFM measurements is established, providing a framework for the metrology of emerging electromechanical materials.

Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11339-0

Reconstruction of radiative forcing resulting from worldwide peatland drainage over the past two centuries reveals a persistent net warming effect caused by the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions over that of avoided CH4 emissions.

content:

Architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer drive cell state diversification through mechanochemical reprogramming of stem cell identities.

title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
content:
Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11315-8

In flies, sugar-sensing enteric neurons activate brain neurons that inhibit crop duct motor neurons, relaxing the foregut muscles to facilitate food transfer to the crop, which sustains ingestion and regulates food intake.
journal: Nature

title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
content:
Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11353-2

Quantum confocal microscopy enables deterministic preparation of high-photon-number Fock-like states with up to 500 photons, reducing photon-number variance by 21.5 dB and achieving record displacement-sensing precision 19.2 dB beyond the standard quantum limit.

title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
content:

title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
content:
Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11341-6

Dental morphology and proteomic analyses of fossils from southern China identify lineages with and without Denisovan affinity, indicating the diversity of hominin populations in this region in the Middle to Late Pleistocene.

title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
content:
Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11313-w

content:

title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
content:

Integrated photonics could overcome key size, power and performance trade-offs in augmented-reality glasses, enabling compact, efficient displays while opening opportunities across quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

content:

content:
Nature, Published online: 25 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11354-1

Climate change and natural disturbances are key drivers of tree abundance dynamics: warming tends to shift tree abundance upslope whereas major disturbances, such as wildfires and insect outbreaks, tend to shift it downslope, creating opposing pressures on tree species’ elevational redistribution.

title:
Photoinduced
Eosin Y Self-Disproportionation Enables
Reactivity beyond Direct Excited-State Electron Transfer
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Photoredox catalysis is commonly governed by the redox properties of the initially excited photocatalyst, which can limit the activation of difficult-to-oxidize alkenes. Here, we identify photoinduced self-disproportionation of neutral eosin Y (EH2) as an alternative activation pathway. In fluorinated-alcohol media, specific hydrogen-bonding interactions stabilize a minor population of the visible-light-absorbing EH2_acid tautomer. Following excitation and intersystem crossing, triplet EH2 undergoes intermolecular hydrogen-atom transfer with ground-state EH2 to generate the complementary radicals EH• and EH3•. Time-resolved spectroscopy shows that the alkene substrate does not measurably intercept excited EH2 but instead reacts with the secondary radical EH•, thereby separating photon absorption from substrate activation. Fluorinated alcohols further couple this radical-pair chemistry to productive C–C bond formation, as illustrated by highly selective polyene cyclizations. These findings establish photocatalyst self-disproportionation as a distinct mechanistic pathway that generates secondary reactive species whose reactivity is not accessible via direct excited-state electron transfer.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Cross-Linked
Halide Networks for Lithium Superionic
Conduction
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) hold great promise for next-generation energy storage owing to their high safety and energy density, yet their performance critically depends on solid electrolytes (SEs) with high ionic conductivity and structural robustness. Mixed-anion chemistry, exemplified by the Cl/O system, has emerged as an effective approach for designing halide-based superionic conductors, where partial oxygen incorporation distorts the regular halide framework and enhances Li+ mobility. However, we herein show that uncontrolled oxygen incorporation is prone to generate nonbridging oxygens (NBOs), which can hinder Li+ migration via Coulombic interactions. To address this, we develop a polyanion-assisted cross-linking strategy that promotes more bridging-oxygen (BOs) coordination and less formation of NBOs. This yields a highly disordered, frustrated energy landscape conducive to efficient Li+ percolation and rapid ion migration. As an example, PO43– polyanion cross-linked ZrClx halide networks (ZrCl4-xLi3PO4) are developed and exhibit ionic conductivities up to 2.8 × 10–3 S cm–1 at 30 °C, competitive with state-of-the-art rare-metal halides, while maintaining &gt;10–3 S cm–1 after humid exposure (5% RH, 12 h). ASSBs incorporating these electrolytes demonstrate stable cycling not only under elevated temperatures (55 °C) but also under high voltages (4.6 V). These findings identify NBO environments as potential transport inhibitors and establish inorganic cross-linking topochemistry as a structural design principle for robust, high-performance, halide solid electrolytes.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Large 77Se NMR Signal Enhancements in Solutions
by Overhauser Dynamic Nuclear Polarization at 9.4 T for Real-Time
Reaction Monitoring
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>77Se nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) is a key method to probe selenium functional centers in biology and materials science, yet its practical application is severely hindered by its intrinsically low sensitivity due to the low gyromagnetic ratio (19% of 1H) and natural abundance (7.6%). Overhauser effect dynamic nuclear polarization (OE-DNP) has recently emerged as a promising method for generating steady-state signal enhancement in high-field liquid NMR at room temperature. However, its application to 77Se has remained unexplored to date. Here, we present liquid-state OE-DNP as a route for 77Se NMR. At 9.4 T, we report 102 to 103 fold signal enhancements for organoselenium compounds, including the drug candidate ebselen, with polarization buildup within seconds. The large enhancements are the result of efficient electron-to-nuclear polarization transfer with OE-DNP coupling factors of ≳|0.4|, the highest reported so far at high magnetic fields (≥3 T) for NMR-active nuclei. The replenishable signal enhancements allow reaction monitoring by NMR on timescales longer than nuclear T1. As a proof of concept, we monitor a diselenide metathesis reaction over 48 h, capturing species evolution for kinetic studies. This effect can be further expanded to the heavier chalcogen, tellurium, as demonstrated by 123Te OE-DNP with similar efficiency.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Micelle-Driven MOF
Degradation for Enhanced Cargo
Release in Micromotors
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are widely explored as cargo-delivery platforms, yet efficient release of the encapsulated cargo remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that anionic surfactant micelles actively destabilize the HKUST-1 MOF framework through Cu2+ extraction, converting a typically undesired degradation process into a mechanism for enhanced cargo release. Complementary mechanistic studies reveal that this process depends on surfactant self-assembly and on the accessibility and coordination environment of the metal nodes. The resulting framework destabilization greatly enhances the release of different cargos from HKUST-1. This mechanistic concept is subsequently translated into tubular MOF-based micromotors by confining SDS within an agarose matrix inside the micromotor cavity. Local surfactant release generates a micelle-rich microenvironment that promotes MOF degradation and cargo release while limiting bulk surfactant exposure and reducing the cytotoxic effects associated with free surfactant under the tested conditions. The resulting platform integrates micelle-mediated MOF disassembly with spatially confined micromotor delivery, providing a strategy for localized and enhanced cargo release from MOF-based dynamic systems.</jats:p>

Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Subambient Synthesis
of Freestanding Monolayer Cubic
ZrO2 Crystals with High Dielectric Permittivity
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Two-dimensional (2D) polymorphic materials offer access to unconventional crystal structures that trigger exotic properties and functionalities beyond equilibrium phases. However, extending this opportunity to metal oxides remains highly challenging because both thickness reduction and phase transformation involve large energy barriers in such strongly bonded ionic structures. Here we report an atomic-freezing conversion strategy that kinetically stabilizes freestanding 2D metastable oxide crystals under subambient conditions. Single-crystalline cubic ZrO2 of monolayer thickness is produced and stabilized below room temperature, although this phase is typically stable only at temperatures above 2000 °C in bulk. Structural analysis reveals that the layered ZrNCl precursor contains a Zr atomic framework that matches the (111) planes of cubic ZrO2. During conversion, suppressed atomic motion under low temperatures and 2D confinement preserves the nonequilibrium cubic structure. The resulting 2D cubic ZrO2 exhibits a high dielectric permittivity of ∼23.5 and enables MoS2 field-effect transistors with an on/off ratio of ∼108 and a subthreshold slope as low as 63.5 mV dec–1. This approach also applies to cubic HfO2 and tetragonal Bi2O3, providing a general kinetic route to bypass thermodynamic phase constraints and expanding access to metastable oxides in the 2D limit.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
A Bowl-Shaped B,N-Tetraquinane
Organic Super-Reductant
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Developing a stable molecular reductant with exceptionally strong reducing power remains highly challenging. In this work, we synthesized and characterized a bowl-shaped B–N tetraquinane in a single high-yield step. Cyclic voltammetry reveals a reduction potential of −3.2 V vs Fc/Fc+, a new record among organic reductants. This super-reductant enables [3 + 2] cycloadditions with ketones and imines, dearomatization of phthalazine, cleavage of strong C–Si bonds, direct reduction–borylation of fluorobenzene, deoxygenative coupling of nitrosobenzene, and ring-opening C–C coupling of aromatics into polyenes. Computational studies support its synthetic pathway, ring strain, high reactivity, and remarkably negative reduction potential. These findings demonstrate how three-dimensional topological strain can transform a boron-based dianion into a powerful reagent for reductive reactions and demanding bond activations.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Dynamic Li+/Na+-Exchanging
Interphase Stabilizes High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathodes for 557 Wh kg–1 Lithium Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>High-voltage operation of Ni-rich layered cathodes LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) accelerates electrolyte decomposition at the surface and destabilizes the bulk lattice with oxygen loss. Conventional strategies for regulating the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) commonly suppress persistent parasitic reactions at Ni-rich cathode surfaces, but increase interfacial polarization and offer limited protection against structural degradation in the bulk. Here, a dynamic interphase is constructed by coating NCM811 with a Na+-based solid-electrolyte Na3Zr2Si2PO12 (NZSP). During cycling, Li+/Na+ exchange transforms the NZSP layer into a fast Li+ conducting interphase LixNa3–xZr2Si2PO12 (L-NZSP), while the Na+ ions are incorporated into the NCM811 lattice. The L-NZSP suppresses parasitic reactions at high charging voltages. Meanwhile, the incorporated Na+ ions provide pillar-like support for the layered framework, stabilizing the oxygen lattice and mitigating chemo-mechanical degradation. Consequently, the modified cathode retains 80% capacity after 511 cycles at 4.7 V and enables a 4 Ah pouch cell to deliver 557 Wh kg–1 with 80.5% retention over 118 cycles. This work demonstrates Li+/Na+-exchanging interphase as an effective strategy to couple interfacial protection with bulk lattice reinforcement for high-voltage Ni-rich cathodes in high-energy lithium batteries.</jats:p>

Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Local
Molecular Motions Encode Time-Resolved Infrared
Spectra of Proteins
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy probes protein dynamics over time scales spanning more than 10 orders of magnitude, yet the molecular motions underlying the observed kinetic signatures have remained elusive. Here we combine transient infrared spectroscopy with nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations to establish a direct connection between experimental relaxation times and local structural motions. Studying single-domain allosteric proteins, we find that inter-residue contact distances provide the structural representation that most faithfully reproduces the experimental dynamics. Correlation analysis identifies localized networks of coordinated contacts that mediate long-range coupling between secondary-structure elements. The characteristic time scales of these contact networks quantitatively match the experimentally observed relaxation processes, enabling each kinetic step to be assigned to a specific molecular motion. Applied to allosteric signal propagation in PDZ3 and photoinduced perturbation of the binding pocket of PDZ2 or a ligand binding to PDZ2, this framework provides an atomistic picture of hierarchical protein relaxation and establishes a general framework for connecting transient infrared spectroscopy with the molecular mechanisms of protein dynamics.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Asymmetric
Partial Hydrogenation of Quinazolines:
Overcoming Catalyst Poisoning by a Robust yet Active Solo-Coordination-Vacant
Ir(III) Pincer Catalyst
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Catalytic asymmetric partial hydrogenation of quinazolines to afford enantioenriched 3,4-dihydroquinazolines, a privileged scaffold in medicinal chemistry, is a long-standing challenge likely due to product-induced catalyst deactivation. Here, we report a robust yet highly reactive solo-coordination-vacant Ir(III) pincer catalyst being capable of overcoming this poisoning challenge. This catalyst enables the asymmetric partial hydrogenation of a broad range of quinazolines, affording 3,4-dihydroquinazolines in high yields (up to 98%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). In a dedicated catalyst-loading study, the loading could be reduced to 0.001 mol % (10 ppm, TON = 38,000). Mechanistic investigations, including NMR spectroscopic detection of a key Ir–H intermediate and base-dependence studies, support a catalytic cycle proceeding through a well-defined Ir(III)-hydride species and suggest that an alkali-metal-assisted pathway is unlikely to be dominant.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Negative-Charge-Transfer
Ligand Holes Enhance Ferromagnetism
and Topological Transport in van der Waals Magnets
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Many prototypical 3d van der Waals (vdW) magnets contain heavy ligands with closed p shells, whose strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC) influences the magnetism only indirectly through p–d hybridization. Here we show that negative charge transfer (NCT) creates spin-polarized, SOC-active holes in the ligand p states bordering the vdW gap, coupling magnetic exchange and topological transport within the same states. First-principles calculations identify the synthesized MnSiTe3 as an NCT d5L ferromagnet comprising high-spin Mn2+ and one formal Te 5p ligand hole per f.u. The Te-derived holes strengthen both intralayer and, in particular, interlayer ferromagnetic exchange, favoring ferromagnetic over antiferromagnetic interlayer order by a surprisingly large 84.1 meV/f.u. SOC within the partially occupied Te 5p manifold produces an easy-plane magnetocrystalline anisotropy of 3.6 meV/f.u. The resulting simulated Curie temperature reaches 464 K. The SOC-active Te 5p holes further generate multiple Weyl points, yielding a calculated intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity of 760 Ω–1 cm–1 that remains large over a broad energy window around the Fermi level. All those results stand in sharp contrast to ligand-shell-closed vdW magnets. This NCT ligand-hole picture and the resulting magnetic and transport responses also extend to the synthesized MnGeTe3 and the predicted iodides Cr0.5Mn0.5I3 and MnI3. These results establish NCT as a chemical strategy that makes the vdW interface magnetically and topologically active. Substituting later 3d metals or heavier p ligands into existing vdW magnets drives them toward the NCT regime, providing a design principle for the discovery of new NCT candidates.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
A Cu-Modified Layered
Thiostannate for Selective Pb
Capture from Strongly Acidic Media
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Layered metal sulfide ion exchangers are powerful platforms for soft-metal capture, but their application in strongly acidic environments requires framework stability while preserving accessible ion-exchange pathways. Here, we introduce a new series of Cu-modified SnS2-derived layered chalcogenides, AMS-8 (A = Na, K, Rb, Cs), featuring labile interlayer alkali metal ions. NMS-8 (Na1.13Cu1.32Sn3.34S8·xH2O) demonstrates that Cu+ can be incorporated into the SnS2-derived AMS layered motif without disrupting the fundamental architecture. Upon acid exposure, NMS-8 undergoes Na+/H+ exchange and interlayer contraction, showing low Sn leaching in 6 M H2SO4 but substantial Sn dissolution in 6 M HCl after prolonged exposure, despite persistent powder X-ray diffraction reflections of the layered phase. NMS-8 can rapidly capture Pb2+ from water, achieving near-complete removal within 20 s under dilute conditions, a Sips-fitted capacity of 178.2 ± 12.4 mg g–1 (regression standard error), and high selectivity against common competing cations. Structural characterization supports preservation of the lamellar network and a proposed structural model featuring Cu+ displaced off-center within a distorted octahedral framework environment. In an acid mine drainage simulant, NMS-8 selectively removes Pb, Cd, and Cu under acidic multicomponent conditions while retaining its layered structure. Local structural characterization of NMS-8@Pb reveals a spatially heterogeneous Pb distribution within individual crystallites that is not appropriately described by a simple homogeneous interlayer exchange model and is consistent with local structural reorganization during Pb2+ uptake. These results highlight Cu-modified layered thiostannates as promising platforms for rapid, selective soft-metal capture, with substantial resistance to concentrated sulfuric acid and Pb retention dependent on the leaching medium.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Bioinspired Ångström-Scale
Coupling of
Reductive Centers in Covalent Organic Frameworks Drives Efficient
Photocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The photocatalytic oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is crucial for solar-to-chemical energy conversion but faces challenges from weak oxygen adsorption and slow kinetics. Inspired by the spatially cooperative multimetal centers in natural enzymes, we develop a strategy of Å-scale spatial coupling of reductive centers in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Ortho-amino-functionalized COFs were constructed with catalytic pockets that position multiple acceptors within subnanometer proximity, creating coupled reductive centers for cooperative O2 adsorption and multielectron relay. The optimal framework, with a model-derived separation of approximately 3.3 Å between reductive centers, achieves a hydrogen peroxide production rate of 4.10 mmol g–1 h–1 in pure water under visible light without sacrificial agents, along with a high apparent quantum yield of 19.2% at 450 nm. Practical viability is confirmed through operation in diverse water sources and continuous-flow systems. Moreover, the enhanced ORR activity accelerates oxidative coupling of benzylamine derivatives, showing over 80% conversion for 12 analogues. Experimental and theoretical analyses indicate that the confined neighboring sites enhance O2 adsorption and activation, stabilize •OOH intermediates, and promote the two-electron reduction pathway. This work establishes convergent multicenter coupling as a foundational design principle, unlocking new avenues for the rational creation of high-performance photocatalysts in sustainable chemistry.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
In Situ High-Pressure
NMR Reveals Pressure-Defect
Generation in Aluminum Acetylacetonate toward Integrated Optical Response
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Stimuli-responsive luminescent materials featuring real-time pressure-response with persistent memory effects hold considerable promise for advanced photonic computing. However, most pressure-memory behavior depends on triggered irreversible phase transitions, which hinders the integration of reversible optical sensing. Synergistic pressure treatment and defect generation serve as an effective approach that ensures the phase-transition-free structure while affording excellent photoluminescence (PL) performance. In this work, we employ pressure-defect generation strategy in aluminum acetylacetonate that effectively integrates short-term pressure response with long-term history memory. Notably, the PL wavelength acts as a digital readout across 476–486 nm, alongside an intensity-based analog signal below 4 GPa. Upon crossing this threshold, the response further embeds memory states dependent on pressure history. In situ high-pressure nuclear magnetic resonance (HP-NMR) measurements reveal, from both static and dynamic perspectives, the progressive deepening of pressure-induced local responses within the molecular framework, from ligand-associated modulation to Al–O coordination perturbation. This establishes a two-regime pressure-defect generation pathway: reversible structural distortion induces electronic-state defects, whereas partially trapped severe distortion may generate radical defects. Our work not only highlights the unique capability of local dynamic probing for the design of pressure-responsive materials, but also broadens the horizons of single-material multifunctional information-processing systems.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Cation Pinning toward
High-Concentration Formic Acid
Fuel Cells
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Despite the high theoretical energy density of concentrated formic acid, direct formic acid fuel cells (DFAFCs) incorporating conventional nanoparticle or emerging single-atom anodes exhibit a precipitous power loss as fuel concentration scales. While CO poisoning is traditionally blamed, we show that this limitation is governed by interfacial acid–base kinetics. By implementing a cation-pinning strategy via rare-earth oxide-modified Rh single-atom sites, we stabilize OH– from water dissociation through interfacial ionic anchoring to trigger localized pH inversion. This modulation leads to the preferential enrichment of interfacial formate, identified here as the primary reactive species. Consequently, Dy2O3–Rh/NC delivers a mass activity 641-fold higher than that of nanoparticle benchmarks. The resulting anode achieves an exceptional peak power density of 375 mW cm–2, surpassing commercial Pd/C across all concentrations. This work establishes precision ionic management as a versatile approach to breaking performance limits in multiphase catalysis.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Ligand-Controlled Chemodivergent
β-Methylene
C(sp3)–H Heteroarylation of Aliphatic Acids
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Achieving ligand-controlled chemodivergence in C–H activation is still difficult because several competing reaction pathways are available when multiple C–H bonds are present. We describe a Pd(II)-catalyzed, chemodivergent β-methylene C(sp3)–H heteroarylation of free aliphatic acids in which two distinct classes of bidentate pyridone ligands each deliver a different product. These two ligands also overcome a long-standing inhibitory effect of heteroaryl iodides, demonstrating the potential of this protocol to serve as a general C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling method using readily available aliphatic acids as the alkylating partner. Mechanistic experiments and DFT analyses reveal that π–π stacking between the quinoline motif and the heteroaryl ring lowers the barrier for rotation of the carbon–palladium bond, favoring protodepalladation to the reductive Heck product, whereas the oxime ether ligand lacks this interaction and steers the key intermediate toward β-H elimination to give the oxidative Heck product.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Immobilizing Ionomers
by Strong Hydrogen Bonds for
Highly Stable Industrial Water Electrolysis at 3.0 A/cm2
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Raising the operating current density can effectively reduce the high cost of proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), but this approach is limited by rapid electrode degradation. Our previous research identified a critical degradation mechanism in which ionomer migration blocks mass-transport channels in the anode catalyst layer (ACL). Here, we find that each sulfonate group of the ionomer forms only about half a hydrogen bond on the IrO2 surface, indicating a weak catalyst–ionomer interaction. Rather than modifying the IrO2 surface, we propose to introduce additives that provide additional adsorption sites forming stronger hydrogen bonds (SHB) with the sulfonate groups. The resulting SHB-ACL maintains a stable ionomer distribution and pore network even after aging, and exhibits a roughly four fold lower degradation rate over 2500 h at 3.0 A/cm2. Furthermore, the electrode can be readily scaled up to 600 cm2. The improvement stability is at least in part attributable to enhanced interface interaction, although preserved porosity, water/gas transport, and interparticle contacts may also contribute. These findings offer a scalable route toward durable industrial PEMWE devices.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Single-Atom
Catalysts for Biomass Valorization
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Biomass, the only renewable organic carbon resource on Earth, offers a promising feedstock for producing value-added chemicals and fuels. However, the principal challenge in biomass valorization stems from the inherent complexity of its functional groups, necessitating catalysts capable of precisely activating specific C–O/C═O/C═C bonds while suppressing undesired side reactions. Single-atom catalysts (SACs), featuring unique geometric and electronic structures as well as high atomic utilization efficiency, have shown potential for highly effective biomass conversion in thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. Drawing upon recent continuous efforts on SACs in biomass valorization, we provide a comprehensive overview of recent advances in applying SACs to the transformation of main components of lignocellulosic biomass and their platform molecules. Structure–activity relationships and catalytic behavior of SACs under different external stimuli (e.g., thermal, electrical, and photonic) are emphasized, showcasing their innovative applications. The important factors governing catalytic activity and selectivity with a particular focus on the geometric and electronic structures of active sites are discussed, aiming to derive fundamental principles for the rational design of efficient and selective catalysts for biomass valorization. Finally, an outlook highlights the key challenges and prospects in this flourishing field.</jats:p>
journal: Chemical Reviews

title:
Nanotechnology
Meets Brain Diseases: Emerging Therapeutic
Strategies for Drug Delivery
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Brain diseases, encompassing neurodegenerative disorders, cerebrovascular diseases, and brain tumors, impose a profound global health burden. Conventional therapeutic strategies often fail due to the formidable blood–brain barrier (BBB) and complex pathological microenvironment of the central nervous system (CNS). The rapid evolution of nanotechnology offers unprecedented opportunities to overcome these delivery hurdles. This review comprehensively summarizes recent developments in engineered nanoplatforms for the diagnosis and targeted therapy of brain diseases. It first outlines the pathological characteristics and nanoprobe-enhanced diagnostic methods for various brain disorders, followed by a critical evaluation of five major classes of nanocarriers for CNS drug delivery: lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, bio-derived, and hybrid nanocarriers. This evaluation highlights their structural attributes and delivery efficiencies. The discussion then examines advanced strategies to improve delivery precision, including multilevel targeting (e.g., BBB penetration and specific cell targeting), stimuli-responsive theranostics, and functional surface modifications. Linking these nanotechnological innovations to specific neurological diseases highlights their clinical potential. Finally, the review addresses current translational challenges, including biosafety, scalable manufacturing, and interindividual variability, and offers a forward-looking perspective on the rational design of next-generation precision neuro-nanomedicines.</jats:p>
