title:
Single-Molecule
DNA Sequencing with Nanopores
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>DNA sequencing is indispensable in healthcare, agriculture, environmental protection, and understanding of biology. DNA sequencing with nanopores uses a unique principle where individual DNA strands are threaded through a ring-like nanopore, which acts as a read head to electronically detect the bases. Due to the simple principle, nanopores enable sequencing at previously unachieved speeds and read lengths as well as direct sensing of epigenetically modified bases. The electrical nature also allows highly portable devices to be used in the clinic or the field. This review places DNA nanopore sequencing within the context of other DNA sequencing technologies and explains its functional principle and the essential components of commercial nanopore sequencing platforms. The advantages of nanopore sequencing are demonstrated with relevant case studies, and nanopore sequencing is compared to other technologies in terms of sequencing parameters such as read length, throughput, cost per base, and accuracy. A brief outlook discusses how the current shortcomings of nanopore sequencing can be addressed with future advances.</jats:p>
journal: Chemical Reviews

title:
Advances in Synthetic Methodologies for Isotopic Labeling
of Organic Molecules
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Radioactive and stable isotopes are essential tools in the discovery and development of new agrochemical and pharmaceutical molecules. Consequently, the body of research focused on developing novel synthetic methodologies for isotope incorporation into bioactive molecules continues to grow. Progress in this field has largely been driven by innovative catalytic methods, including late-stage functionalization (LSF) methods like hydrogen isotope exchange (HIE), carbon isotope exchange (CIE), molecular skeletal editing, biocatalysis, and other labeling approaches. These methods enable efficient and sustainable site-specific introduction of isotopes into bioactive molecules at late stages of synthesis. Given the broad applications across various scientific fields, this comprehensive, critical, and accessible review summarizing diverse isotope labeling methodologies will be of great benefit to researchers in academia as well as professionals in the pharmaceutical and agrochemical industries. This review focuses primarily on recent developments in catalytic methodologies for incorporating 2H, 3H, 11C, 13C, 14C, 15N, 18O, 18F, and 34S isotopes into organic molecules, along with a brief overview of well-established methods reported in this field.</jats:p>
journal: Chemical Reviews

title: Cathode-Generated Hydrogen Peroxide Contributes to Degradation of the Membrane Across Its Full Thickness in PEM Water Electrolyzers
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Proton-exchange membrane (PEM) water electrolyzers must operate for 80,000 h, and membrane degradation limits this lifetime. Because electroosmotic drag carries degradation products toward the cathode, the fluoride emission rate, the standard diagnostic, underrepresents anode-side and bulk degradation. It also misses larger fluorocarbon fragments (LC-MS); after correction for compression, about 80% of the excess measured thinning (SEM) over fluoride-derived thinning at 1 A cm−2 is chemical loss. Depth profiles at both membrane faces in time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry, with transport analysis, indicate anisotropic degradation across the full PEM thickness, consistent with cathode-generated hydrogen peroxide diffusing toward the anode, most strongly at 0.5–1.0 A cm−2. The estimated peroxide production rate is six times the molar rate of membrane loss. To reach 80,000 h, our results point to two design targets: oxygen crossover an order of magnitude below today's 1% benchmark, and peroxide-decomposition catalysts distributed throughout the membrane bulk.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title: Localized High-Concentration Electrolyte with Nonfluorinated Diluent for Wide-Temperature Sodium-Ion Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Localized high-concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) have been extensively investigated to improve rechargeable battery performance, yet most rely on costly fluorinated diluents. Herein, we develop a 1M LHCE using toluene as nonfluorinated and low-cost diluent for wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). The 1M LHCE features a compressed solvation structure and preserved ion-transport pathways, enabling the antimonene alloy anode to deliver stable capacities of 555.2 mAh g–1 over 600 cycles at 25 °C and 573.2 and 512.3 mAh g–1 at 50 and –20 °C, respectively. Na3V2(PO4)3//antimonene full cells further demonstrate stable operation under 50 and –20 °C. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the 1M LHCE forms an adaptive solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that dynamically regulates composition and thickness, which becomes thicker and more organic-rich after sodiation but thinner and more inorganic-rich after desodiation. Such “breathable” SEI effectively accommodates large volume changes and ensures efficient Na+ transport. This work provides a rational electrolyte design strategy for wide-temperature SIBs.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Energy Letters

title:
Ligand Engineering
of Atomically Precise Au2Cu6 Nanoclusters for
Concurrent Control of Spin Conversion
and Triplet Energy Transfer
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ligand engineering offers a molecularly precise strategy for controlling excited-state processes in atomically precise metal nanoclusters (NCs), yet simultaneous regulation of intracluster spin conversion and intermolecular triplet energy transfer (TET) remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate such concurrent regulation in Au2Cu6(S-Adm)6(PR3)2 (Au2Cu6R; S-Adm = 1-adamantanethiolate) NCs by replacing aromatic triphenylphosphine (PPh3) with aliphatic trialkylphosphines, tri-n-octylphosphine (P(Oct)3) or tris(2-methoxycarbonylethyl)phosphine (P(MCE)3). This substitution switches phosphorescence-dominant Au2Cu6Ph to TADF-dominant Au2Cu6Oct and Au2Cu6MCE, with photoluminescence quantum yields of up to 88% in fluid solution. For Au2Cu6Oct, experimentally determined ISC/RISC kinetics yield a small effective singlet–triplet free-energy offset, ΔGST = 14 meV, consistent with efficient reversible spin conversion. Concurrently, the donor triplet energy increases by 0.10 eV, while the limiting TET rate constant (kmax) increases by ∼19-fold, consistent with enhanced short-range donor–acceptor accessibility for Dexter-type TET. Together, these effects accelerate TET to 9,10-diphenylanthracene (DPA) by more than 240-fold relative to Au2Cu6Ph. This simultaneous optimization of spin conversion and TET enables red-to-blue triplet–triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC) with a quantum yield of 13.0% in deaerated solution (23.5% after reabsorption correction on the 50% maximum basis) and 7.5% green-to-blue TTA-UC under ambient air in a room-temperature viscous DPA matrix. Spectroscopic, kinetic, structural, and electronic-state analyses support a second-order spin-vibronic mechanism in which strongly spin–orbit-coupled higher triplet states enhance the effective S1–T1 interaction through vibronic mixing within a ligand-dependent nuclear-coordinate landscape. These results establish peripheral-ligand engineering as a strategy for concurrent regulation of intracluster spin conversion and intermolecular triplet sensitization in atomically precise metal NCs.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Programmed Metal-Ion
Reconstruction of Small-Molecule
Nanoassemblies for Thermoresponsive Hydrogel-Mediated Photothermal
Antibacterial and Immunoregulatory Wound Repair
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>MRSA-infected wound repair remains challenging because persistent bacterial colonization, oxidative stress, and dysregulated inflammation mutually reinforce each other within the wound microenvironment. Although multifunctional hydrogels have been widely explored for infected wound management, many systems still rely on the physical combination of independently functioning components, limiting structural integration, and functional coupling. Here, we report a programmed metal-ion reconstruction strategy in which chlorogenic acid (CGA) and glycyrrhizic acid (GA) were first assembled under Ag+ mediation to form Ag-containing nanoassemblies (AGC), followed by stepwise Fe3+ coordination to generate reconstructed Ag/Fe-integrated nanoassemblies (AGCF). This reconstruction altered the local coordination environment and enhanced near-infrared responsiveness and photothermal conversion while retaining the ROS-regulating activity. Incorporation of AGCF into a PNIPAM/PVA network yielded a preformed thermoresponsive hydrogel dressing, P/P@AGCF, exhibiting temperature- and microenvironment-dependent Ag/Fe release. Under 808 nm irradiation, P/P@AGCF markedly enhanced MRSA killing and biofilm disruption while reducing the intracellular ROS accumulation and promoting fibroblast migration. In the MRSA-infected full-thickness wound model, P/P@AGCF reduced bacterial burden, accelerated wound closure, enhanced blood perfusion and angiogenesis, and improved inflammatory resolution, collagen deposition, and tissue remodeling. Proteomic analysis, Western blotting, Nrf2 nuclear translocation analysis, in vivo Nrf2 immunofluorescence, and ML385 inhibition collectively supported an important role of Nrf2/Keap1/HO-1 signaling in the oxidative-stress regulation and immunoregulatory effects of P/P@AGCF, accompanied by attenuation of JAK2/STAT3 inflammatory signaling and macrophage transition toward a reparative phenotype. This work establishes a programmed metal-ion reconstruction strategy for converting natural small-molecule nanoassemblies into structurally integrated hydrogel therapeutics that couple photothermal antibacterial activity with ROS regulation and immunomodulation for MRSA-infected wound healing.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Viscophoretic Nanoparticle
Transport
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Viscosity is a fundamental property of liquids and sets the diffusivity of suspended particles. When viscosity varies in space, diffusivity does too; under isothermal conditions, stochastic thermodynamics predicts a particle drift term v = ∂xD(x) arising from position-dependent viscosity. Here, we impose steep, stable viscosity gradients in a microfluidic channel and directly image nanoparticle motion at the single-particle level using high-resolution microscopy. We find viscous-gradient-driven drift velocities that exceed Stokes–Einstein-based estimates, and we quantify this discrepancy through simultaneous measurements of local diffusivity and drift extracted from the same trajectories. We then illustrate how such controlled gradients enable passive focusing in a phoretic trap that combines viscophoresis with diffusiophoresis. Our measurements provide a quantitative single-particle characterization of viscous-gradient-driven transport that is of importance in any system and any application exhibiting viscosity gradients, from membrane separation processes to inter- and intracellular biomolecular transport.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
High-Strength Elastic
Superhydrophobic Composite Aerogels
with Stress-Tunable Broadband Microwave Absorption
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tunable elastic electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorbing materials have attracted considerable attention for coping with multiband interference. However, existing strategies that pursue extreme elasticity through directional freezing often suffer from insufficient mechanical strength and moisture-induced degradation, restricting their utility in load-bearing and extreme-environment applications. Herein, we design a high-strength elastic superhydrophobic composite aerogel, denoted (CF/Ni@CNTs)@SSA, that resolves the high strength-EMW absorbing tunability trade-off through a spatial function-decoupling strategy. A near-zero-shrinkage elastic silica aerogel (SSA) protective layer, which integrates high mechanical strength, thermal insulation, and superhydrophobicity, effectively encapsulates and reinforces an internal multiscale carbon foam-supported nickel@carbon nanotubes (CF/Ni@CNTs) absorbing scaffold, allowing independent optimization of load-bearing and electromagnetic tuning functions. The effective absorption bandwidth shifts continuously from 6.82 to 18.0 GHz under 0% to 40% strain, covering the C, X, and Ku bands with a minimum reflection loss of −71.59 dB. The compressive strength of the composite at 40% strain is 5.26 times that of existing elastic absorbers. In addition, the composite exhibits a superhydrophobic water contact angle of 153.8° and a low thermal conductivity of ∼0.04 W m–1 K–1. This work establishes a design paradigm for multifunctional high-load-bearing EMW absorbers through architectural function decoupling.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Nitrogen–Defect
Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3: From Structural Reconstruction
to Water Oxidation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Earth-abundant ABO3-type perovskite oxides provide a versatile platform for understanding how anion chemistry and defects govern electrocatalytic behavior. Here, we use epitaxial LaFeO3−δNy thin films to reveal how dilute N incorporation (&lt;0.8% N/O) couples to defect formation, structural reconstruction, and water oxidation. Nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition introduces N and is accompanied by reduced oxygen content, localized Fe-metal exsolution, and pronounced lattice expansion, while predominantly preserving Fe3+ in the bulk of the film. Ab initio calculations identify a plausible charge-balanced extended defect configuration involving coupled oxygen and Fe vacancies with substitutional N incorporation, reproducing the experimentally observed lattice expansion while preserving the bulk-average Fe oxidation state. The resulting electronic-state redistribution is accompanied by substantially modified electrical transport and nearly 2 orders of magnitude higher initial oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity than undoped LaFeO3. Under OER conditions, however, the highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface N depletion and Fe0 oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay toward a quasi-steady state. pH-dependent kinetics and post-OER anion redistribution are consistent with possible lattice-oxygen participation. These results establish relationships among dilute anion incorporation, coupled defect reconstruction, electronic properties, and electrochemical behavior in perovskite oxides.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title: pH-Triggered Contractile Dendritic-Cell-Decorated DNA Hydrogel for Efficient In Situ Tumor Cell Restriction and Immune Activation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The extracellular matrix (ECM) and immune system serve as critical barriers against tumor metastasis. However, in the complex tumor microenvironment (TME), the ECM exerts an immunosuppressive effect and its degradation synergistically facilitates tumor metastasis. Simultaneously regulating the ECM structure and eliciting a robust immune response remains a major challenge. Herein, we develop an intelligent DNA hydrogel (CDDTG) embedded with “C”-motif sequences that undergoes acid-triggered contraction via formation of i-motif structures. Upon peritumoral injection, the contracted CDDTG hydrogel can form a dense physical barrier that tightly wraps around tumor spheroids, enabling in situ tumor cell trapping and restriction. Concurrently, the hydrogel releases endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeting tetrahedral DNA (FAL-Td@GOx) loaded with glucose oxidase (GOx). GOx catalyzes glucose oxidation to gluconic acid, further acidifying the TME and reinforcing hydrogel contraction while generating hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) within the ER. This ER-targeted ROS production depletes intracellular glucose, triggers ER stress, and induces immunogenic cell death (ICD) in tumor cells. The resulting ICD promotes exogenous dendritic-cell (DC) activation and amplifies antitumor T-cell responses, thereby reversing immunosuppression. By synergistically combining a mechanically retractable physical barrier with ER stress-driven immunotherapy, CDDTG hydrogel effectively suppresses tumor cell migration and invasion in vitro and potently inhibits lung and bone metastasis in vivo. This work establishes a smart artificial ECM platform that integrates physical cell restriction with immune activation, thereby offering a promising strategy for antimetastatic therapy.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Recognition–Transduction
Coupling in Noble-Metal-Modified
WO3 for Selective BTEX Sensing
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Noble-metal decoration is widely used to enhance gas sensing, yet how modifier identity governs BTEX sensing remains insufficiently understood. Molecular recognition and signal transduction functions are usually modified simultaneously, obscuring their respective contributions to sensing response and selectivity. Here, WO3 nanofibers modified with Au, Pt, or Pd are used to examine how noble-metal identity modulates the coupled receptor and transducer functions across structurally similar BTEX analytes. Au-WO3 combines strong molecular interactions with substantial barrier modulation, enabling efficient conversion of molecular recognition into resistance changes. It enhances all four BTEX responses with calculated lower limit of detection of 15 to 97 ppb. Ethylbenzene adsorption on Au transfers 0.18 e and shifts the Au 5d band center downward by 0.70 eV, therefore Au-WO3 achieves pronounced response of 15.68 to 5 ppm ethylbenzene. Pd-WO3 receives 0.13 to 0.16 e from toluene and p-xylene but modulates the energy barrier by only 0.06 eV, so even strongly adsorbed p-xylene does not yield a correspondingly large response. However, Pt-WO3 shows the opposite imbalance, with the largest energy barrier modulation of 0.50 eV but charge transfer below 0.10 e from every analyte. Therefore, it responds weakly to all BTEX analytes in general. Meanwhile, fingerprints from the sensors identify the four analytes with 97.9% accuracy on unseen replicates and 93.2% when entire concentration groups are withheld. These contrasting regimes indicate that tunable sensitivity and selectivity rely on the balance between molecular recognition and signal transduction, establishing their coordinated modulation as a design principle for selective metal-oxide sensors.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Normalized Nucleic
Acid Payload in Lipid Nanoparticles:
A Perspective on the Harmonization of Published Data
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Precise and consistent reporting of the nucleic acid payload per lipid nanoparticle (LNP) is important for advancing the understanding and development of nanomedicines. However, the reported number of RNA molecules ranges between ∼1–300 in recent investigations. To evaluate the RNA payload across investigations, we introduce and apply a normalized nucleic acid payload metric which accounts for differences in LNP size, nucleotides per RNA and N/P charge ratio. The normalized payload results in a similar value for siRNA- and mRNA-containing LNPs of different LNP sizes, where the average value of 73 ± 17 nucleotides/zeptoliter agrees well with the expected payload density based on molecular packing arguments. The use of normalized payload harmonizes the reported payload, complements existing payload metrics and enables comparison across samples and measurement techniques at both the single-particle and ensemble-average level.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
All-Transistor Probabilistic
Bits with Deterministic
Clamping for Bayesian Inference and Integer Factorization
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Probabilistic bits (p-bits) have emerged as promising hardware primitives for solving inference and combinatorial optimization problems, while their implementations based on area-intensive CMOS circuits or emerging stochastic devices often face scalability and CMOS co-integration challenges. Here, we present Janus-type hardware for p-bits and their applications in Bayesian inference and integer factorization, composed of homotypic stochastic and deterministic transistors that share an identical structure yet operate through distinct mechanisms. The stochastic field-effect transistor (S-FET) explores the energy landscape through its intrinsic probabilistic switching behavior, whereas the deterministic field-effect transistor (D-FET) provides clamping, which is required to intentionally fix the states of selected p-bits and thereby enable the remaining p-bits to perform probabilistic computations under imposed conditions. This Janus-type architecture reduces the area overhead while decoupling stochastic switching for p-bit generation from deterministic operations for selective clamping. Using this platform, we demonstrate Bayesian network inference with local clamping for conditional probability estimations, as well as integer factorization, in which the output bits are fixed to the target integer and a subset of input bits is selectively clamped to suppress unnecessary configurations, reshape the energy landscape, and increase the probability of reaching the correct global minimum, thereby improving the factorization accuracy.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Defining
a Surface ζ-Potential Window
for Optimal Lymphatic Trafficking and Immunization of Liposomal Vaccines
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>How surface ζ-potential governs nanocarrier trafficking from the skin to draining lymph nodes (LNs) remains unresolved in vaccine delivery. Herein, we have constructed a library of 31 liposomal formulations spanning approximately +41 mV to −60 mV and screened the lymphatic drainage efficiency in vivo. The screen revealed a nonmonotonic relationship: LN accumulation was not monotonically linked to ζ-potential but concentrated within an optimal fitted window of −2.73 mV to −25.43 mV. Guided by this window, we designed four anionic lipids and formulated liposomes within the high-efficiency range. These formulations independently reproduced the predicted drainage window. Mechanistically, strongly negatively charged liposomes (&lt;−30 mV) were physically trapped by the subcutaneous collagen fibers network, whereas weakly negative liposomes exploited transcellular transport mediated by lymphatic endothelial cells. Using the optimal ζ-potential, we coloaded the Axl receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor R428 with tumor antigens to develop a cancer vaccine that dramatically enhanced antigen delivery, elicited potent CD8+ T cell responses, and significantly suppressed prostate tumor growth. These findings establish surface ζ-potential as a fundamental design parameter for LN-targeted liposomal vaccines.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Inflammation-Programmed
Tumor Endothelium Enables
Active Nanoparticle Transport for Enhanced Cancer Therapy
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Efficient delivery of nanotherapeutics to solid tumors remains limited by the tumor endothelial barrier, but it is unknown how tumor vasculature regulates the transport of nanotherapeutics compared to healthy vasculature. Here, we identify an inflammation-associated tumor vascular phenotype that enables nanoparticle transport across endothelium. Using intravital microscopy, we showed that inflammatory tumor microenvironments reduced the glycocalyx coverage on endothelial vasculature and exposed intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), thereby promoting active nanoparticle–endothelium interactions and transendothelial transport. Low-dose X-ray radiation to tumors at 6 Gy further amplified this vascular phenotype. Guided by these insights, we engineered high-drug-content paclitaxel nanocrystals functionalized with anti-ICAM-1 antibodies and demonstrated that combining endothelial-targeted paclitaxel nanocrystals with low-dose radiation significantly enhanced tumoral drug delivery and antitumor efficacy. This work reveals tumor endothelium as a programmable biological interface for nanotherapeutic transport and establishes vascular targeting as a strategy to overcome drug delivery barriers for cancer therapies.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Supramolecularly
Assembled Conjugated Polymer for
High-Capacity, Fast, and Durable Potassium Storage
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Potassium-ion batteries (PIBs) are considered promising candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to the abundance and low cost of potassium resources. Organic anodes, with their flexible molecular frameworks and abundant redox-active sites, are well suited for the reversible storage of relatively large K+. However, achieving high capacity, fast charge transfer, and long-term stability simultaneously remains challenging. Here, we report a supramolecularly assembled crystalline conjugated polymer, poly(tetraaminobenzoquinone) (pTABQ), as an anode material for PIBs. By incorporating abundant carbonyl sites into an extended C–N conjugated framework and forming an ordered layered supramolecular structure through in-plane hydrogen bonding and out-of-plane π–π stacking, pTABQ undergoes charge redistribution within the framework and local rearrangement of the stacking structure during potassiation, enabling high capacity, fast charge transfer, and long-term cycling stability. Benefiting from the synergy between its structural and electronic properties, pTABQ delivers a high reversible capacity of 460 mAh g–1 at 100 mA g–1 and an ultralong cycle life of more than 8600 cycles at 2000 mA g–1. Furthermore, a pTABQ//KMnF full cell achieves a high energy density of 284 Wh kg–1. This work provides a design strategy for high-performance organic materials for electrochemical energy storage.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Molecule Bridging
Enables Integrated Design of a Hydrogen-Bond
Network and Li+ Coordination Chemistry for Long-Life Solid-State
Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>PEO-based electrolytes extensively applied in solid-state lithium metal batteries are always confronted with issues of sluggish ion transport and unfavorable interfacial stability. Although various supramolecular strategies, particularly H-bond engineering, have been attempted, their actual efficacy is fundamentally crippled by the structural lability of the H-bond cross-linking network (HBCN) and the chemical/electrochemical instability of conventional hydrogen bond donors (HBDs) at the interface. Herein, ellagic acid (EA) with abundant phenolic hydroxyl and lactone groups is identified as a valuable HBD and “molecule bridge” in the PEO-based electrolyte, together with the integrated design of a stable HBCN and favorable Li+ coordination chemistry. Through intense H-bond (C–C–O···H–O) and ion–dipole interactions (Li+···O═C–O), strong PEO–Li+ chelation is effectively weakened while enriching the Li+ solvation sheath with TFSI– and EA. Notably, the appearance of TFSI–-rich Li+ coordination and Li+–EA complex in situ generates a robust LiF-, Li3N-, and PhOLi-rich SEI, facilitating uniform lithium deposition and improved interfacial stability. Consequently, the Li|LFP batteries can achieve a stable Li stripping/plating cycle over 3500 cycles at 1C with a capacity retention of 83.8% at the 1000th. The stable operation of more than 200 cycles at 0.5C of 50 μm Li|LFP pouch batteries further confirms the practicality of the EA molecule bridge.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Introducing Controlled
Backbone Porosity and Functionality
into Aerogels through Mesoporous Nanoparticle Assembly
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Precise control over the structural architecture of aerogels remains a central challenge, particularly in integrating well-defined nanoscale porosity within the aerogel backbone. Here, we present a nanoparticle-assembly strategy for synthesizing aerogels with controlled backbone porosity using preformed mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as building blocks. This approach decouples network formation from pore generation, enabling independent control over composition, structure, and porosity. The resulting MSNs aerogel exhibits a high specific surface area of 960 m2 g–1 and significantly enhanced adsorption performance compared with the corresponding powders, driven by improved accessibility of active sites within the hierarchical porous framework. The intrinsic surface roughness of the MSNs promotes interparticle interlocking, resulting in accelerated gelation, a lower percolation threshold, and enhanced structural stability during wetting, as supported by experiments and computational modeling. To demonstrate the versatility of this concept for sensing applications, a pH-responsive probe was incorporated into the MSN dispersion prior to assembly, yielding a solid-state pH indicator. These findings highlight the potential of nanoparticle assembly as a strategy for integrating controlled backbone porosity and tailored functionality into aerogels for applications in adsorption and sensing.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Endometrial Micro-
and Nanoplastics Exposure and Recurrent
Spontaneous Abortion: Evidence from a Human Study and Computational
Toxicology
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly recognized as human environmental contaminants, but their polymer-specific relevance to uterine reproductive health remains unclear. We analyzed endometrial tissues from 82 reproductive-age women, including 43 with recurrent spontaneous abortion (RSA) and 39 controls, using laser direct infrared imaging, scanning electron microscopy, and pyrolysis-GC/MS. Endometrial MNPs were detected in nearly all samples, indicating widespread internal exposure at a clinically relevant reproductive site. Across Bayesian kernel machine regression, weighted quantile sum regression, and quantile g-computation, polypropylene (PP) and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) showed the most consistent positive associations with RSA status, with single-polymer odds ratios of 11.48 (95% CI, 2.02–66.38) and 5.04 (95% CI, 1.08–23.19), respectively. Multiaxis integration linked these polymer-specific signals to a 210-gene program enriched in an SPP1 + macrophage-decidual stromal niche. NEAT1, PPARG, S100A8, and GSDMD were retained as mechanistic candidates supported by distinct genetic, expression, or pathway evidence. Network perturbation prioritized GSDMD-PPARG interplay, and drug-repurposing analyses nominated metformin for preclinical evaluation. These observational and computational findings suggest that PP- and PVC-associated endometrial MNP burdens may mark RSA risk through inflammatory maternal–fetal-interface programs, warranting prospective, multicenter, and additive-resolved validation. These findings prioritize polymer-specific mechanisms at the maternal–fetal interface for testing in future reproductive health research.</jats:p>

title:
Programmable Transistor
Arrays Based on Wafer-Scale
p-Type Monolayer WSe2 with Nanoscale Triboelectrification
Tunability
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Postfabrication customization of transistor arrays remains challenging because gate architectures and electrical functionalities are permanently defined during device fabrication. Here, we report a programmable gate strategy for transistor arrays fabricated from wafer-scale monolayer WSe2, in which nanoscale triboelectrification at the dielectric surface modulates carrier transport in the underlying semiconductor. Nanoscale triboelectric potential generated by charge transfer between the dielectric and the atomic force microscope tip enables reversible modulation between neutral and p-doped states in WSe2 with a maximum on/off ratio over 106. The programmable gating strategy allows the geometry, polarization strength, and spatial distribution of the gated regions to be arbitrarily defined and rewritten after fabrication. Using this strategy, we demonstrate programmable arrays with channel lengths down to 1 μm and an integration density of 4444/mm2, realizing NOT, NAND, NOR, AND, OR, and AOI21 logic functions. The proposed strategy extends the charge-based gating to high-density WSe2 transistor arrays with substantially improved gate modulation efficiency, while providing a versatile platform for next-generation electronic and optoelectronic systems with on-demand customization and dynamically tunable functionalities.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Process-Biomimetic
Hydrogel with Time-Programmed Stiffening
and Oxygen Delivery Orchestrates the Immune-Osteogenic Cascade for
Bone Regeneration
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Tissue remodeling progressively stiffens the extracellular matrix (ECM), generating stage-specific biomechanical cues that guide tissue morphogenesis. However, conventional biomaterials fail to recapitulate its spatiotemporal variation due to their inherently static and nonadaptive nature. Herein, we developed a biomimetic fracture-healing hydrogel that optimizes the osteogenic microenvironment through coupled adaptive matrix mechanics and sustained oxygen delivery. Matrix stiffening relies on the programmed, sustained release of Ca2+ from polydopamine-coated calcium peroxide particles (CaO2@PDA), which act as time-dependent ionic cross-linkers. We control Ca2+ release kinetics to achieve a stiffening trajectory from ∼20 to ∼61 kPa over 10 days, accurately recapitulating the mechanical evolution of native callus. This strategy autonomously remodels the matrix from a soft, immune-permissive state to a stiff, osteoinductive one, while simultaneously releasing O2 to mitigate hypoxia-driven necrosis and fuel angiogenesis. Moreover, RNA sequencing and complementary validation revealed that the dynamic hydrogel promotes integrin-mediated mechanotransduction into the TGF-β/Smad2/3 axis to drive osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. In a rat distal femoral defect model, this hydrogel effectively enhanced new bone formation and neovascularization, while exerting notable immunomodulatory functions. Featuring spatiotemporally adaptive mechanics, this hydrogel provides a strategy for bone defect repair and promises to expand the biomedical potential of dynamically tunable biomaterials.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Coupling O2 Activation with Proton Capture
Boosts Carbon Nitride Fixed-Bed Flow Photosynthesis of Hydrogen Peroxide
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Practical H2O2 photoproduction via the 2e ORR by polymeric carbon nitride (CN) is hindered by insufficient surface reaction kinetics, limitations in continuous reaction, and extra H2O2/catalyst separation. This work engineered fixed-bed CN networks with oxophilic Ni nanoparticles and proton-affinitive anthraquinone moieties, which enhanced the catalyst’s O2 adsorption/activation and proton capture capability. Besides, due to the electronic delocalization and extended π–π conjugation system, they imparted the catalyst with extended light absorption and improved charge separation. The as-synthesized photocatalyst demonstrated a 12.7-fold enhancement of H2O2 yield in flowing water, which reaches 3.6 mmol m–2 h–1 (1362 μmol g–1 h–1), outperforming most reported CN-based catalysts. Under natural sunlight irradiation, 581.8 μmol H2O2 was produced in 9 h using a 12 cm × 8.5 cm photocatalyst sheet. The practical application was exemplified by efficient on-site flow photo-Fenton degradation of organic contaminants with &gt;90% degradation in 1.5 h. Electronic studies and local reactant enrichment investigation revealed that the adsorbed O2 at the Ni site and protons at AQ proceed to generate H2O2 upon participation of photogenerated electrons via the two-step 1e ORR process with high selectivity. This work demonstrates a successful surface chemistry design of fixed-bed CN networks for efficient continuous-flow photoproduction of H2O2 with facile separation.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Climate-Selective
Dynamic Window with Temperature-Dependent
Morphological Tuning of Zn Electrodeposits
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Reversible metal electrodeposition (RME) dynamic windows are promising energy saving devices that enable dynamic modulation of incident light and radiative heat flow through windows. However, for practical application, physical robustness in diverse climate zones is necessary, especially under subzero conditions in high-latitude regions with high per-capita energy consumption. Here, we developed N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) based electrolytes for Zn RME dynamic windows operating from room-temperature (RT) to low-temperature as −30 °C (LT). The optimized device exhibits distinct optical modes in the electrodeposited state depending on temperature, with a reflective mode at RT to suppress solar heat gain and an absorptive mode at LT to enhance photothermal absorption of visible-near-infrared (VIS–NIR) light. This temperature-selective optical transition originates from modulation of Zn2+ solvation environments and diffusion-controlled growth, resulting in differences in electrodeposition behavior. In particular, a pronounced absorptive optical response is associated with void-rich porous morphology, emphasizing the importance of morphology control. In this work, unlike conventional RME dynamic windows that retain a reflective optical response regardless of temperature, we demonstrate temperature-dependent selection between reflective and absorptive optical modes in the electrodeposited state, highlighting the potential for climate-selective light and thermal management.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Nanofibrous
Catalysts for Local Prodrug Activation
through Bioorthogonal Uncaging Reactions
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Bioorthogonal chemistry through implant-based catalysis provides powerful strategies for site-specific drug activation, enabling therapeutic control beyond what conventional systemic dosing or local delivery depots can achieve. In oncology, this approach is particularly compelling because dose-limiting systemic toxicity often prevents therapeutic drug exposure at the tumor, limiting treatment efficacy. Despite its promise, in vivo implementation remains limited by challenges such as catalyst instability, insufficient spatial confinement, and uncontrolled diffusion of activated drugs. This Perspective focuses on recent efforts to localize and sustain bioorthogonal uncaging reactions within living systems, with a particular emphasis on heterogeneous catalytic approaches. Building on advances that employ metallic nanoparticles as bioorthogonal catalysts, we highlight both their successes and the outstanding barriers associated with biofouling, catalyst leaching, and mass-transport constraints. Here we propose nanofibrous catalytic implants as an emerging platform for localized bioorthogonal chemistry. By integrating metallic nanocatalysts within nanofibrous implants, these systems can combine high surface area, efficient reactant transport, mechanical adaptability, and prolonged catalyst retention. We discuss fabrication strategies, key biological considerations, and future design principles that may guide the development of safer and more precise implant-based drug activation technologies.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Molecularly Woven
Quasi-3D Covalent Organic Frameworks
Enable Piezocatalytic PANoptosis for Potent Cancer Immunotherapy
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Metastatic breast cancer remains refractory to current immunotherapies due to insufficient immunogenic cell death and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Here, we engineer a piezocatalytic quasi-3D covalent organic framework (COF) nanoplatform (PPyrr-COF NPs) through a molecular weaving strategy, in which aligned polypyrrole (PPyrr) chains are covalently integrated into the COF scaffold, enabling efficient piezocatalysis-driven immunotherapy. Theoretical and experimental analyses demonstrate that the covalent linkage between the PPyrr chains and the COF skeleton creates z-axis-oriented electron-transport pathways, increases charge density, and narrows the bandgap, thereby substantially augmenting piezocatalytic oxidation activity. Under ultrasound irradiation, PPyrr-COF NPs generate abundant reactive oxygen species, which trigger a distinct PANoptotic cell death pathway and robust immunogenic cell death, characterized by the release of damage-associated molecular patterns. In murine 4T1 breast cancer models, PPyrr-COF NPs combined with ultrasound irradiation not only suppress primary tumor growth but also inhibit distant tumors and prevent lung metastasis. These effects are mediated by systemic antitumor immunity, including dendritic cell maturation and cytotoxic T lymphocyte infiltration, supported by transcriptomic analysis revealing regulation of PANoptosis and immune-related pathways. This work establishes a strategy for designing high-performance organic piezocatalysts and presents a noninvasive synergistic approach for cancer immunotherapy.</jats:p>

title:
Contactless Nanoscale
Temperature Mapping Using a
Luminescent Nanoparticle Attached to a Sharp Glass Tip
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Temperature mapping of surfaces and surface structures at the nanoscale is of key importance in a variety of fields including nanoelectronics, optoelectronics, and biology. To meet this need, a range of scanning thermal microscopy techniques have been developed that utilize various sensing principles and probes. Because the temperature-sensing probe is operated in a contact or near-contact range with the sample to provide efficient thermal coupling, the probe’s heat conductance and heat capacity need to be considered in quantitative temperature measurements. This work demonstrates an isolated single luminescent NaYF4:Yb3+/Er3+ core@shell nanoparticle attached to a sharp glass tip as a nanoscale luminescent temperature probe operated in a noncontact atomic force microscope setup. We found that, in contrast to gold tips, glass tips, due to their lower thermal conductivity, do not measurably alter the detected temperature within the measurement accuracy of 1 °C. The thermal coupling efficiency between the heated surface and the temperature-sensing nanoparticle attached to the glass tip is sufficient to establish thermal equilibrium. Nanoscale temperature maps of an optically heated gold nanoparticle at varying heating intensities and of laser-heated monolayers of transition-metal dichalcogenides on glass illustrate the spatial and temperature resolution of the approach together with its broad applicability.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Four-Dimensional
Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy
Nanoscale Phase Mapping of the Lithium-Metal Surface Passivation Layer
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Mapping microstructural features is vital to developing next-generation materials in renewable energy applications. However, the nanometer-scale dimensions, chemical heterogeneity, and beam sensitivity of these materials make their structural characterization exceptionally challenging. Here, we present a data acquisition and analysis workflow for four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) applied to a beam-sensitive lithium-metal filament sample with a surface passivation layer. By combining data dimensionality reduction with unsupervised machine-learning approaches, we perform real-space clustering to enhance signal-to-noise ratios across large data sets. Automated Bragg reflection analysis was then used to identify distinct crystallographic phases within the surface passivation layer. This approach enables nanoscale phase mapping of dominant species across large fields of view with nanometer-level lateral resolution. We identify lithium oxide and lithium hydroxide as the predominant crystalline phases in the lithium-metal surface passivation layer.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Formation
of Dynamic Nanoporous Shells on Bimetallic
Particles During Carbon Dioxide Hydrogenation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol relies on dynamic interactions between metal nanoparticles and oxide supports, yet a comprehensive, particle-resolved understanding of catalyst restructuring during activation and reaction remains difficult to obtain via conventional ensemble-averaged or post-reaction characterization. Here, identical-location high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (IL-HRTEM) has been used to track the same PdCu nanoparticles on ZnO, from the as-prepared state, through H2 activation, to subsequent CO2 hydrogenation. The most pronounced restructuring occurred under H2 conditions used for catalyst activation, when the number of observable nanoparticles decreased by a factor of 2, their average size increased, and crystalline lattice features became more readily identifiable. Particle-by-particle tracking directly distinguished migration and coalescence processes from Ostwald ripening, demonstrating that both mechanisms contribute concurrently to particle coarsening. Support-derived atomically thin ZnOx overlayers start to grow over PdCu nanoparticles under H2 and continue during CO2 hydrogenation, concurrent with a slowing of nanoparticle coarsening. The ZnOx shells are dynamic, opening and closing subnanometre pores during reaction. Identical-location single-particle analysis showed that ZnOx shells restrict nanoparticle migration and coalescence while still allowing sub-nm dynamics to readjust particle shape, mediating optimized admission of gas molecules to the metal for catalysis. Our findings reveal the mechanisms by which a morphologically uniform PdCu/ZnO material evolves into a complex PdCu–ZnOx interface governed by coupled interparticle and metal–support dynamics. Importantly, the PdCu–ZnOx form correlates with high methanol productivity, linking catalytic function to the atomic dynamics of the PdCu–ZnOx interface resolved by IL-HRTEM. More broadly, self-assembled porous oxide shells may provide a powerful general strategy for stabilizing supported metal catalysts while preserving access to active interfacial sites.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Nonvolatile Multistate
2D Nanoelectromechanical Memories
toward In-Memory Computing
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS) are promising for post-Moore-era memory and computing paradigms, thanks to the low power consumption, high reconfigurability, and high-temperature compatibility enabled by the mechanical degree of freedom. In particular, NEMS based on two-dimensional (2D) materials demonstrate record-high frequency tunability, making them ideal for realizing frequency-shift-based computing. However, such frequency shifts are volatile, which seriously limits the applications of nanomechanical memory and in-memory computing. Here, we address this challenge by embedding hafnium-oxide-based nonvolatile resistive random-access memories (RRAMs) inside 2D NEMS resonators. By leveraging the ultrahigh frequency tunability of 2D NEMS resonators, we create frequency-shift-based multistate nanomechanical memories. We achieve nonvolatile coding and discernment of 32 resonant states, which can be further extended. We further show that in-memory mechanical computing circuits using such 2D NEMS memories as weights of artificial neural networks can achieve high-accuracy (&gt;99%) and robust (both with and without considering device variation) inference operations. These results demonstrate nonvolatile multistate nanomechanical memory and its high potential for in-memory computing applications.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Side-Chain Engineering
Stabilizes Long-Lived Photosensitizer
Radical-Ion Pairs for Hypoxic Photodynamic Therapy
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Photosensitizer radical-ion pairs (PS+•/PS–•) can drive self-oxygen-supplying photoredox cascades for hypoxia-tolerant photodynamic therapy (PDT), but their rapid recombination limits photoredox efficiency. Here, we demonstrate that cationic side chains can regulate molecular packing in zwitterionic photosensitizer nanoclusters to modulate PS+•/PS–• formation and recombination dynamics, enabling self-oxygen-supplying photoredox cascades for hypoxia-tolerant PDT. Mechanistic studies reveal that triphenylphosphonium side chains favor compact cross-arranged molecular packing in photosensitizer (C3TPH) nanoclusters through their combined electrostatic and steric effects. Compared with its face-to-face-packed counterpart C3PH, C3TPH preserves comparable electronic coupling for charge separation (69 vs 82 meV) while substantially reducing charge-recombination coupling (45 vs 133 meV), thereby prolonging the PS+•/PS–• pair lifetime from hundreds of picoseconds to 21.6 ns. The resulting PS+• oxidizes water to produce O2, which serves as the starting substrate for a PS–•-mediated photoreduction cascade that ultimately yields •OH. This cascade enables C3TPH to achieve a 4.1-fold higher •OH generation than the commercial photosensitizer TMPyP4 under hypoxia. Accordingly, C3TPH achieves a more than 10-fold enhancement in antibacterial efficacy relative to vancomycin. This work establishes side-chain engineering as a design principle for regulating radical-ion-pair dynamics to enhance photoredox reactivity for hypoxia-tolerant PDT.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
A
Pd Single-Atom/Nanocluster Nanozyme Achieves High
Dual Peroxidase- and Catalase-like Activities via Interlayer-Confined
Oxygen-Species Spillover
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nanozymes that reproduce the multienzyme antioxidant machinery of living tissue remain difficult to engineer because the atomic sites that most strongly activate H2O2 also bind the reaction intermediates too tightly to release them─a trade-off, rooted in the Sabatier principle, that often caps the activity of single-atom catalysts. Here, we report an atomically dispersed palladium nanozyme, Pd1+NPs/G, in which isolated Pd single atoms and ultrasmall Pd nanoclusters coexist on graphene oxide (GO) and propose, based on density functional theory (DFT) calculations and isotope labeling, that this architecture relieves this trade-off through an interlayer-confined hydroxyl (*OH) spillover mechanism. Prepared by atomic layer deposition, Pd1+NPs/G exhibits the highest mass-normalized peroxidase (POD)-like and catalase (CAT)-like activities among its single-atom (Pd1/G) and nanoparticle (PdNPs/G) counterparts, with 18- and 8-fold higher specific activities than Pd1/G. DFT calculations indicate that the Pd single atom acts as a strong-binding electron-donor site and the Pd cluster as a moderate-binding acceptor site; an *OH intermediate is proposed to migrate across the ∼7–10 Å GO interlayer gap between them with a barrier of only 0.34 eV, enabling O–O coupling on the cluster, consistent with the observed 16O18O isotope scrambling. This spatial decoupling of the activation and desorption steps drives simultaneously efficient •OH generation and O2 evolution. The dual activity translates into H2O2-enhanced killing of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, macrophage M1 → M2 repolarization, enhanced angiogenesis, and accelerated closure of S. aureus-infected wounds in vivo without detectable systemic toxicity. This work establishes support-geometry-directed oxygen-species spillover as a design principle for high-activity synergistic nanozymes.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Ratiometric Multispectral
Upconversion-Photoacoustic
Nanoprobes for Noninvasive Imaging of Hepatic and Urinary Copper Dynamics
in Wilson’s Disease
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Wilson’s disease (WD) is an inherited disorder of copper metabolism, and the lack of a noninvasive, real-time monitoring method for copper accumulation presents a significant clinical challenge. Herein, we report a galactose-targeted, dual-modal ratiometric nanoprobe, termed Cu-MB, which integrates multispectral upconversion luminescence (mUCL) and multispectral photoacoustic tomography (mPAT) for the sensitive, specific, and dynamic visualization of hepatic copper in deep tissues. The nanoprobe features a Cu2+-responsive NIR-II chromophore (Cu-RB) and an internal reference dye coloaded onto upconversion nanoparticles, enabling self-calibrated quantification via the ratiometric signals of PA930/PA680 and UCL660/UCL800. This design effectively corrects for environmental interference and offers superior tissue penetration. In WD mouse models, Cu-MB enables real-time, longitudinal monitoring of hepatic copper deposition and accurately quantifies urinary copper excretion, showing excellent correlation with the clinical gold standard (ICP-MS). Furthermore, it allows for the visual assessment of the efficacy of copper chelation therapies (e.g., EDTA and D-pen). Notably, in a blinded clinical validation using human urine samples, the mPAT signal from Cu-MB achieved high diagnostic accuracy in this preliminary cohort, showing a clear separation trend between WD patients and healthy controls. This work presents a robust nanoprobe platform for noninvasive imaging of copper dynamics, enabling the diagnosis, dynamic monitoring, and therapeutic evaluation of Wilson’s disease.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title: Synergistic high negative pressure enables direct lithium crystallization from raw salt-lake brine
content: Extracting lithium from salt-lake brines is expected to solve the growing demand for lithium resources. However, conventional technologies require high electrical energy and freshwater consumption and involve long processing times. Herein, we developed a solar-driven separation–crystallization pump (SCP) for direct lithium crystallization from raw salt-lake brine. The SCP synergistically harnesses the capillary negative pressure of a nanoporous polyvinyl alcohol hydrogel and the evaporation negative pressure of a reduced graphene oxide loaded TiN evaporation zone, achieving an ultrahigh negative pressure of 65.26 bar, which is an order of magnitude higher than that obtained via conventional technologies. This ultrahigh pressure is sufficient to overcome the osmotic pressure of raw salt-lake brines, thereby enabling direct Mg2+/Li+ separation via a nanofiltration membrane without dilution. Additionally, the highly soluble lithium salt is subjected to controlled crystallization for collection, overcoming the bottleneck of conventional technologies that cannot directly harvest lithium products. Thus, the SCP outperforms reported membrane-based technologies with regard to treated brine concentration, separation factor, and electrical energy consumption, while achieving a Li+ yield of 0.32 g m−2 and co-producing freshwater with a flux of 32.71 L m−2 h−1 for 308.51 g L−1 raw Caka salt-lake brine outdoors. This study demonstrates a green and consumption-free process for direct lithium extraction from raw salt-lake brines, providing a low-consumption route for solar-driven lithium extraction.

title: In Situ Polymerized Interfaces Enable Robust and High‐Performance Dry‐Coating Electrodes
content:
An in situ polymerization strategy is reported to construct mechanically stable interfaces in dry‐coating electrodes. A deep eutectic liquid composed of acrylonitrile, acrylamide, and LiTFSI infiltrates the electrode composite during dry mixing, followed by photopolymerization to form an adhesive polymer network. The resulting Poly‐DC electrodes exhibit enhanced interfacial contact and electrochemical performance, demonstrating their potential for scalable dry‐coating electrode manufacturing.








ABSTRACT
Dry‐coating electrode technology eliminates the use of toxic N‐methyl‐2‐pyrrolidone and offers a promising route for sustainable battery manufacturing. However, its practical implementation remains limited by the weak interfacial mechanics among rigid cathode particles, polytetrafluoroethylene nanofibers, and conductive carbon additives. These fragile interfaces reduce mechanical robustness and interfacial stability, thereby compromising both processability and electrochemical performance. Here, we report an in situ polymerization strategy using a polymerizable deep eutectic liquid additive, which forms an adhesive polymer network upon photopolymerization, thereby reinforcing contact among electrode components and improving electrode robustness. The resulting dry‐coating LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) electrodes exhibit a 55% increase in elongation at break and deliver a reversible specific capacity of 121 mAh g−1 at 5 C with a mass loading of 10 mg cm−2. A 3.77 Ah Li||NCM811 pouch cell achieves maximum cell‐level energy and power densities of 412 Wh kg−1 and 574 W kg−1, respectively. In addition, a 0.60 Ah graphite||NCM811 pouch cell retains 70% of its capacity after 870 cycles. Our results establish in situ polymerization as a viable route for mechanically robust, high‐performance dry‐coating electrodes.

title: Unified Grain‐Boundary and Electrode‐Interface Engineering Enables High‐Performance Magnesium‐Based Thermoelectrics
content:
A unified interface engineering strategy is developed for Bi‐rich Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectrics. Nb‐rich internal interfaces regulate grain‐boundary carrier transport, while Nb‐based external contacts reduce electrode‐interface losses. This coupled design improves material transport and device integration, enabling high‐performance Mg‐based thermoelectric modules for low‐temperature‐gradient power generation and active cooling.








ABSTRACT
High‐performance thermoelectric devices require not only intrinsically efficient materials but also minimized transport losses across multiple interfaces during device integration. However, internal transport interfaces and external electrode contacts are typically optimized independently, creating a persistent challenge in translating material‐level advances into device‐level performance. Here we establish a unified interface engineering strategy in Bi‐rich Mg3(Sb,Bi)2 thermoelectrics by using Nb as a multifunctional interface modifier. In Mg3Sb0.7Bi1.3, Nb‐rich internal interfaces regulate grain‐boundary carrier transport, while Nb foils provide chemically stable and low‐resistance electrode contacts. First‐principles calculations and atomic‐scale characterization reveal that the Bi‐rich composition suppresses extensive Nb‐related reactions while enabling electronically favorable confined interfaces. Nb incorporation increases the weighted mobility to 315.6 cm2·V−1·s−1 and achieves a room‐temperature zT above 0.8, while Nb foil contacts yield an intrinsic contact resistivity of 1.8 µΩ·cm2. Integrating Nb‐engineered n‐type Mg3Sb0.7Bi1.3 with p‐type MgAgSb enables Mg‐based thermoelectric modules with a conversion efficiency of 3.8% at ΔT = 100 K and a maximum cooling temperature difference of 82.7 K at a hot‐side temperature of 373 K. This work establishes a general interface design principle for thermoelectrics, demonstrating that interface modifiers for bulk transport optimization can also serve as electrode‐contact materials to bridge the gap between high‐performance materials and practical devices.

title: In Situ Formation of Inorganic‐Rich Interphase via SiO2 Additive for High‐Performance Sodium Metal Batteries
content:
This work overturns the conventional view of silicon dioxide as an electrochemically inert material toward Na by revealing its dual‐function role in sodium metal batteries. Through in situ electrochemical reduction, silicon dioxide forms an inorganic‐rich interphase enriched with Na2O and NaF. This synergistic interphase regulation effectively suppresses dendrite growth and enables highly reversible, long‐life sodium metal batteries.








ABSTRACT
Sodium metal batteries (SMBs) are promising candidates for next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage systems, yet their practical application is hindered by dendritic growth and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation. Herein, we report an in situ interfacial regulation strategy by introducing amorphous SiO2 (a‑SiO2) into Na metal anodes through an accumulative roll bonding process. We reveal that SiO2 undergoes electrochemical reduction reaction with Na, generating SiOx (1<x<2) and Na2O—a beneficial inorganic SEI component that enhances interfacial ion transport and mechanical robustness. Furthermore, a‐SiO2 exhibits superior interfacial reactivity and strong adsorption affinity toward fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC), promoting a NaF‐rich SEI that suppresses electrolyte decomposition. This synergetic inorganic‐rich SEI homogenizes Na deposition and accelerates ion diffusion kinetics. As a result, the Na/a‑SiO2 symmetric cell achieves an ultralow overpotential of 24 mV at 0.5 mA cm−2 and stable cycling for over 1350 h. When paired with the Na3V2(PO4)2O2F cathode, the full cell delivers excellent rate capability (73.9 mAh g−1 at 60 C) and cycling stability with 80% capacity retention after 8000 cycles at 20 C. This work establishes SiO2 as a scalable and effective inorganic additive for tailoring SEI chemistry, offering a practical pathway toward high‐energy and durable SMBs.

title: Ion‐Pair Decoupler Tunes Solvation Chemistry for Room‐Temperature Polymer Electrolytes With Built‐In Flame Retardancy
content:
An ion‐pair decoupler is introduced into the polymer solid‐state electrolyte. It features multi‐coordinated active sites, with charge‐rich centers that can competitively bind Li+ with the polymer chains, while also utilizing hydrogen bond donors to anchor TFSI‒, thereby restructuring the solvated Li+ into solvent‐separated ion pairs. This design significantly enhances the room‐temperature electrochemical performance of the polymer solid‐state electrolyte with weakened the Li+ migration energy barrier, while also conferring excellent flame‐retardant properties.








ABSTRACT
Solid‐state polymer electrolytes for high‐energy lithium‐metal batteries are severely constrained by low room‐temperature ionic conductivity. However, mainstream approaches focus on regulating the aggregate structure and flexibility of polymer chains while neglecting the ionic solvation microenvironment, which caps ionic conductivity gains at a marginal level. Here, an innovative ion‐pair decoupling strategy is proposed to reshape the Li+ solvation chemistry within polymer matrices and to facilitate rapid ionic conduction. The ion‐pair decoupler, diethyl phosphoramidate, promotes the dissociation of lithium salt into a configuration dominated by solvent‐separated ion pairs by coordinating with Li+ via its electron‐rich P = O groups and anchoring TFSI‒ through hydrogen bond donors. Consequently, the ionic conductivity of the engineered electrolyte increases 24.6‐fold at 25°C. Li symmetric cells achieve stable cycling over 850 h, and Li||LiFePO4 cells deliver a high‐capacity retention rate of 96.5% after 400 cycles at 25°C. Furthermore, the designed electrolyte exhibits excellent self‐extinguishing flame‐retardant properties by combining gas‐phase radical scavenging and condensed‐phase char‐forming mechanisms. Thus, a single molecular design simultaneously serves as an ion‐pair decoupler and an intrinsic flame retardant, establishing solvation‐chemistry tuning as a new paradigm for safe, room‐temperature solid polymer electrolytes.

title: Ion‐Pair Mediation Enables Low‐Viscosity, Nonflammable Ternary Hybrid Electrolytes for High‐Voltage Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
content:
A low‐viscosity, nonflammable ternary hybrid electrolyte enables high‐voltage AZMBs via an ion‐pair‐mediated ordered interfacial assembly. EMIM+‐TFSI−/OTf− ion pairs undergo adsorption‐reduction‐anchoring to form an inner inorganic/outer organic bilayer, in which OTf−/TFSI− decomposition generates a robust fluoride‐rich SEI that subsequently anchors EMIM+ as a dynamic cationic shield. The Zn//LiMn2O4 cells deliver a high discharge plateau of 1.86 V vs. Zn.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) have garnered attention as promising energy storage devices owing to their intrinsic safety. However, the practical energy density of AZMBs is severely constrained by the narrow electrochemical window and sluggish kinetics inherent to conventional concentrated or viscous aqueous electrolytes. To address these limitations, a ternary hybrid system comprising a Zn(OTf)2/LiOTf dual‐salt matrix and low‐volume (5 vol.%) 1‐ethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide (EMIMTFSI, abbreviated as EMT) ionic liquid is constructed. In the ternary system, EMIM+‐TFSI−/OTf− ion pairs reconstruct the hydrogen‐bond network of the dual‐salt framework, thereby reducing bulk viscosity and broadening the electrochemical stability window to 2.76 V at low total salt concentrations. More importantly, these ion pairs undergo adsorption‐reduction‐anchoring to form an inner inorganic/outer organic bilayer, where OTf−/TFSI− decomposition generates a robust fluoride‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that subsequently anchors EMIM+ as a dynamic cationic shield. Consequently, the Zn//Zn symmetric cells achieve an outstanding lifespan of 3215 h at 1 mA cm−2. Zn//MnO2‐CNT battery demonstrates 88.21% capacity retention after 1100 cycles at 1 A g−1 within a high‐voltage range (0.8–2.0 V), and Zn//LiMn2O4 battery exhibits a high discharge plateau of 1.86 V v s. Zn. This work offers a promising electrolyte design strategy for high‐voltage and long‐cycle‐life AZMBs.

title: An Electrically Gated Solid‐State Thermal Transistor for Energy‐Efficient Thermal Management
content:
An electrically gated bulk single‐crystal BaTiO3 thermal transistor switches heat flow by reorienting ferroelectric domains. Electric‐field‐driven redistribution between a‐ and c‐domains, quantified by in situ X‐ray diffraction, continuously tunes the thermal conductivity from 2.7 to 4.3 W m−1 K−1. On an equal‐time duty cycle, the transistor delivers the same temperature modulation as a vapor‐compression heat pump while requiring approximately ninefold lower time‐averaged electrical input.








ABSTRACT
Vapor‐compression heating and cooling systems dominate modern thermal management, yet their efficiency and scalability remain constrained by mechanical complexity and refrigerant‐based operation. Solid‐state approaches offer an attractive alternative, with recent demonstrations showing the potential for highly efficient, compact thermal control. Here we demonstrate an electrically gated solid‐state thermal transistor based on bulk single‐crystal barium titanate, achieving a switching ratio of 1.6, among the highest reported for bulk ferroelectrics. We further introduce switching efficiency as a figure of merit, reaching ∼8.52 cm3 J−1, more than two orders of magnitude higher than that of the highest‐performing reported thermal switch, PbZrO3. Unlike previous thermal switches that operate between two discrete states, this device provides continuously tunable thermal‐conductivity states, enabling transistor‐like modulation and amplification of heat flow. In situ x‐ray diffraction combined with first‐principles calculations shows that switching originates from anisotropic phonon transport between ferroelectric domains. Integrated into a proof‐of‐concept thermal‐management system, the device shifts the baseline temperature of a miniature human analog by ∼0.6°C at a cycle‐averaged power input of 33 µW cm−2, approximately ninefold lower than a vapor‐compression heat pump performing the same task. These results establish ferroelectric thermal transistors as a programmable, energy‐efficient platform for solid‐state thermal management.

title: Data‐Driven Conformational Mismatch Design Enables Extreme‐Temperature Energy Storage in Copolyimides
content:
Machine learning guides the prediction of glass transition temperatures in polyimides. Structural and molecular analyses connect diamine bridge design with atomic thermal fluctuations and conformational entropy. Tetrahedral carbon bridges disrupt repetitive conformational sequences and introduce conformational mismatches, highlighting the interplay between chain rigidity and conformational entropy in governing the thermal response of polyimides.








ABSTRACT
High‐temperature capacitive energy storage requires polymer dielectrics to combine a wide optical bandgap (Eg) with a high glass‐transition temperature (Tg), properties that are often difficult to optimize simultaneously through conventional backbone design. Here, we introduce conformational mismatch into semi‐alicyclic polyimide copolymers and identify promising monomer combinations through a multistage workflow integrating machine‐learning prediction of Tg, density‐functional‐theory calculations of electronic structure, and molecular‐dynamics analysis of chain conformations. Incorporating a methyl‐substituted diamine yields Co‐PI‐tC, in which local conformational mismatch modifies molecular fluctuations and chain packing while suppressing thermally activated charge transport. Conformational entropy estimates derived from atomic fluctuations quantitatively capture these changes and complement conventional structural and electronic descriptors. The resulting Co‐PI‐tC film combines a Tg of 271.52°C with Eg of 4.28 eV, delivers a discharged energy density of 8.6 J cm−3 at 200°C with 90% efficiency and retains 6.7 J cm−3 at 250°C, setting a high‐temperature energy‐storage record among reported copolymer dielectrics. These results establish conformational mismatch as an effective molecular‐design strategy for reconciling thermal stability and electrical insulation in high‐temperature polymer dielectrics.

title: Magnetic Switching of Exciton Lifetime in CrSBr
content:
The authors study CrSBr layers using time‐resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy in an external magnetic field, revealing a step‐like reduction of the exciton lifetime during the magnetization flip from the antiferromagnetic to the ferromagnetic phase. The magnetic switching of the exciton lifetime is attributed to disorder‐induced exciton localization, with magnetic order controlling the spatial extent of the exciton wavefunction.








ABSTRACT
Exciton dynamics in layered magnetic semiconductors provide a sensitive probe of the interplay between spin order and light–matter interaction. Here, we study thin CrSBr layers using time‐resolved photoluminescence spectroscopy in an external magnetic field, revealing a step‐like reduction in the exciton lifetime from 11 to 7 ps during the magnetization flip from the antiferromagnetic to the ferromagnetic phase. The reduction of the exciton lifetime in the ferromagnetic phase persists below the Néel temperature, as evidenced by its strong magnetic‐field dependence that disappears in the paramagnetic phase. Ab initio calculations reveal a one‐dimensional nature of free excitons, accompanied by a pronounced change in the oscillator strength across the magnetic phase transition, predicting a shorter radiative lifetime of free excitons in the antiferromagnetic phase of CrSBr, contradicting the experimental observations. This discrepancy is explained by strong localization of excitons at low temperature. We show both experimentally and theoretically that the observed magnetic switching of the exciton lifetime is attributed to a larger exciton localization volume leading to a larger oscillator strength in the ferromagnetic phase. The results show that disorder‐induced localization effects play a key role in exciton dynamics in CrSBr.

title: Highly Adaptable Electrochemical Lithium Extraction From Brine via Heterojunction Engineering
content:
Electrochemical lithium extraction from brines is limited by slow desolvation and Na+ competition. A Li–Ti–O heterojunction on LiFePO4 (LFP‑SEF) accelerates Li+ desolvation via a built‑in electric field and blocks Na+ by sieving. It achieves high separation factors (Na/Li ≈990, Mg/Li ≈1857) and 83.72% capacity retention after 50 cycles in high‑Na brine (Na/Li = 150). The device scales to 1.5 m2, demonstrating industrial promise.








ABSTRACT
Electrochemical lithium extraction from salt‐lake brines has received extensive attention due to its low energy consumption, environmental friendliness, and high efficiency. However, conventional electrode materials suffer from sluggish desolvation kinetics and competing cations intercalation (Na+) in the diverse brine environment across the world. Herein, a heterojunction engineering strategy was proposed to solve the above challenges. A lithium titanium oxides (LTO) heterojunction was rationally designed and constructed on the surface of LiFePO4 (named LFP‐SEF), which could expedite the desolvation process of Li+ via the induced built‐in electric field and suppress competing cation intercalation via size sieving. Consequently, the LFP‐SEF‐based device consistently delivers outstanding lithium extraction performance in a series of brines (Na/Li ≈ 1–150) around the world. Even in the brine from southern Tibet (Dangxiongcuo Salt Lake) with a high Na/Li mass ratio of 150, LFP‐SEF also exhibits 83.72% capacity retention after 50 cycles with high separation factor (Na/Li ≈ 989.80; Mg/Li ≈1856.50). The exceptional performance is preserved as the device size increases from lab‐scale to production‐scale (1.5 m2), demonstrating its excellent industrialization prospects. The concept of heterojunction engineering proposed in this work opens a promising route to industrial‐scale lithium extraction in complex brine environment.

title: Multiscale Design of Strong and Tough Gelatin Hydrogels for Biomedical Applications
content:
This review discusses the structural origins of gelatin hydrogel mechanics and the multiscale strategies used to achieve strengthening and toughening, spanning molecular, network, domain/interface, and higher‐order structure levels. The review highlights their role in partially alleviating mechanical coupling and expanding biomedical applications, along with future opportunities in strand‐level design, mechano‐biological integration, long‐term stability, scalable manufacturing, and clinical translation.








ABSTRACT
Gelatin, a natural polypeptide derived from partial hydrolysis of collagen, possesses excellent biocompatibility, biodegradability, inherent cell‐adhesive properties, and abundant functional groups for chemical modification. These intrinsic advantages have established gelatin hydrogels as promising platforms for diverse biomedical applications. Despite these merits, conventional gelatin hydrogels exhibit insufficient strength and toughness, restricting their use in mechanically demanding and long‐term biomedical scenarios. Recent advances have addressed these limitations through multiscale engineering of molecular interactions, network topology, domain or interface organization, and higher‐order structures. These approaches substantially enhance strength and toughness, while providing additional control over other coupled mechanical responses. This review outlines the design principles and multiscale strategies for strong and tough gelatin hydrogels, summarizes recent progress in their biomedical applications, and discusses key challenges and future directions toward mechanical regulation and clinical translation.

title: Reconstructing Structural Dynamic Cooperativity Suppresses Conduction Loss in Linear Aliphatic Polymer Dielectrics at Elevated Temperatures
content:
Aromatic engineering reconstructs polymer dynamic cooperativity, revealing a monotonic trend between hierarchical structural dynamics and electronic‐state fluctuations. This strategy shifts collective motions into localized fluctuations, suppressing fluctuation‐assisted carrier transport and enhancing insulation stability. Consequently, furan‐modified polymers achieve a discharged energy density of 8.38 J cm−3 at 120°C while maintaining over 90% efficiency.








ABSTRACT
Linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics show increased conduction loss at elevated temperatures as thermally activated structural fluctuations modulate electronic states and facilitate charge transport. We examine how aromatic side groups with different π‐electron delocalization affect structural dynamic cooperativity and charge transport. Side‐group modification alters intermolecular interactions and local dynamic constraints, shifting long‐range cooperative motion to localized heterogeneous fluctuations. This transition coincides with reduced collective structural fluctuations and improved local electronic‐state stability, consistent with suppressed phonon‐assisted carrier transport. As a result, the furan‐modified polymer exhibits a statistical electronic energy fluctuation descriptor of 0.132 eV and nearly two orders of magnitude higher volume resistivity. It achieves a discharged energy density of 8.38 J cm−3 at 120°C, approximately 45 times that of pristine polymer while maintaining a charge‐discharge efficiency above 90%. It also retains an efficiency above 93% over 5 × 105 charge‐discharge cycles at 200 MV m−1. Although the higher glass transition temperature of the furan‐modified polymer may also contribute to its performance near 120°C, its advantage is already evident at 25°C and 80°C, well below the glass‐transition regime. This work highlights structural dynamic cooperativity as a descriptor linking molecular dynamics and charge transport in linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics.
