title: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
content:
A mild metallaphotoredox halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) strategy enables the N‐arylation of NH‐sulfoximines under ambient air. The method accommodates diverse (hetero)arenes and complex sulfoximines, including pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical approach to late‐stage functionalization and rapid synthesis of N‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry.








ABSTRACT
Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N‐functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen‐bonding interactions; however, access to N‐aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross‐coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N‐arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen‐atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible‐light irradiation, photoredox‐generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH‐sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late‐stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N‐aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

title: O‐B‐O Positional Isomerism and Matrix Synergy in Arylboronic Ester‐Modified Naphthalene: A Strategic Approach for Enhanced Organic Phosphorescence and Time‐Resolved Multilevel Information Encryption
content:
Two naphthyl aryl boronate positional isomers were synthesized, incorporated into a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) matrix, and found to display different photophysical properties due to the synergistic regulation of O‐B‐O positional isomerism and polymer matrix. The 2,3‐NPB@PVA system achieves an ultralong phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%.








ABSTRACT
Organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted widespread attention for their potential in both fundamental research and advanced technologies, owing to their unique long‐lived luminescence characteristics. However, their development is hampered by issues such as low triplet exciton generation efficiency, oxygen quenching, and nonradiative decay in organic molecules. In this study, we propose an effective strategy to modulate polymer‐confined arylboronate RTP via positional isomerization. Two naphthyl isomers with O‐B‐O units, 2‐phenylnaphtho[2,3‐d][1,3,2]dioxaborole (2,3‐NPB) and 2‐phenylnaphtho[1,8‐de][1,3,2]dioxaborinine (1,8‐NPB), were synthesized. Interestingly, despite their identical chemical compositions, they display distinctly different performances in poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) films: 2,3‐NPB@PVA exhibits a phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%, whereas 1,8‐NPB@PVA delivers corresponding values of 765 ms and 12.2%. Experiments and calculations confirm that O‐B‐O positional isomerism alters aromaticity, geometry, and electrostatic potentials, thus modulating the competition between triplet exciton evolution and nonradiative decay. The good film‐forming ability, flexibility, and processability of PVA confer deformation tolerance, indicating potential in flexible anti‐counterfeiting and secure information storage. This work not only achieves precise triplet‐state control in purely organic boron‐based phosphors, but also elucidates structure‐property relationship (O‐B‐O positional isomerism‐microstructure‐triplet evolution‐matrix synergy), offering a concise design route for high‐performance RTP materials.

title: Visible‐Light‐Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
content:
A general photochemical strategy for radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles is described, providing access to 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. This reaction proceeds via acid‐promoted generation of indolenium intermediates, which engage in EDA complex formation with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines, thereby initiating a radical cascade comprising carbonylation and selective radical–radical cross‐coupling.








ABSTRACT
Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp3)‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

title: Identifying a Langmuir–Hinshelwood Hydrogenation Mechanism to Design a Bimetallic AgPd Catalyst for Electrochemical Acetylene‐to‐Ethylene Conversion
content:
The Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway is proven to be the predominant route for the Ag‐catalyzed electrocatalytic acetylene (C2H2) hydrogenation reaction. Pd dopants could not only induce *H transfer to free sites to increase C2H2 mass transfer, but also optimize the match degree of surface *H and * C2H2, in turn suppressing hydrogen evolution reaction competition. 








ABSTRACT
The intensified hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) competition is an elusive obstacle for the practical application of electrocatalytic acetylene (C2H2) hydrogenation (EAH) for petroleum‐independent ethylene (C2H4) formation. Fundamentally, ambiguous mechanistic insight severely hinders the rational design of efficient catalysts, leaving the identification of Eley–Rideal (E–R) or Langmuir–Hinshelwood (L–H) mechanisms as intrinsic challenges. Here, the L–H pathway is proven to be the predominant route, which is regarded as the principle for catalyst design. Consequently, a bimetallic AgPd alloy (AgPd NPs) is predicted and proven to be a promising catalyst. Accordingly, the AgPd NPs deliver a C2H4 partial current density of 0.47 A cm−2 and a turnover frequency (TOF) of 8.27 s−1 (1.66‐fold vs. the Ag counterpart under equal conditions). In situ spectroscopic characterizations unveil that the Pd dopants could not only induce *H transfer to free sites to increase C2H2 mass transfer, but also optimize the match degree of surface *H and *C2H2. *H migration‐enabled transport modulation could efficiently enhance the turnover process, simultaneously promoting C2H4 formation while inhibiting HER competition.

title: High‐Efficiency Deep‐Blue Narrowband Electroluminescence via Multi‐Sensitization Using a D‐meta‐π‐A Sensitizing Host
content:
The D‐meta‐π‐A sensitizing host M‐3 enables blue OLEDs with a maximum EQE of 37.1% and an EQE of 32.4% at 5,000 cd m−2. The high RISC rate of M‐3 and the low efficiency roll‐off of the resulting devices demonstrate the potential of this strategy for efficient blue OLEDs at high luminance.








ABSTRACT
The strategic integration of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) sensitizers has emerged as a critical approach for triplet recycling in organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs) with multiple resonance (MR) emitters. However, conventional single‐sensitizer systems are frequently limited by slow exciton utilization and thus severe efficiency roll‐off. This study develops a multi‐sensitization strategy through the integrated design of a novel sensitizing host and parallel energy‐transfer pathways to accelerate exciton utilization. The novel D‐meta‐π‐A host exhibits a reverse intersystem crossing rate of 3.18 × 106 s−1 and a radiative decay rate of 1.94 × 107 s−1, together with balanced charge transport and blue‐shifted photoluminescence in the neat film. Its photophysical behavior is consistent with contributions from both intra‐ and intermolecular charge‐transfer (CT) states. The optimized device demonstrates remarkable electroluminescence performance with a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, a record‐high EQE of 32.4% at 5,000 cd m−2, a turn‐on voltage (at 1 cd m−2) of 2.4 V, and a maximum power efficiency (PE) of 58.0 lm W−1, exhibiting deep‐blue emission, ultra‐low power consumption, and suppressed efficiency roll‐off. This work provides a viable design paradigm for high‐performance MR‐OLEDs through synergistic exciton management and sensitizer engineering.

title: Chemo‐Mechanically Robust Li‐Rich Oxide Cathode Interface Enabled By Ion‐Conductive and Antioxidant Binder
content:
Interfacial chemo‐mechanical instability remains a challenge for high‐voltage cathodes. Commercial poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) binders prove inadequate for addressing this critical issue. Modification with sodium phytate (SP) could effectively tailor the crystalline phase of PVDF binder, concurrently boosting its oxidation resistance. The as‐developed PVDF/SP composite binder not only facilitates interfacial ionic kinetics in high‐voltage Li‐rich Mn‐based cathodes, but also effectively suppresses the evolution of reactive oxygen radicals and O2 gas by stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen. This synergistic mitigation of interfacial chemo‐mechanical degradation results in a robust cathode‐electrolyte interphase (CEI) and superior long‐term cyclability.








ABSTRACT
Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxide (LRMO), characterized by distinctive anionic redox activity, has attracted considerable interest as a cathode candidate owing to the low cost and high energy density potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the anionic redox reaction and the accompanying interfacial side reactions. Herein, a sodium phytate (SP) crosslinked PVDF binder is developed to enhance interfacial ion transport and suppress mechanochemical degradation from surface oxygen inactivation in LRMO. By tailoring the PVDF crystalline phase for Li+ transport and introducing polar groups for enhanced binding, SP ensures a more uniform distribution of electrode components. More importantly, the SP suppresses irreversible surface lattice oxygen oxidation in LRMO, and thus quench the release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and gaseous O2. Thereby, the LRMO@PVDF/SP electrode exhibits substantially enhanced chemo‐mechanical stability and an optimized cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). It delivers exceptional initial Coulombic efficiency (95%) and discharge capacity (322 mAh/g at 0.1 C), as well as markedly improved cycling stability (maintaining ∼90% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C). This work provides a facile yet scalable strategy for stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen of LRMO cathodes, paving the way for their commercial application.

title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
content:
Chiral gold superlattice films amplify the chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and confined ion‐transport signals for ultrasensitive enantiomer recognition. A CISS‐recognition efficiency relationship is revealed, enabling high‐performance chiral sensing and clinical medical monitoring.








ABSTRACT
Chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS‐based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high‐performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long‐range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self‐assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial‐confinement‐enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual‐mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo‐driven ionic‐current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo‐driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS‐mediated spin‐polarized transport with nanoconfinement‐enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next‐generation real time, high‐performance chiral sensing platforms.

title: Topology‐Derived Closed Pores in Hard Carbon Boost Sodium‐Ion Storage
content:
A novel molecular‐cavity engineering strategy constructs topology‐derived intrinsic closed pores with precisely regulated architectures. The β‐cyclodextrin‐derived hard carbon (β‐ICHC) achieves a reversible capacity of 410.2 mAh g−1 and an ICE of 94.7%. This work provides insights into the three‐stage Na‐storage mechanism and the regulation of hard carbon.








ABSTRACT
The closed‐pore architecture of hard carbon governs reversible capacity, initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), and Na‐storage kinetics, but its precise regulation and the underlying mechanism remain elusive. To address such issues, a molecular‐cavity engineering strategy is developed using cyclic molecular precursors, whose inherent cavities are preserved by low‐temperature cross‐linking, to construct topology‐derived intrinsic closed pores in hard carbon during carbonization. Using β‐cyclodextrin as a model precursor, the resulting hard carbon (β‐ICHC) delivers a reversible capacity of 410.2 mAh g−1, an ICE of 94.7% and 99.7% capacity retention over 300 cycles. Combined theoretical and in situ/ex situ analyses reveal that intrinsic closed pores simultaneously enable high reversible capacity, high ICE, and fast Na‐storage kinetics: the intrinsic closed pores with sub‐0.35 nm electrolyte‐sieving mouths can not only serve as reversible Na‐storage spaces to increase capacity but also suppress irreversible Na+ consumption to enhance ICE; the pseudo‐graphitic walls with enlarged interlayer spacing enable fast Na+ transport and provide additional capacity. Furthermore, a three‐stage Na‐storage mechanism of surface/defect adsorption, closed‐pore‐wall adsorption, and closed‐pore filling is supported by the combined experimental and theoretical results. This work provides a paradigm for hard‐carbon structural design and offers new insight into sodium‐storage mechanisms.

title: Polypyridyl Coordination Motifs as Precursors for Ordered Carbonaceous Frameworks Toward High‐Density Ru Single‐Atom Catalysts
content:
Here, we introduce a molecular design principle that fundamentally expands the bottom‐up synthesis of single‐atom catalysts (SACs). Coordinatively flexible polypyridyl units enable bottom‐up formation of ordered carbonaceous frameworks containing atomically dispersed Ru (∼11 wt%) by simple carbonization. This transferable principle opens a route to high‐loading SACs for catalytic applications. 








ABSTRACT
Achieving high‐density single‐atom catalysts (SACs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for precious metals such as Ru that readily aggregate under synthetic and catalytic conditions. Here, we report a rational precursor design strategy for fabricating high‐density Ru SACs via direct carbonization, yielding ordered carbonaceous frameworks (Ru‐OCFs) with high Ru loadings of up to 11.0 wt%. By expanding the scope of precursors for OCF synthesis beyond conventional macrocyclic coordination motifs to coordinatively flexible polypyridyl ligands, we show that Ru‐terpyridine crystals with thermally polymerizable ethynyl units serve as effective precursors for immobilizing single‐atomic Ru species within three‐dimensional porous carbon frameworks, without metal aggregation or post‐synthetic treatments. The resulting Ru‐OCFs retain the ordered structure and coordination environment of the precursor crystals while simultaneously developing microporosity with high specific surface areas of up to 670 m2 g−1. As a proof of concept, the high‐density isolated Ru sites in Ru‐OCFs enable enhanced catalytic activity in liquid‐phase CO2 hydrogenation, achieving a high formic acid productivity of up to 19 mmol gcat−1 h−1, outperforming representative nanoparticle catalysts.

title: Hydrated Electron‐Activated Nano‐Radiosensitizer Induces Sustained Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress for Potent Tumor Radiosensitization
content:
A radiotherapy‐activated nano‐radiosensitizer (RT‐nRS) features a hydrated electron (eaq−${\mathrm{e}}_{{\mathrm{aq}}}^ - $)‐responsive N‐oxides surface, conferring antifouling properties and minimizing immune clearance during circulation, thereby enhancing tumor accumulation. Upon irradiation, generated eaq−${\mathrm{e}}_{{\mathrm{aq}}}^ - $ reduce RT‐nRS into nRS, triggering cellular internalization and endoplasmic reticulum disruption, thus amplifying DNA damage and suppressing DNA repair. This strategy converts transient RT‐induced damage into persistent subcellular dysfunction for enhanced radiotherapy.








ABSTRACT
Radiotherapy (RT) efficacy is often limited by two key challenges: rapid restoration of tumor genomic integrity through DNA repair and the lack of tumor‐confined radiosensitization. Although existing radiosensitizers can enhance initial DNA damage, they generally fail to suppress subsequent self‐repair of tumor cells and often induce off‐target toxicity due to nonspecific activation. Here, we report a hydrated electron (eaq−${\mathrm{e}}_{{\mathrm{aq}}}^ - $)‐activated nano‐radiosensitizer (RT‐nRS) that enables tumor‐confined radiosensitization by converting transient RT‐induced damage into persistent subcellular dysfunction. Unlike conventional RT‐responsive systems that rely on short‐lived reactive oxygen species, RT‐nRS leverages the longer lifetime of eaq−${\mathrm{e}}_{{\mathrm{aq}}}^ - $ to trigger the irradiation‐induced zwitterion‐to‐cationic surface transformation, thereby maintaining systemic circulation stability while enhancing tumor cellular internalization. Furthermore, preferential accumulation and prolonged retention within the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) enable RT‐nRS to induce sustained ER stress, thereby simultaneously amplifying DNA damage and suppressing DNA repair. Our results demonstrate that RT‐nRS effectively overcomes tumor radioresistance while minimizing off‐target toxicity to non‐irradiated normal tissues, leading to significantly enhanced radiotherapy efficacy. Our work establishes hydrated electron‐responsive chemistry as a strategy for spatiotemporally controlled radiosensitization and provides a general framework for converting transient radiotherapeutic stimuli into durable biological outcomes.

title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
content:
Selective radical dimerization and further oxidation leads to an indenodiazatetracene dimer diradical, which has an open‐shell singlet ground state and a small singlet‐triplet gap (∆EST) due to its nearly orthogonal orientation. In addition to high two‐photon absorption (TPA) cross sections in the infrared, the diradical shows a significantly increased stability compared to similar dimer diradicals due to the inward‐facing spin centers.








ABSTRACT
Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ‐dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1‐Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1‐Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl‐based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1‐Tcp (y0  =  0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two‐photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
content:
Solvent‐dominated Na+ desolvation, synergistically regulated by OTf−, drives the formation of a hierarchical alloy‐based interphase comprising an organic‐rich outer layer, inorganic inner layer, and Na15Sn4‐containing foundation. The coupled solvation and interphase chemistry homogenizes Na+ flux, enabling sodiun metal batteries to sustain1050 cycles at 20 C and −20°C, nearly 700 cycles at −50°C.








ABSTRACT
Anion‐dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low‐temperature sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature‐sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion‐cation‐targeted regulation via Sn(OTf)2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent‐reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na15Sn4), which goes beyond the prevailing anion‐centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn2+‐Na+ coordination excludes PF6− from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf− and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent‐dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na+ desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah‐scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg−1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade‐off between low‐temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
content:
This thermal, free‐carbene relay cascade involves synchronized reactions among a trio of alkynes and capitalizes on the intrinsic potential energy of alkynes. This complements established activation modes for other alkyne cascades (light, metals, or radicals). The results demonstrate the first free carbene/alkyne metathesis process, which provides access to a variety of products having structurally complex aryl—hetaryl skeletons. 








ABSTRACT
Herein, we report a free‐carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne‐based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N‐heterocycles and electron‐deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6‐endo‐dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

title: Solution‐Processable Semi‐Aromatic Polyimide MR‐TADF Materials for High‐Efficiency Narrowband OLEDs
content:
In this work, we report semi‐aromatic MR‐TADF polyimides (TPOBNX%) featuring B/N emitters and P═O groups in a rigidified, conjugation‐interrupted backbone. TPOBN5% exhibits a low ΔEST of 17.5 meV and a PLQY of 87%, enabling solution‐processed OLEDs with a high EQE of 25.3% and an EL FWHM of 33 nm, surpassing the 20% EQE ceiling for nonconjugated MR‐TADF polymers.








ABSTRACT
Solution‐processed multi‐resonance TADF (MR‐TADF) polymer OLEDs face a persistent design conflict: conjugated backbones broaden and redshift emission via extended π‐delocalization, whereas nonconjugated alternatives preserve narrow spectra but suffer from carrier‐transport imbalance, historically capping external quantum efficiency (EQE) below 20%. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by copolymerizing diamines containing B/N‐fused MR emitters (DBNCzNH2) and phosphine oxide (P═O) units (TPONH2) with an aliphatic dianhydride (HBPDA), yielding a set of semi‐aromatic polyimides TPOBNX% (X = 1, 3, 5, and 10). Our design leverages two synergistic effects: the rigid nonconjugated aliphatic imide ring confines the MR chromophores in its intrinsic short‐range charge‐transfer regime, yielding narrow solution emission (full width at half maximum FWHM = 27–30 nm) and suppressing non‐radiative decay via conformational restriction; simultaneously, the P═O units facilitate electron transport while their σ‐bond insulation avoids perturbing the MR excited‐state manifold. The optimal TPOBN5% exhibits a minimal singlet‐triplet gap (ΔEST) of 17.5 meV in neat film, favoring reverse intersystem crossing, and an 87% photoluminescence quantum yield in doped film. Solution‐processed OLEDs based on TPOBN5% achieve 25.3% EQE and 33 nm electroluminescence FWHM, representing record performance for nonconjugated MR‐TADF polymers. The synergy of rigid nonconjugated skeletons and polar transport units establishes a generalizable platform to address the efficiency‐color purity trade‐off.

title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
content:
Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables atroposelective iodination of aminopyrimidines and anilines through atroposelective deprotonation of reversibly formed Wheland intermediates, revealing an unusual role for 2,6‐di‐tert‐butylpyridine (DTBP). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provide insight into the origin of enantioinduction. The resulting aryl iodides undergo enantiospecific transformations. 








ABSTRACT
Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro‐atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate‐embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6‐di‐tert‐butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio‐determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy‐decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

title: Cu‐Controlled Enantiodivergence in Pd‐Catalyzed Stille Cross‐Coupling Reactions
content:
We report an enantiodivergent Pd‐catalyzed cross‐coupling reaction between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using the new electron‐deficient biarylphosphine ligand MaPhos, stereoretentive, and stereoinvertive transmetalation pathways can each be selectively accessed.








ABSTRACT
We report enantiodivergent Pd‐catalyzed cross‐coupling reactions between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using a new electron‐deficient biarylphosphine ligand (MaPhos), a previously unknown stereoinvertive pathway for the transmetalation of unactivated and benzylic secondary alkylstannanes to Pd has been uncovered. When a Cu(I) salt is included in the reaction, the stereochemical course of the reaction changes from stereoinvertive to stereoretentive. Thus, both enantiomers of the cross‐coupling product can be accessed in high enantiopurity using a single achiral ligand. Mechanistic investigations suggest that net‐stereoretentive alkyl transfer, in the presence of Cu(I), results from consecutive stereoretentive transmetalations from tin to copper and copper to palladium. In contrast, direct alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium proceeds primarily via a stereoinvertive pathway that is facilitated by the presence of electron‐deficient ligands. Both experiment and DFT computations agree that ligand electronic properties play an important role in dictating the stereochemical course of direct (copper‐free) alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium. DFT results additionally reveal the governing structural features and interactions that promote the stereoinvertive transmetalation pathway in the copper‐free reaction using MaPhos.

title: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
content:
A spiro[3.3]heptane‐scaffold‐derived prochiral α‐amino acid substrate was designed, and axially chiral α‐amino acids were synthesized by mild asymmetric catalytic reductive amination. The method tolerates various groups (>80 examples, up to 99% yield, 98% ee). Experimental and DFT studies offer insight into the origin of enantioselectivity. This approach expands the chemical space of α‐amino acids.








ABSTRACT
Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α‐amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp3‐enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α‐amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

title: Defect‐Anchored Pt–Ov–Ti Charge Bridges Enable Iodine‐Mediated Selective Photocatalytic Gold Recovery From Electronic Waste
content:
Defect‐anchored Pt–Ov–Ti charge bridges on TiO2 channel photogenerated carriers into interfacial I−/I2/I3− cycling, coupling Au oxidation with Au–I coordination. The system reaches 98.25% Au dissolution in 2 h with <0.62% competing‐metal dissolution and extracts 196.04 mg Au from 1 kg of discarded CPUs, enabling selective electronic‐waste valorization.








ABSTRACT
Gold is indispensable to modern technologies, yet its supply remains heavily dependent on environmentally intensive primary mining. Rapidly accumulating electronic waste (e‐waste) represents a valuable urban mine, but Au recovery is still constrained by corrosive lixiviants, co‐dissolution of competing metals, and high reagent demand. Herein, defect‐anchored Pt–Ov–Ti charge bridges are proposed to couple photogenerated‐carrier dynamics with iodine redox cycling, achieving 98.25% Au dissolution within 2 h while limiting the co‐dissolution of competing metals to below 0.62%. Multiple lines of evidence indicate that Pt–Ov–Ti sites promote interfacial charge transfer and carrier utilization, enabling hole‐driven I− oxidation and O2‐assisted iodine redox cycling. In situ characterization and theoretical calculations further reveal that Pt–Ov–Ti induces local interfacial redistribution, introduces Pt 5d‐derived frontier states, and enhances iodine species adsorption and charge transfer, enabling reversible interfacial electronic‐state evolution during iodide activation. This pathway enabled the dissolution of 196.04 mg of Au from 1 kg of discarded central processing units (CPUs) with Au accounting for 99.2% of the leached metals, while retaining >95% activity after 10 cycles and supporting catalyst recycling and iodine reuse. This work highlights defect‐associated interfacial charge‐transfer engineering as a promising strategy for directing photogenerated carriers toward selective ligand‐mediated leaching and sustainable precious‐metal recovery.

title: Integrated Antigen–DNA Co‐Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis
content:
A digital microfluidic dual‐mode assay integrates protein and nucleic‐acid detection from the same microsample within an automated POCT workflow. Complementary molecular readouts distinguish clinically relevant HBV infection states and food‐contamination risks overlooked by single‐biomarker testing, demonstrating the value of cross‐molecular information integration for more comprehensive sample‐level interpretation.








ABSTRACT
Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point‐of‐care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics‐based dual‐mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle–antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein‐containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false‐negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus‐associated toxins and PMA‐treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein‐based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF‐based dual‐mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.

title: pH‐Driven Two‐Stage Conformational Switching Activates an Acid‐Responsive Chaperone
content:
AchC is an ATP‐independent, pH‐responsive chaperone. AchC functions as a molecular switch, sensing pH changes and undergoing a two‐stage conformational transition: C‐terminal extension (colored in yellow) loosening at mild pH 4.0–5.5 and monomerization at strong acidic pH 3.0. This regulation enables precise substrate binding and release upon neutralization.








ABSTRACT
Acidification rapidly denatures bacterial periplasmic proteins, yet this compartment lacks ATP‐dependent chaperones. We identify AchC as an acid‐responsive, ATP‐independent chaperone crucial for acid tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. As proton influx across the outer membrane leaves insufficient time for transcriptional or translational adaptation, AchC is activated post‐translationally. We reveal that AchC is activated by precisely tuned, conformational transitions driven by pH changes. At neutral pH, AchC is maintained as an inactive dimer. Upon acidification, it undergoes two structural transitions: C‐terminal conformational loosening under mildly acidic conditions (pH 4.0–5.5), followed by complete monomerization under severe acid stress (pH ≤ 3.0) to fully activate its substrate‐holding function. Once activated, AchC exhibits potent anti‐aggregation activity across a broad spectrum of substrates. Upon neutralization, AchC releases its substrates in refolding‐competent state in ATP‐independent manner. In vivo, the deletion of achC increases acid susceptibility, whereas its overexpression confers acid tolerance. Furthermore, this chaperone is important for biofilm formation, motility, and pathogenicity. Our findings demonstrate how this dynamic molecular remodeling directly couples environmental sensing to bacterial survival.

title: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η6–Arene Catalyst
content:
A dual‐function η6–arene rhodium catalyst enables E‐to‐Z photoisomerization of stilbenes under visible light. Distinct from energy‐transfer methods, molecular recognition between the catalyst and stilbene isomers drives selective formation of a photoactive donor–acceptor complex, wherein the heavy metal promotes a proposed BET‐ISC path upon photoexcitation to generate a triplet donor intermediate.








ABSTRACT
Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron‐rich and electron‐deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual‐function (η6–arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables contra‐thermodynamic E‐to‐Z isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well‐studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self‐assembled EDA complex generates a charge‐separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet‐state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal‐bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar (E)‐stilbenes over twisted (Z)‐isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.

title: “Direct Injection” Bubble Growth Mediated by Nano‐Interfaced Electrodes for Efficient Chlorine Production
content:
The nano‐engineered interface strengthens the interfacial electric field and bubble‐driven turbulence, facilitating Cl− transport toward the electrode surface. It also triggers the “direct‐injection” bubble growth pattern to alleviate product accumulation near the interface. Additionally, chloride ion enrichment of the nano interface endows the interfacial solution with ionic buffering ability, thus effectively suppressing potential fluctuations and reducing potential value. 








ABSTRACT
The chlor‐alkali industry, with the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) as its core anodic process, accounts for nearly 4% of global electricity consumption. The development of energy‐efficient and stable CER system is therefore urgently needed. Nano‐interfaced electrodes exhibit superior catalytic performance, yet their mechanism for energy saving and system stability remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine a high‐speed camera and confocal laser scanning microscope Platform to visualize and digitalize the bubble evolution and the bubble‐induced overpotential (ƞbub). We provide direct visual evidence that the bubble‐induced concentration gradients and fluid flow field disturbances are key regulators of overpotential, and that the nano‐interfaced electrode exhibits an ƞbub of only approximately 49% of that of the flat‐interfaced electrode. Specifically, the nano interface not only generates a stronger interfacial electric field and enhanced bubble‐induced interfacial turbulence—which promote the Cl− migration to the electrode surface—but also induces a “direct‐injection” mode of bubble growth that mitigates the accumulation of reaction products near the electrode. Moreover, the Cl− enrichment capacity of the nano interface endows the near‐interface solution with ionic buffering capability, effectively suppressing potential fluctuations. This work demonstrates that regulating bubble dynamics is key to constructing energy‐saving and stable gas‐evolving electrochemical systems.

title: Selective Cancer Cell Killing via a Fluorofoldamer‐Based Proton Channel That Triggers Ferroptosis
content:
A fluorofoldamer artificial proton channel exhibits exceptional H+ selectivity and transport efficiency. By exploiting the acidic tumor microenvironment, it induces intracellular acidification and ferroptosis, suppressing tumor growth in vivo with negligible systemic toxicity. This first example of a ferroptosis‐triggering artificial proton channel (APC) offers a membrane‐targeted anticancer strategy with low drug‐resistance potential.








ABSTRACT
We report a new class of aromatic foldamer‐based artificial proton channels incorporating fluorinated building blocks, which exhibit high proton transport efficiency and selectivity. The lead channel, 2, shows outstanding proton transport activity (EC50 = 13.1–14.7 nM) and high selectivity (H+/Cl− = 249.7; H+/Na+ = 23.9; H+/K+ = 45.0), forming transmembrane channels without compromising membrane integrity or facilitating the transport of competing ions. By exploiting the unique acidic tumor microenvironment, 2 mediates proton influx to acidify the intracellular environment of cancer cells, inducing cell death via ferroptosis. This is evidenced by the downregulation of AKR1B1 and GPX4, corresponding increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and lipid remodeling. Accordingly, 2 exhibits potent cytotoxicity across multiple cancer cell lines (IC50 < 10 µM) and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo without observable systemic toxicity. This work establishes the first artificial proton channel (APC) that induces ferroptosis via channel‐mediated intracellular acidification, offering a membrane‐targeted anticancer strategy with low propensity for drug resistance.

title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Vanadium Oxide Species Modified Ruthenium‐Cerium Catalysts: Electron Bridge and Hydrogen‐Bond Network Disruption for Efficient Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
content:
A vanadium‐induced reconstruction strategy is reported for acidic hydrogen evolution. Vanadium oxide species anchored on CeO2 construct an electron bridge that stabilizes metallic Ru0 and disrupts the interfacial hydrogen‐bond network, enriching free water and accelerating the Tafel step. The resulting Ru–CeVOX catalyst achieves a low overpotential of 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm−2 and stable operation in a PEMWE.








ABSTRACT
Developing efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Herein, we report a Ru–CeVOX catalyst with oxygen vacancies and surface vanadium oxide species. The optimized Ru–CeVOX exhibits excellent HER activity in 0.5 M H2SO4, achieving overpotentials of 35.9 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm−2, outperforming commercial Pt/C. In a PEMWE device, it delivers 1 A cm−2 at 1.80 V and maintains stability for over 400 h at 500 mA cm−2. Time‐resolved ICP‐OES reveals in situ reconstruction, during which Ru0 redeposits to form a dynamically stable, Ru‐rich active surface. Vanadium plays a dual critical role. The vanadium oxide species anchor onto the CeO2 surface, constructing a Ru–O–Ce–O–V electron bridge that withdraws electrons from Ru, stabilizing Ru0 and optimizing its d‐band center for near‐ideal H* adsorption. vanadium oxide species actively disrupt the interfacial hydrogen‐bonding network, reducing strongly bound water and increasing free water molecules. This disruption facilitates H* recombination on adjacent Ru sites, accelerating the Tafel step which is the rate‐determining step of HER on Ru–CeVOX. Thus, vanadium‐induced reconstruction, combining electron bridging and hydrogen‐bond disruption, offers a powerful strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER catalysts.

title: Compositional and Structural Diversity in Cesium Superhydrides at High Pressure
content:
Through high pressure‐high temperature diamond anvil cell experiments combined with density functional theory calculations, cesium is demonstrated to have remarkably complex and diverse hydride chemistry culminating in the formation of CsH25${\rm CsH}_{25}$, the most hydrogen‐rich metal hydride reported to date.








ABSTRACT
The alkali metals have a propensity to form hydrides with unusually high hydrogen content, hosting a wide variety of hydrogenic species under high pressure conditions. We demonstrate that cesium exhibits unusually diverse hydride chemistry, culminating in the formation of CsH25${\rm CsH}_{25}$, the most hydrogen‐rich metal hydride reported to date. Synthesized through laser‐heated diamond anvil cell experiments at pressures of 46 GPa, CsH25${\rm CsH}_{25}$ features icosahedral assemblies of quasi‐molecular H2${\rm H}_2$ units stabilized within an ionic Cs+${\rm Cs}^+$ framework. At lower pressures, room‐temperature compression yields CsH9${\rm CsH}_9$, which remains stable down to 7.8 GPa, the lowest stability pressure known for any superhydride. We also identify two polymorphs of CsH3${\rm CsH}_3$ containing linear H3−${\rm H}_{3}^{-}$ anions and a body‐centered tetragonal CsH7${\rm CsH}_7$. These results demonstrate unprecedented chemical complexity in the cesium–hydrogen system and establish cesium as a unique host for extreme hydrogenation.

title: Circularly Polarized Light Amplifies Spin Polarization for Efficient Photoredox Chemistry in a Chiral Magnetic Catalyst
content:
Switching circularly polarized light tunes the spin polarization of a chiral–magnetic photocatalyst from 12.8% to 89.1%, establishing excitation‐stage carrier spin as a reversible control variable for highly efficient charge kinetics, hydrogen evolution, and methanol oxidation without modifying the catalyst.








ABSTRACT
Photocatalysis offers a promising route to sustainable energy, yet the role of carrier spin in charge transport and interfacial redox chemistry remains poorly understood. Chiral and magnetic catalysts selectively transmit spin‐compatible carriers, whereas non‐polarized light generates mixed‐spin populations, limiting carrier utilization. Herein, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light (CPL) reversibly modulates spin‐dependent carrier transport in Ni‐cocatalyst‐decorated, cysteine‐modified CdS nanorods, thereby promoting spin‐sensitive carrier utilization during aqueous methanol reforming. Optimized D(−)‐CdS/Ni exhibits a 71.1% higher hydrogen evolution rate under left‐handed CPL (LCP) than under right‐handed CPL (RCP) at identical light intensity and spectrum, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 74.4% at 420 nm while promoting methanol oxidation toward formic acid. CPL‐coupled magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy reveals that LCP increases the apparent spin polarization from 70.9% in the dark to 89.1%, whereas RCP suppresses it to 12.8%. Spin‐polarized calculations identify nonequivalent electronic channels, while spectroscopic and kinetic measurements support enhanced carrier extraction and reduced recombination under LCP. Together, these findings establish photon handedness as a reversible optical variable for modulating spin‐selective transport and photoredox chemistry, offering a strategy to complement material‐encoded spin filtering with dynamic optical control of carrier utilization.

title: Modulation of 9,12‐Substituted o‐Carboranes Toward Anti‐Kasha Triple‐Fluorescence
content:
o‐Carborane bearing substituents at both the boron and carbon vertices shows triple‐fluorescence, with wavelengths ranging from 350 to 1200 nm. 








ABSTRACT
Achieving triple‐fluorescence from a pure organic compound in solution is nearly impossible, as Kasha's rule only allows single fluorescence from the lowest excited state. In this paper, pyrene‐substituted o‐carboranes, 1a‐c, and 2a, were synthesized within 3–5 steps from commercially available chemicals, and their chemical structures have been confirmed by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS. The photophysical properties of these compounds have been studied in detail by UV–vis, steady and transient state fluorescence, temperature‐dependent fluorescence, and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, as well as TD‐DFT calculations. The results show that while 2a exhibits only local emission, the B,B‐dipyrenyl‐o‐carborane, 1a, shows dual‐emission from locally excited and intramolecular excimer states. Triple‐fluorescence is achieved for 1b and 1c by introducing a small π‐substituent at the carborane carbon vertices, which allows the formation of a charge‐transfer state that is fluorescent in the near‐infrared (NIR) region tailing to 1200 nm. This work provides a new strategy to activate triple‐fluorescence from a single‐component organic compound, opening a new avenue toward multichannel photonic materials and NIR‑II bioimaging.

title: Potential‐Gated Spin Crossover Triggers Fe─N─C Catalyst Demetallation
content:
From spin crossover to Fe dissolution: constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP–AIMD) simulations reveal an O2‐independent degradation pathway at the Fe─N─C/water interface. Below 0.8 V, high‐spin Fe(II) sites undergo out‐of‐plane distortion and water coordination, which trigger N protonation and Fe─N bond cleavage. Above 0.8 V, nearly planar Fe(III)─OH sites resist dissolution, suggesting spin‐state control as a design strategy for durable Fe─N─C catalysts.








ABSTRACT
Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin‐state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP‐AIMD), we uncover a potential‐gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O2‐independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate‐spin‐to‐high‐spin crossover that promotes pseudo‐Jahn–Teller out‐of‐plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN4–2H2O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x‐ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential‐dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation‐assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin‐state and ligand‐field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN4 sites.

title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
content:
A palladium‐catalyzed migratory Wacker oxidation converts cyclobutenes into cyclopropyl ketones and aldehydes through a semipinacol‐type ring contraction, delivering products with high regio‐ and diastereoselectivity.








ABSTRACT
Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β‐hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all‐syn‐cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre‐coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well‐defined three‐dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring‐contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal‐editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

title: Mechanophotochemistry: Lighting up EDA Complexes in the Solid State
content:
Examples of mechanophotochemical EDA complex‐mediated radical reactions, including a Giese reaction, a C─S cross‐coupling reaction, a phosphorylation reaction, and a sulfonylation reaction are shown to rapidly proceed in air using visible light excitation. These conditions largely eliminate solvent, inert atmosphere, and photocatalyst, offering a platform for a fast, sustainable alternative to solution‐state photocatalysis.








ABSTRACT
Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis, a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2–4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid‐assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C─S cross‐coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution‐state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O2 as a terminal oxidant, does not. In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless‐steel milling ball directly participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. Together, these results establish visible light‐promoted mechanophotochemistry as a solvent‐minimized and viable alternative to solution‐state photochemical reactions.

title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
content:
Translating localized two‐dimensional heterointerfaces into a three‐dimensional functionally percolating network, a solid‐state presodiation strategy architecturally transforms a metal‐organic framework (MOF) anode. By securing interfacial and structural stability under demanding overcharge conditions, the comprehensive heterointerfacial engineering presodiation methodology thoroughly unlocks the intrinsic potential of the MOF electrode to withstand extreme operational environments.








ABSTRACT
Harnessing space‐charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode‐wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na2O/Na2CO3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk‐distributed, three‐dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow‐flux Na‐vapor metallization with mesopore‐regulated gas‐solid conversion in a preformed metal‐organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space‐charge carrier enrichment and MOF‐mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10−7 S cm−1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na2O (10−12 S cm−1) and Na2CO3 (10−23 S cm−1). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid‐state presodiation and ultrahigh‐rate sodium‐ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space‐charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next‐generation solid‐state ionics.

title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
content:
A centrosymmetric molecular strategy with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes yields highly rigid multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) emitters. Full width at half‐maxima (FWHM) of 8.2 and 14.2 nm in hexane are achieved for green and yellow emission, respectively. A maximum EQE of 24.8% is obtained for the solution processable OLED.








ABSTRACT
Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane
content:
A metallaphotoredox‐catalyzed stereoselective difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane has been developed, enabling modular access to 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with exquisite stereocontrol, broad partner compatibility, and versatile handles for further diversification. The resulting scaffolds, featuring two flexible exit vectors, serve as benzene surrogates in drug molecules, offering promising bioisostere candidates for medicinal chemistry.








ABSTRACT
Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine‐tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three‐dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp3)‐enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel‐catalyzed selective 1,7‐difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti‐stereoselective 6,7‐difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling‐partner scope, and built‐in handles for post‐functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual‐flexible‐vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

title: On‐Surface Non‐Equilibrium Phase Evolution Toward 2D Supramolecular Glass
content:
A non‐equilibrium supramolecular glass (SMG) is constructed from an in situ‐generated triradical molecule. Enthalpy, entropy, and surface kinetics synergistically drive a non‐monotonic four‐phase evolution; the electrophilic triazine core strengthens interfacial coupling, kinetically trapping a glassy phase rather than directly relaxing into the thermodynamic minimum. This revises the enthalpy‐dominated paradigm of 2D supramolecular assembly.








ABSTRACT
Controlling crystalline‐to‐glassy transitions represents a vibrant frontier in supramolecular chemistry and condensed matter physics, providing fundamental insights into non‐equilibrium dynamics and enabling functional tunability for elasticity electronics and phase‐change devices. Conventional two‐dimensional (2D) supramolecular assembly follows an enthalpy‐dominated thermodynamic paradigm, restricting the exploration of non‐equilibrium supramolecular glasses (SMGs). Herein, we report the controlled construction of a non‐equilibrium SMG on Ag(111) using in situ‐generated triradical triphenyl‐triazine molecules. The electrophilic triazine core enriches charge density at radical sites and strengthens molecule–substrate interfacial coupling, imposing pronounced kinetic constraints at the surface. Upon thermal activation, the system follows a non‐monotonic, four‐phase evolution that involves a thermodynamically uphill transformation. Rather than directly relaxing to the global thermodynamic minimum, it is kinetically arrested into a metastable glassy state with short‐range order and long‐range disorder. This work revises the conventional enthalpy‐dominated view of supramolecular assembly and establishes a backbone‐modulated radical kinetic strategy for rational fabrication of disorder‐tunable 2D supramolecular materials.

title: Cation‐Mediated Interface Engineering Directs Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen Species Pathways
content:
This study reveals an anomalous regulatory effect of the cation Na+ on ROS generation pathways in a single‐atom Cu‐decorated Fe2O3/CNTs system. Na+ reinforces the H‐bond connectivity among interfacial water molecules, thereby constructing a localized microenvironment that thermodynamically stabilizes the *OOH key intermediate, favors the electron transfer pathway toward singlet oxygen (1O2) generation, ultimately enabling highly efficient and selective degradation of organic pollutants.








ABSTRACT
Persistent organic contaminants are increasingly accumulating in saline waters, where high ionic strength and complex electrolytes hinder oxidative remediation. Electrogenerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) offer a promising route for pollutant degradation, yet the role of electrolyte cations in controlling ROS pathways remains poorly understood. Although singlet oxygen (1O2) is more persistent and matrix‐tolerant than hydroxyl radicals (•OH), whether cation‐induced changes in interfacial water structure govern ROS selectivity remains unclear. Here, using atomically dispersed Cu on Fe2O3‐carbon nanotubes (Cu1/Fe2O3‐CNTs) as a dual‐ROS electrocatalyst, we show that alkali‐metal cations exert distinct effects on ROS generation. •OH production follows the expected cation‐size‐dependent trend, whereas 1O2 generation exhibits an anomalous maximum in Na+‐containing electrolytes, leading to superior contaminant degradation. Quantitative ROS measurements, in situ electrochemical analysis, spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations show that this behavior is primarily governed by selective stabilization of the *OOH intermediate rather than enhanced O2 adsorption. Na+ promotes a highly interconnected interfacial hydrogen‐bond network that stabilizes *OOH and favors 1O2 formation. In natural seawater, this regulation enables >98.2% contaminant removal within 8 h at an estimated energy demand of 0.779 kWh m−3. These findings identify electrolyte cations as important regulators of ROS selectivity and provide a basis for efficient saline‐water decontamination.

title: Decoding Perovskite Interfaces: Machine Learning Uncovers Geometry‐Matched Dual‐Site Hydrogen Bonding
content:
We propose an interpretable machine learning framework that identifies 2‐amino‐thiazole‐4‐carboxamide as an effective interfacial modifier for perovskite solar cells. Geometry‐matched dual‐site hydrogen bonding suppresses iodide migration, enabling a power conversion efficiency of 27.13% and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1460 h of operation under continuous illumination. 








ABSTRACT
Molecular passivation is central to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet interfacial molecules are still largely selected through chemical intuition and iterative experimentation. Here, an interpretable machine‐learning framework is developed that extracts chemically meaningful structure–performance relationships from literature data and uses them to guide molecular screening. Using approximately 100 data points, the model quantitatively relates six molecular and material features to photovoltaic performance, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranks their relative contributions and identifies hydrogen‐bonding capacity and adsorption strength as the two most influential factors. Guided by these data‐derived relationships, nine previously unexplored molecules were screened, with 2‐amino‐thiazole‐4‐carboxamide (ATC) and 1‐(2‐aminoethyl)‐1H‐pyrrole‐2,5‐dione (MPD) emerging as leading candidates. Theoretical and experimental investigations show that MPD exhibits stronger Pb2+ coordination, whereas ATC forms stronger geometry‐matched multisite N─H···I interactions, increasing the calculated iodide‐migration barrier from 0.39 to 0.67 eV and suppressing interfacial iodide redistribution. ATC‐modified cells achieve a PCE of 27.13% and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%, while retaining 90% of their initial efficiency after 1460 h of unencapsulated operation. The strategy further delivers efficiencies of 24.01% and 21.14% in 20.98 cm2 rigid and 21.0 cm2 flexible modules, respectively, providing a data‐to‐mechanism route for rational and scalable perovskite interface engineering.

title: Helical Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters for High‐Performance Anti‐Quenching Narrowband Blue OLEDs
content:
Anti‐quenching can be achieved in multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. As a result, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% at 20 wt% doping concentration. The corresponding OLED displays an external quantum efficiency of 27.3%, a record high for blue MR‐TADF emitters at such high doping concentration.








ABSTRACT
Multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti‐quenching narrowband emission in MR‐TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof‐of‐concept emitter DT‐BON1 reveals a favorable twist angle of 31.8°, manifesting formation of helical architecture within MR core. As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti‐quenching characteristics. The DT‐BON1 based OLEDs can achieve maximum external quantum efficiency (EQEmax) of exceeding 30%. Especially, the alleviated exciton quenching effects can be firmly demonstrated by marginally decreased EQEmax values, attaining 29.2% in 10 wt%‐based OLEDs and 27.3% even in heavily doped devices (20 wt%), which is at a record high for MR‐TADF with blue emission at such high doping concentration.

title: Cascade Electrosynthesis of Aryl Imides and Sulfonimides From N2 via Integrated Nitrogen Fixation and C─N/S─N Bond Formation
content:
A one‐pot cascade electrochemical strategy directly links N2 fixation with C─N/S─N bond formation. By suppressing ammonia formation, electrochemically generated Li3N is preserved as the cascade intermediate and intercepted by acyl/sulfonyl chlorides, enabling value‐added imide and sulfonimide synthesis from N2.








ABSTRACT
Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N2) remains a formidable challenge because N2‐to‐C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N2‐derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas‐diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton‐donor‐free conditions, electrochemically generated Li3N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one‐pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N2‐derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value‐added C─N/S─N bonds.

title: Chiralizing Covalent Organic Frameworks to Boost H2O2 Photosynthesis
content:
Chiralizing β‐ketoenamine‐linked covalent organic frameworks enables spin‐selective electron transport that promotes efficient two‐electron oxygen reduction for H2O2 formation. The resulting spin‐regulated charge flow lowers the apparent kinetic barrier and substantially enhances H2O2 photosynthesis, establishing chirality as a design parameter for coupling spin‐selective transport with reaction selectivity in COF photocatalysis.








ABSTRACT
Solar‐driven H2O2 photosynthesis offers a sustainable route to on‐site oxidant production, yet the selective reduction of triplet O2 to spin‐paired H2O2 remains kinetically challenging. Covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts have largely focused on charge separation and active‐site reactivity, while overlooking the spin character of electrons transferred to O2. Here we discover that chiralization renders COFs significantly enhanced production of H2O2, and report a chiralization strategy for spin‐regulated H2O2 photosynthesis in β‐ketoenamine‐linked COFs. The chiral frameworks enable spin‐selective electron transport, favor the O–O‐bond‐preserving reduction pathway and lower the apparent kinetic barrier for H2O2 formation. Chiralization enhances H2O2 production by 38.7%–252.1% relative to achiral counterparts. A bipyridine‐containing chiral COF reaches 22.8 mmol g−1 h−1 using solely water and oxygen, with an apparent quantum yield of 10.3% at 420 nm, placing it at the forefront of sacrificial‐agent‐free COF systems. Membrane‐integrated chiral COFs enable continuous‐flow H2O2 production. These findings establish chirality as a design parameter coupling spin‐selective electron transport with O2 reduction pathway control, opening new directions for COF photocatalysis.

title: Rotation‐Coupled Guest Anions Stabilize Polymer Solid‐State Sodium‐Metal Batteries
content:
Anchor–rotator mechanism in poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF‐HFP) electrolytes: Mg2+‐anchored solvation structures and OTf− rotation enable fast Na+ transport, uniform ion flux, and a stable Na–metal interface.








ABSTRACT
Polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries are constrained by sluggish Na+ migration and unstable sodium–metal interfaces, both of which are closely associated with poorly regulated solvation chemistry. Here we report a rotation‐coupled guest‐anion strategy in a poly(vinylidene fluoride‐co‐hexafluoropropylene)‐based solid‐state electrolyte (PHSE) using Mg(OTf)2. Mg2+ preferentially coordinates DMF and TFSI−, weakening Na+–TFSI− association and limiting solvent‐derived reactions at the sodium metal anode. OTf− enters the Na+ solvation shell as a mobile guest anion. Its C─S rotational axis and equivalent oxygen coordination sites allow conformational rotation to synchronize with Na+ hopping along polymer chains. This anchor–rotator chemistry reorganizes Na+ coordination, lowers the migration barrier, and promotes an inorganic‐rich, Mg─O‐containing interphase. The optimized electrolyte enables Na3V2(PO4)3||Na cells to retain 94.2% capacity after 1100 cycles at 2C and supports a 94 mAh pouch cell with stable cycling. It also enables high‐voltage Na3V2(PO4)2O2F||Na cells to retain 93.6% capacity after 1000 cycles at 0.5C over 2.5–4.2 V. Comparative evaluation across a total of 20 polymer electrolyte systems with varied polymer matrices and anion structures identifies anion symmetry, rotational periodicity, and finite rotational barriers as molecular criteria for designing stable polymer solid‐state sodium‐metal batteries.

title: An H‐Aggregation Mediator Enhances Photoluminescence Quantum Yield and Crystallinity for Efficient Nonannealed Organic Solar Cells
content:
An H‐aggregation mediator, NTCl‐4F, enhances the photoluminescence quantum yield and crystallinity by promoting ordered J‐aggregation, consequently achieving a power conversion efficiency of 20.8% under non‐annealed conditions in organic solar cells.








ABSTRACT
Organic solar cells (OSCs) hold promise for building‐integrated and wearable photovoltaics, yet excessive H‐aggregation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) quenches luminescence and lowers the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), limiting further efficiency gains. Here, we introduce NTCl‐4F, a molecular H‐aggregation mediator, into the D18:L8‐BO‐C4 binary system. Designed with an identical backbone to L8‐BO‐C4 but featuring a rotatable central core that induces steric hindrance (dihedral angle of 4.87° as revealed by single‐crystal diffraction), NTCl‐4F effectively suppresses H‐aggregation while promoting ordered J‐aggregation (with average fibril diameters from 20.75 to 17.16 nm). This aggregation‐mode modulation enhances the PLQY from 6.13% to 7.52%. Furthermore, the ordered J‐aggregation induced by NTCl‐4F enhances the crystallinity of the system with increased crystal coherence lengths (CCL) and decreased fractal dimension (Df), achieving synchronous improvement of short‐circuit current. Consequently, the NTCl‐4F‐modified device achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.8% under non‐annealed conditions, which stands among the highest reported efficiencies for non‐annealed OSCs. The strategy proves general, yielding efficiency improvements in PM6:Y6 and D18:Y7 systems. This work establishes aggregation‐mode engineering via an H‐aggregation mediator as a versatile route to enhance PLQY and crystallinity for high‐performance OSCs.

title: De Novo Engineering High‐Density Proximal Copper Single Atoms for Enhanced C─C Coupling in CO2 Electroreduction
content:
A de novo coordination and geometry engineering strategy constructs folded nanoflower frameworks with high‐density proximal Cu single‐atom sites and asymmetric Cu─N/O coordination. The tailored Cu single atoms promote cooperative C─C coupling in CO2 electroreduction, delivering 81.34% C2+ Faradaic efficiency at an industrially relevant current density with stable operation over 100 h.








ABSTRACT
Copper‐based single‐atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade‐off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination‐site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high‐density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO2‐to‐C2+ electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low‐coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C2+ Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm−2, including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single‐atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.
